modes.title: Standard Calibration
modes.blurb: The full calibration: empty-scale zero plus one known test weight. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 1280 has five ways to do it — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: If this indicator is sealed, the touchscreen will not open the Configuration menu. Getting in means breaking the wire seal and removing the large fillister screw, then pressing the setup switch inside the indicator with a non-conductive tool. Press lightly — the manual warns that pressing hard can damage the switch or the board.
1. On the weigh mode screen, open the Main Menu.
2. Open the Configuration menu. If it asks for a password, enter the password.
3. If the Configuration menu does not appear, the indicator is sealed: break the wire seal, remove the large fillister screw, and press the setup switch inside with a non-conductive tool — lightly. Enter the password if it asks.
4. From the Configuration menu, open the Scales menu. Select the scale you are calibrating — 1 to 8 — then open Calibration.
5. Press Calibrate Scale. The step-by-step calibration starts.
6. Select Standard Calibration as the method, then press Next.
7. Tell it whether chains, hooks or other rigging are used to apply the weights, then press Next.
8. Remove all weight from the scale — except the chains and hooks, if you said you use them.
9. Press Calibrate Zero. The current weight shows, then Zero Calibration Complete.
10. Press Next.
11. Enter the Span weight — the true value of the test weights you are about to use. The screen starts at 10,000; change it to your real test weight. This must be in before the span can run.
12. Place the test weight on the scale.
13. Press Calibrate Span. The current span weight shows.
14. Press Next. The calibration results show.
15. Press Finish. You are back at the Calibration menu.
16. If chains or hooks were used, take them and the test weights off the scale, then press Re-Zero. That removes the offset the rigging put into the calibration.
17. If the reading sits a division off, Up and Down nudge the calibrated weight one display division at a time; Expanded Resolution nudges by a tenth of a division.
18. Leave the Calibration menu back to the Configuration menu, then press Save and Exit to return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If you broke the wire seal to get in, put the large fillister screw back and have the indicator resealed — the setup switch is sealed with a lead wire seal, with jumper JP1 in the off (right) position.
References: Rice Lake 1280 Technical Manual Doc 167659 — Access Setup Parameters (printed p. 50), Scale Calibration (printed p. 58), Standard Calibration (printed pp. 58-59). [PDF pp. 58, 66-67]

modes.title: Multi-Point Calibration
modes.blurb: Standard calibration plus up to four extra points between zero and span, for a straighter line across the whole range.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 1280 has five ways to do it — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: If this indicator is sealed, the touchscreen will not open the Configuration menu. Getting in means breaking the wire seal and removing the large fillister screw, then pressing the setup switch inside the indicator with a non-conductive tool. Press lightly — the manual warns that pressing hard can damage the switch or the board.
1. On the weigh mode screen, open the Main Menu.
2. Open the Configuration menu. If it asks for a password, enter the password.
3. If the Configuration menu does not appear, the indicator is sealed: break the wire seal, remove the large fillister screw, and press the setup switch inside with a non-conductive tool — lightly. Enter the password if it asks.
4. From the Configuration menu, open the Scales menu. Select the scale you are calibrating — 1 to 8 — then open Calibration.
5. First complete a standard zero and span calibration — the book requires both before any linear point can be added.
6. Know this before you start: if linear points were entered before, doing the initial zero calibration resets those values to zero.
7. Place a test weight that falls between the zero point and the span point on the scale.
8. Enter that weight's true value as the Linear Point Weight.
9. Press Calibrate for that point. Calibration Complete shows when the point is captured.

modes.title: Last Zero Calibration
modes.blurb: Truck scales: turn a verification with the weights already on into a calibration, without pulling the test weights off.
modes.text:

modes.title: Temporary Zero Calibration
modes.blurb: Hopper scales: zero the load sitting in the hopper, calibrate the span, and keep the original zero.
modes.text:

modes.title: Theoretical Calibration
modes.blurb: No test weights hung: zero the empty scale, then set the span from the load cells' own numbers — total build and average mV/V.
modes.text:

modes.title: Standard Calibration (Zero and Span)
modes.blurb: The everyday calibration. Empty scale for zero, one known test load for span. First-time and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 720i calibrates from its front panel — zero, a known test weight for span, and, when the job calls for it, up to five extra points in between. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode — the display reads Scale Configuration.
2. From the SCALES menu, press Down, select the scale to be calibrated, press Down again (GRADS is highlighted), then press Left to highlight the CALIBR submenu.
3. Press Down to go to zero calibration, WZERO.
4. Know your softkeys on the calibration screens: Calibrate performs the calibration for the point on screen; Last Zero recalls the last established zero; Millivolts (or Counts) switches the display between A/D counts and millivolts; plus-minus toggles positive and negative entry.
5. Make sure the scale is empty. If the test weights will hang from hooks or chains, put the hooks or chains on the scale now, empty.
6. At WZERO, press Down to show the current zero value, then press the Calibrate softkey. The new A/D count shows when it finishes. Press Enter to save the zero and move to WVAL.
7. At WVAL, press Down to show the stored test weight value. Enter the true value of your test weights with the arrow keys or the keypad, then press Enter to save and move to WSPAN. Book tip: if the keypad will not change the value, set the first digit with the up/down arrows, then key in the rest — for 25000, arrow the first digit to 2, then key 5000.
8. Put the test weights on the scale. Press Down to show the current WSPAN value, then press the Calibrate softkey. Press Enter to save the span. The display moves on to WLIN — linearization is optional from here.
9. Press Up to return to the SCALES menu, or press the Save and Exit softkey to leave setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 720i Technical Manual Doc 103121 — Calibration overview (§5.0, p. 60), Front Panel Calibration (§5.2, p. 61).

modes.title: Five-Point Linearization (WLIN)
modes.blurb: Added accuracy across the range. After a standard calibration, the scale is also taught at up to five points between zero and span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 720i calibrates from its front panel — zero, a known test weight for span, and, when the job calls for it, up to five extra points in between. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode — the display reads Scale Configuration.
2. From the SCALES menu, press Down, select the scale to be calibrated, press Down again (GRADS is highlighted), then press Left to highlight the CALIBR submenu.
3. Press Down to go to zero calibration, WZERO.
4. Know your softkeys on the calibration screens: Calibrate performs the calibration for the point on screen; Last Zero recalls the last established zero; Millivolts (or Counts) switches the display between A/D counts and millivolts; plus-minus toggles positive and negative entry.
5. Finish the Standard Calibration first — linearization begins at the WLIN prompt, right after span is saved. To skip linearization entirely, just press Up back to the CALIBR submenu.
6. Know this: if linearization values were entered before, they are reset to zero during calibration — re-teaching is part of the job.
7. At WLIN, press Down to POINT 1. Press Down again to the weight prompt (WGT 1), then Down once more to show the weight value.
8. Put the first test load on the scale. Key in its true value and press Enter to save and move to the CAL 1 prompt.
9. Press Down to show the current calibration value, then press the Calibrate softkey. Press Enter to save the point and move to the next point, POINT 2.
10. Repeat for as many points as the job needs, up to five. Press Up to return to WLIN when done.
11. Press Up to return to the SCALES menu, or press the Save and Exit softkey to leave setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 720i Technical Manual Doc 103121 — Front Panel Calibration (§5.2, p. 61).

modes.title: Rezero for Hooks or Chains
modes.blurb: The test weights hung from hooks or chains during calibration. Rezero removes that rigging offset afterward. CAUTION from the book: rezero cannot be used with five-point linear calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 720i calibrates from its front panel — zero, a known test weight for span, and, when the job calls for it, up to five extra points in between. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode — the display reads Scale Configuration.
2. From the SCALES menu, press Down, select the scale to be calibrated, press Down again (GRADS is highlighted), then press Left to highlight the CALIBR submenu.
3. Press Down to go to zero calibration, WZERO.
4. Know your softkeys on the calibration screens: Calibrate performs the calibration for the point on screen; Last Zero recalls the last established zero; Millivolts (or Counts) switches the display between A/D counts and millivolts; plus-minus toggles positive and negative entry.
5. If no hooks or chains were used, there is nothing to rezero: take the test weights off and press Up to return to the CALIBR submenu.
6. If hooks or chains hung the weights, take everything off the scale — weights and rigging — until the scale is completely empty.
7. Go to the REZERO parameter. Press Down to show the current zero value, then press the Calibrate softkey. This adjusts both the zero and span calibration values.
8. Press Enter or Up to return to the CALIBR submenu.
9. Press Up to return to the SCALES menu, or press the Save and Exit softkey to leave setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 720i Technical Manual Doc 103121 — Front Panel Calibration (§5.2, p. 61).

modes.title: Gravity Compensation (set before you calibrate)
modes.blurb: The indicator was calibrated in one place and will work in another. Set latitude and elevation first; the book credits the difference into the calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 720i calibrates from its front panel — zero, a known test weight for span, and, when the job calls for it, up to five extra points in between. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode — the display reads Scale Configuration.
2. From the SCALES menu, press Down, select the scale to be calibrated, press Down again (GRADS is highlighted), then press Left to highlight the CALIBR submenu.
3. Press Down to go to zero calibration, WZERO.
4. Know your softkeys on the calibration screens: Calibrate performs the calibration for the point on screen; Last Zero recalls the last established zero; Millivolts (or Counts) switches the display between A/D counts and millivolts; plus-minus toggles positive and negative entry.
5. In the FEATURE menu, set the LOCALE parameter ON.
6. Set LATUDE, the latitude, and ELEVAT, the elevation in meters, for where the scale will work.
7. Do this before calibrating. Then run the Standard Calibration.
8. Worth knowing: if the indicator is later moved, you can apply gravity compensation to the already-calibrated indicator just by adjusting LATUDE and ELEVAT — no new test weights required by this section.
9. Press Up to return to the SCALES menu, or press the Save and Exit softkey to leave setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 720i Technical Manual Doc 103121 — Gravity Compensation (§5.1, p. 60).

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The standard calibration — empty scale for zero, one test load for span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 482 works from its front panel — pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Press the setup switch only with a non-conductive tool, reached in through the access hole in the back of the enclosure — that is this book's own instruction.
1. Remove the setup switch access screw from the back of the enclosure.
2. Insert a non-conductive tool into the access hole and press the configuration switch. The display changes to CONFIG.
3. Press the right key until CALIBR is displayed.
4. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights need hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, for the zero.
5. Move to WZERO, then CAL, then ENTER to capture the zero. The display shows *CAL* while it works; when it finishes, the milli-volt value for zero is displayed.
6. Save the zero value and go back to CAL, then move to WVAL.
7. Show the test weight value, edit it to the true value of the test weights you will use, and store it.
8. Move to WSPAN, then CAL, then ENTER. Place the test weights on the scale and capture the span. The display shows *CAL* while it works; the net milli-volt value of the test weight is displayed — that is the raw mV at span minus the mV captured at zero.
9. Save the value and go back to CAL, then return to the CALIBR menu.
10. Remove all weight from the scale, back out until the display reads CONFIG, then exit configuration mode. Put the setup switch access screw back in the rear panel. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 482 Legend Series Technical Manual Doc 165124 — Front Panel Calibration (§4.1, pp. 52-53).

modes.title: Zero and Span with Hooks or Chains (Rezero)
modes.blurb: Test weights hang from hooks or chains. Calibrate normally, then REZERO takes the hooks' weight back out so zero tells the truth.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 482 works from its front panel — pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Press the setup switch only with a non-conductive tool, reached in through the access hole in the back of the enclosure — that is this book's own instruction.
1. Remove the setup switch access screw from the back of the enclosure.
2. Insert a non-conductive tool into the access hole and press the configuration switch. The display changes to CONFIG.
3. Press the right key until CALIBR is displayed.
4. First run the Front Panel Zero and Span above, with the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero, exactly as the book lays out.
5. At WSPAN, move to REZERO.
6. Remove the hooks or chains and take all test weights off the scale.
7. ZERO displays briefly, then *CAL* shows while the zero and span values are adjusted with all weight removed.
8. Return to the CALIBR menu.
9. Remove all weight from the scale, back out until the display reads CONFIG, then exit configuration mode. Put the setup switch access screw back in the rear panel. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 482 Legend Series Technical Manual Doc 165124 — Front Panel Calibration, REZERO steps 21-22 (§4.1, pp. 52-53).

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: No button-pushing: the indicator takes SC commands over COM 1 from a terminal or computer.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 482 works from its front panel — pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Press the setup switch only with a non-conductive tool, reached in through the access hole in the back of the enclosure — that is this book's own instruction.
1. Remove the setup switch access screw from the back of the enclosure.
2. Insert a non-conductive tool into the access hole and press the configuration switch. The display changes to CONFIG.
3. Press the right key until CALIBR is displayed.
4. Connect COM 1 to a terminal or computer. The commands below are the CALIBR EDP commands from Section 6.0.
5. Remove all weight from the platform. If the test weights need hooks or chains, place them on the scale for the zero.
6. Send SC.WZERO to calibrate zero. The display shows *CAL* while it works.
7. Place the test weights on the scale and send the test weight value with SC.WVAL, in the form WVAL=nnnnnn and Enter.
8. Send SC.WSPAN to calibrate span. The display shows *CAL* while it works.
9. To remove an offset: clear all weight from the scale, including anything used to hang the test weights, then send SC.REZERO. The display shows *CAL* while the zero and span values are adjusted.
10. Send KUPARROW to exit configuration mode.
11. Remove all weight from the scale, back out until the display reads CONFIG, then exit configuration mode. Put the setup switch access screw back in the rear panel. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 482 Legend Series Technical Manual Doc 165124 — EDP Command Calibration (§4.2, p. 53), CALIBR EDP Commands (Table 6-5, p. 59).

modes.title: Fine-Tune the Span
modes.blurb: The scale proves a hair high or low in a strain test. Nudge WVAL and the book's own math corrects it — about 1 lb per 1000 lb in the book's example.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 482 works from its front panel — pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Press the setup switch only with a non-conductive tool, reached in through the access hole in the back of the enclosure — that is this book's own instruction.
1. Remove the setup switch access screw from the back of the enclosure.
2. Insert a non-conductive tool into the access hole and press the configuration switch. The display changes to CONFIG.
3. Press the right key until CALIBR is displayed.
4. Get back to the WVAL prompt and show the test weight value.
5. Adjust the value up or down to move the calibration. The book's example: a scale reading 2 lb high at 2000 lb is corrected by changing WVAL to 999, a linear correction of 1 lb per 1000 lb.
6. Save the value and return to the CALIBR menu.
7. Remove all weight from the scale, back out until the display reads CONFIG, then exit configuration mode. Put the setup switch access screw back in the rear panel. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 482 Legend Series Technical Manual Doc 165124 — Adjust Final Calibration (§4.4.1, p. 54).

modes.title: Zero and Span (Full Calibration)
modes.blurb: First-time calibration and complete recalibration. The book runs zero and span as two softkey captures, one after the other.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IND780 does it from one place — the Calibration setup screen — and its softkeys run the job. Pick the route that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: The metrology switch, S1, inside the terminal guards these settings. If that switch is in the ON, approved position, the Scale branch of setup cannot be changed at all. In legal-for-trade work that switch may be sealed inside the enclosure — if yours is sealed, treat this as sealed work, not a screwdriver job.
1. From the home screen, press the SETUP softkey.
2. If a login screen shows, enter the administrator username and password and press the OK softkey. If no passwords are set, the terminal goes straight into setup.
3. In the setup menu tree, use the UP and DOWN keys to focus the Scale branch, then press the RIGHT key to expand it.
4. Open the Calibration setup screen for the scale you are calibrating.
5. On the Calibration screen, press the CAPTURE ZERO softkey.
6. Empty the scale completely.
7. When the status message tells you to, press the START softkey.
8. If motion is detected, press OK to accept the captured value, or ESC to reject it and return to the calibration screen.
9. When the message confirms the zero capture, press the EXIT softkey to return to the Calibration screen.
10. Press the CAPTURE SPAN softkey.
11. Enter the test load weight and press ENTER. If linearity points are switched on, enter every test load's weight too.
12. Put the first test load on the scale.
13. Press the START softkey and let it capture.
14. If more loads are switched on, put the next load on when prompted, press START, and repeat for each load, up to four.
15. If motion is detected, decide: accept the captured value, or abort and return to the calibration screen.
16. Capture Span OK means the full calibration took. Calibration Failure means repeat it — and if it keeps failing, call METTLER TOLEDO. Press the EXIT softkey to return to the Calibration screen.
17. Press the EXIT softkey to return to the Calibration screen; in the setup menu tree, select Home and press ENTER — or press the first, leftmost softkey — to get back to the home screen. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If you moved the metrology switch, put S1 back in the ON, approved position and reseal the enclosure before this scale returns to legal trade.
References: METTLER TOLEDO IND780 Technical Manual Doc 64057242 — Capture Zero and Capture Span (§3.5.1.4.8, printed pp. 3-31 to 3-33) [PDF pp. 106-108].

modes.title: Capture Zero Only
modes.blurb: Zero drifted, or the dead load changed — a guard rail bolted on, say. Teaches a fresh zero and leaves the span alone.

modes.title: Capture Span Only (keeps the stored zero)
modes.blurb: Span work on big scales. Teaches a new span and leaves the zero you already have. Set the Linearity Adjust method first if you want more than one span point.

CAUTION: The metrology switch, S1, inside the terminal guards these settings. If that switch is in the ON, approved position, the Scale branch of setup cannot be changed at all. 1. From the home screen, press the SETUP softkey.
2. If a login screen shows, enter the administrator username and password and press the OK softkey. If no passwords are set, the terminal goes straight into setup.
3. In the setup menu tree, use the UP and DOWN keys to focus the Scale branch, then press the RIGHT key to expand it.
4. Open the Calibration setup screen for the scale you are calibrating.
5. On the Calibration screen, press the CAPTURE SPAN softkey.
6. Enter the test load weight and press ENTER. If linearity points are switched on, enter every test load's weight too. Whatever value sits in the field is the one START uses, whether you pressed ENTER or not.
7. Do not go too small: the terminal needs at least 1 percent of the counts a full-span load would produce — on a 25,000 kg scale that is about a 250 kg test load.
8. Put the first test load on the scale.
9. Press the START softkey and let it capture; the screen shows the capture running.
10. If more loads are switched on, put the next load on when prompted, press START, and repeat for each load, up to four.
11. If motion is detected, decide: accept the captured value, or abort and return to the calibration screen.
12. Capture Span OK means it took. Calibration Failure means run it again — and if it keeps failing, call METTLER TOLEDO. Press the EXIT softkey to return to the Calibration screen.
13. Press the EXIT softkey to return to the Calibration screen; in the setup menu tree, select Home and press ENTER — or press the first, leftmost softkey — to get back to the home screen. If you moved the metrology switch, put S1 back in the ON, approved position and reseal the enclosure before this scale returns to legal trade.

modes.blurb: Vessels you cannot load to capacity with test weights. The same test weight is added at every step, with substitute material filled in between, building the span up in steps.

7. Press the START softkey. The screen shows a live weight, the target, and the prompt Place Test Load.

9. Press the START softkey. The load is captured, the span factor is saved, Capture Span OK shows, and the prompt changes to Remove Test Load — Fill to Target.

modes.title: Capture Zero
modes.blurb: Teach the empty scale its zero. First half of every full calibration — and the zero half must still be done even after CalFree.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IND570 has four ways to do it on an analog scale — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: If the scale is approved (sealed) and the metrology switch SW1-1 is ON, the Scale branch is locked — view only, no changes. And if an approval is selected but the switch is NOT ON, the terminal will not let you leave setup — it shows Switch UNSECURED. The manual says: after setting the terminal to approved, and before exiting setup, switch SW1-1 to ON while the terminal is powered up, and take care when setting the switch in the powered terminal.
1. Open the setup menu and go into the Scale branch, then to the Calibration screens.
2. Before you capture anything, set the Geo Code for this location, the Calibration Units, and the Linearity Adjustment method — the method decides how many test loads the span capture will ask for. Disabled means zero plus one span point; 3, 4 or 5 point methods ask for each load in turn, and the hysteresis variants also guide the loads back down.
3. Check the Analog Gain Jumper setting matches the physical jumper on the Main PCB — 2 mV/V has the jumper on both pins, 3 mV/V on one pin (the factory default). If this setting is wrong, the CalFree calculation will not be accurate.
4. Press the Capture Zero softkey to enter the Capture Zero page.
5. As prompted on screen, empty the scale, then press Start.
6. Watch the status on screen. The Escape softkey stops the zero process.
7. When it finishes, the screen shows Capture Zero OK. Press the Back/Exit softkey to return to the Calibration page.
8. If Zero Failure shows instead, repeat the same steps. If the process fails again, contact a local METTLER TOLEDO representative for assistance.
9. Back out of the Calibration screens to the setup menu tree. If this scale is approved, SW1-1 must be ON before you leave setup, or the terminal stops you with Switch UNSECURED — set it ON while powered, carefully. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If it does not, do not hand it back — run the capture again.
References: Mettler Toledo IND570 User's Guide 30205308 — Capture Zero (§3.5.1.3.6) [PDF p. 109].

modes.title: Capture Span (with Linearity)
modes.blurb: Span with test weights; runs independently of zero. With the linearity method you picked, it walks each test load in turn — points going up, hysteresis methods also guide the loads back down.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IND570 has four ways to do it on an analog scale — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: If the scale is approved (sealed) and the metrology switch SW1-1 is ON, the Scale branch is locked — view only, no changes. And if an approval is selected but the switch is NOT ON, the terminal will not let you leave setup — it shows Switch UNSECURED. The manual says: after setting the terminal to approved, and before exiting setup, switch SW1-1 to ON while the terminal is powered up, and take care when setting the switch in the powered terminal.
1. Open the setup menu and go into the Scale branch, then to the Calibration screens.
2. Before you capture anything, set the Geo Code for this location, the Calibration Units, and the Linearity Adjustment method — the method decides how many test loads the span capture will ask for. Disabled means zero plus one span point; 3, 4 or 5 point methods ask for each load in turn, and the hysteresis variants also guide the loads back down.
3. Check the Analog Gain Jumper setting matches the physical jumper on the Main PCB — 2 mV/V has the jumper on both pins, 3 mV/V on one pin (the factory default). If this setting is wrong, the CalFree calculation will not be accurate.
4. Make sure the Linearity Adjustment method you want is set first — it decides which test loads you will be prompted for, and every new test load value must be larger than the previous one.
5. Press the Capture Span softkey.
6. If a test load value needs changing, type the new value in the entry box and press ENTER to confirm; keep pressing ENTER until all test load values are confirmed. If no change is needed, press the Down arrow and the Capture Span page shows.
7. As prompted, place the test load shown on screen. Ensure the scale is always loaded to the test load value by adding weights. Caution from the book: if the scale is loaded beyond the test load value, do not remove weight to reach the displayed value — the process must be restarted from the beginning.
8. Press Start to begin the capture and watch the status on screen.
9. When it completes, Capture Span OK shows. Press Back/Exit to return.
10. If Calibration Failure appears, repeat the steps. If the process fails again, contact a local METTLER TOLEDO representative for assistance.
11. For the other test load values, repeat: place the next load, Start, and confirm each prompt in turn.
12. Hysteresis methods only: after the top point, unload to the prompted points, always by removing weights. If the scale is unloaded below a test load value, do not add weight back — the process must be restarted from the beginning.
13. If an analog saturation warning shows after a successful capture, press ENTER to acknowledge, then check the analog gain jumper matches the real load cell output — the book warns saturation can freeze the display and risk overfills and spills.
14. Back out of the Calibration screens to the setup menu tree. If this scale is approved, SW1-1 must be ON before you leave setup, or the terminal stops you with Switch UNSECURED — set it ON while powered, carefully. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If it does not, do not hand it back — run the capture again.

modes.title: Step Calibration (build-up)
modes.blurb: For tanks and hoppers — the same amount of test weight is added at each step, with substitute material filling in between.
modes.text:

1. Open the setup menu and go into the Scale branch, then to the Calibration screens.
2. Before you capture anything, set the Geo Code for this location, the Calibration Units, and the Linearity Adjustment method — the method decides how many test loads the span capture will ask for. 4. Press the STEP CALIBRATION softkey. The Step Calibration setup screen shows.
5. Enter the target weight for the test load — this same amount is used in every step.
6. Press START. The screen shows a live weight display, the target you entered, and the prompt Add test weight.
7. Add test weight to the tank or hopper as prompted. Each time weight is added, the live display shows it.
8. When the full amount of test weight has been added, press OK. The test load is captured and span factors are saved; the display changes to Capturing span, then to Remove test weight then fill to target.
9. Remove the test weight. The live display returns to zero.
10. Fill the tank or hopper with substitute material up to near the target weight. It does not have to be the exact target weight.
11. Press OK. The target recalculates — substitute weight plus the original target — and the next prompt is Add test weight.
12. Add the test weight again and check the live display. Press OK. If the actual weight is not the target, a new span factor calculates, the display matches the target, and it prompts Remove test weight then fill to target.
13. Remove the test weight. The display returns to the previous test-load weight.
14. Repeat — fill, add, capture — until enough calibration steps are done for this application.
15. Press the EXIT softkey at any step to stop and return to the Calibration screen.

modes.title: CalFree (span without test weights)
modes.blurb: Span with NO test weights — calculated from the load cells' rated numbers. Zero still has to be captured the normal way afterwards.

1. Open the setup menu and go into the Scale branch, then to the Calibration screens.
2. Before you capture anything, set the Geo Code for this location, the Calibration Units, and the Linearity Adjustment method — the method decides how many test loads the span capture will ask for. modes.title: Zero Calibration with a Simulator
modes.blurb: Sets the zero point with the calibrator dialed to 0 mV/V. The first half of the book's factory calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration on the 1040 is taught with a calibrator (a simulator), not test weights: the book sets zero at 0 mV/V and span at 1 mV/V, and 1 mV/V equals 10,000 pounds. There is also a SPAN fine-tune in the Setup menu that nudges the reading up or down with a known weight on the scale. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From Gross mode, press and hold the MENU key for three beeps (3 seconds), then release. SET.PAS is displayed.
2. Use the keypad to enter 010101. Asterisks are displayed.
3. Press the SELECT key. ZERO is displayed. You are in the factory calibration menu.
4. From ZERO, press SELECT. SET.0MV is displayed.
5. Dial the calibrator to 0 mV/V and press SELECT. DET.ZER, then DONE is displayed.
6. The display returns to ZERO.
7. Press the GROSS key to return to the Gross weighing mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Avery Weigh-Tronix Model 1040/XL Indicator Service Manual Doc 29812-0015A — SPAN setup-menu adjustment (printed pp. 11-12), Production or Service Factory Calibration: Accessing Factory Calibration Mode and Setting Zero Calibration (printed p. 30), Setting the Span Calibration, Viewing Current Calibration, Viewing Factory Span Factor (printed p. 31), Re-setting Factory Span Without Calibrating with a Simulator (printed p. 32). [PDF pp. 11-12, 30-32]

modes.title: Span Calibration with a Simulator

modes.title: Span Fine-Tune with a Known Weight
modes.blurb: The field touch-up: with a calibrator or a known weight on the scale, nudge the span reading up or down (the book says this adjusts the span plus or minus 10 percent). This one lives in the Setup menu, not the calibration menu.
modes.text:
Calibration on the 1040 is taught with a calibrator (a simulator), not test weights: the book sets zero at 0 mV/V and span at 1 mV/V, and 1 mV/V equals 10,000 pounds. There is also a SPAN fine-tune in the Setup menu that nudges the reading up or down with a known weight on the scale. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From Gross mode, press and hold the MENU key for three beeps (3 seconds), then release. SET.PAS is displayed.
2. Use the keypad to enter 010101. Asterisks are displayed.
3. Press the SELECT key. ZERO is displayed. You are in the factory calibration menu.
4. From Gross mode, press and hold the MENU key for three beeps (3 seconds), then release. SET.PAS is displayed.
5. Key in 1040, then press SELECT. CONFIG is displayed.
6. Press the MENU key several times until SPAN is displayed.
7. Press SELECT. The current weight is displayed.
8. Put the calibrator or a known weight on the scale system.
9. Adjust with the keypad: press 1, 2, 4, or 5 to increase the span; 6, 7, 9, or 0 to decrease it; 3 or 8 returns to the factory calibrated value. Each press moves one division; press and hold to move faster.
10. When the right weight value shows, press SELECT. SPAN is shown.
11. Press the GROSS key to return to the Gross weighing mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Avery Weigh-Tronix Model 1040/XL Indicator Service Manual Doc 29812-0015A — SPAN setup-menu adjustment (printed pp. 11-12), Production or Service Factory Calibration: Accessing Factory Calibration Mode and Setting Zero Calibration (printed p. 30), Setting the Span Calibration, Viewing Current Calibration, Viewing Factory Span Factor (printed p. 31), Re-setting Factory Span Without Calibrating with a Simulator (printed p. 32). [PDF pp. 11-12, 30-32]

modes.title: Restore the Factory Span Value
modes.blurb: Puts the unit back to its factory calibration without running the simulator: read the stored factory span factor, then re-enter it under SET. The book says to retrieve the value first — for example before clearing memory — then enter it back here.
modes.text:
Calibration on the 1040 is taught with a calibrator (a simulator), not test weights: the book sets zero at 0 mV/V and span at 1 mV/V, and 1 mV/V equals 10,000 pounds. There is also a SPAN fine-tune in the Setup menu that nudges the reading up or down with a known weight on the scale. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From Gross mode, press and hold the MENU key for three beeps (3 seconds), then release. SET.PAS is displayed.
2. Use the keypad to enter 010101. Asterisks are displayed.
3. Press the SELECT key. ZERO is displayed. You are in the factory calibration menu.
4. To read the stored value first: from ZERO, press MENU repeatedly until VIEW is displayed.
5. Press SELECT. The current span factor is displayed — 1 mV/V equals 100000 if the electronics are all exact; a little off, like 99990, is normal. Write the number down.
6. Press SELECT. VIEW is displayed.
7. Now, from ZERO, press MENU repeatedly until SET is displayed.
8. Press SELECT. FAC.SPN is displayed.
9. Enter the factory span value. The entered value is displayed.
10. Press SELECT. SET is displayed.
11. Press the GROSS key to return to the Gross weighing mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Zero Reference
modes.blurb: Set the zero reference point by itself — the empty-scale end of the calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 1080 has four ways to do it from the CAL submenu — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time. The book says the indicator must be unsealed to change anything in the Service menu: a jumper must be placed over the pins of P2 inside the indicator, and you remove the jumper to seal the indicator. This hub covers analog scales; the book covers SensorComm scales in a separate chapter.
1. Press and hold the ZERO key for 3 to 5 seconds. PASS_ is displayed. You must begin to scroll in the password within 10 seconds or the display returns to normal operation mode.
2. Key in the Service menu password, 0801, using the numeric entry procedure, then press F1. The first item in the menu is displayed, and the annunciators at the top of the display flash as a reminder while you are in a menu.
3. If you are changing anything in the Service menu, the indicator must be unsealed: remove the screws on the sides and top of the indicator to access the PC boards, and place a jumper over the pins of P2.
4. With CAL displayed, you are at the top of the CAL submenu for analog scales.
5. Press the PRINT key. ZEro is displayed. This item sets the zero reference for the indicator and scale.
6. Remove all weight from the scale and press the F1 key. Live weight is shown.
7. Press the F1 key to perform the zero procedure. buSY is briefly displayed, then the live weight, which should be 0.
8. Press the F1 key to save and return to the ZEro menu item.
9. Press the ZERO key to return to normal operating mode. When SAvE is displayed, press F1 to save the changes, or press ZERO to exit without saving. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If you unsealed the indicator to get in, remove the jumper from P2 to seal the indicator again.
References: Avery Weigh-Tronix 1080 Service Manual Doc AWT35-500446 — Accessing the Menus (printed p. 18), CAL Submenu for Analog Scales (printed pp. 23-26). [PDF pp. 18, 23-26]

modes.blurb: The full span setting with a known test weight, after the zero reference is set.
modes.text:

modes.title: Linearization
modes.blurb: Extra calibration points between zero and span, lightest to heaviest, for a straighter line across the range.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 1080 has four ways to do it from the CAL submenu — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time. The book says the indicator must be unsealed to change anything in the Service menu: a jumper must be placed over the pins of P2 inside the indicator, and you remove the jumper to seal the indicator. 1. Press and hold the ZERO key for 3 to 5 seconds. PASS_ is displayed. You must begin to scroll in the password within 10 seconds or the display returns to normal operation mode.

4. With CAL displayed, you are at the top of the CAL submenu for analog scales.
5. From SPAn, press the UNITS key. LinEAr is displayed. This item sets extra calibration points.
6. Press the PRINT key. 2 is displayed. This represents cal point 2.
7. Press the F1 key to set this calibration point. A numeric value is displayed.

11. Repeat for cal point 3 and cal point 4. When you are done, 4 is displayed.
12. Press the SELECT key to return to the LinEAr menu item.

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The full calibration at the indicator itself: empty-scale zero, the test weight value, then span. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers: an empty scale that truly reads zero, and a known test weight that reads exactly its true value. The 120 Plus calibrates from the front panel or by EDP commands sent from a terminal or PC — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: The book says this about the setup switch: this operation should be performed only by a qualified technician; calibration of the indicator may be disqualified if performed by anyone else. The indicator should always be sealed after initial configuration — sealing materials can be non-reversible lead seals or stickers.
1. Press the recessed setup switch on the back of the indicator with a small non-conductive object. The display reads CONFIG.
2. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
3. Press the 6 key until the display reads CALIBR, then press the 8 key to navigate to zero calibration — the display reads WZERO.
4. With WZERO displayed, press the Enter key to calibrate zero. The indicator displays CAL while calibration is in progress. When complete, WVAL is displayed.
5. With WVAL displayed, place the test weights on the scale and press the 8 key to show the test weight value.
6. Press the Enter key to edit the value — the last digit of the displayed value blinks. Press the Clear key to clear the value, then use the numeric keys 0-9 to enter the test weight value.
7. Press the Enter key to save the test weight value and go to span calibration — the display reads WSPAN.
8. With WSPAN displayed, press the Enter key to calibrate span. The indicator displays CAL while calibration is in progress. When complete, REZERO is displayed.
9. Press the two key until the display reads EXIT Y, then press the Enter key to exit configuration mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. Seal the indicator afterward — the book says it should always be sealed after initial configuration, with non-reversible lead seals or stickers.
References: Rice Lake 120 Plus Technical Manual PN 105914 Rev C — Setup Switch (§1.8), Calibration Menu and Front Panel Calibration (§3.3, printed pp. 25-26), EDP Command Calibration (§3.3.3). [PDF pp. 11, 25-26]

modes.title: Rezero for Hooks or Chains
modes.blurb: Test weights hung from hooks or chains: after zero and span are set, this takes the rigging's offset back out of the calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers: an empty scale that truly reads zero, and a known test weight that reads exactly its true value. The 120 Plus calibrates from the front panel or by EDP commands sent from a terminal or PC — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: The book says this about the setup switch: this operation should be performed only by a qualified technician; calibration of the indicator may be disqualified if performed by anyone else. The indicator should always be sealed after initial configuration — sealing materials can be non-reversible lead seals or stickers.
1. Press the recessed setup switch on the back of the indicator with a small non-conductive object. The display reads CONFIG.
2. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
3. Use this only after WZERO and WSPAN have been set — the book is plain that rezero comes after zero and span.
4. If hooks or chains were used during calibration, remove them and all the test weights from the scale.
5. With REZERO displayed, press the Enter key to rezero the scale. This function adjusts the zero and span calibration values. When complete, LATITD is displayed.
6. Press the two key until the display reads EXIT Y, then press the Enter key to exit configuration mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. Seal the indicator afterward — the book says it should always be sealed after initial configuration, with non-reversible lead seals or stickers.

modes.title: Gravity Values — Latitude and Elevation
modes.blurb: The calibration menu carries the latitude and elevation of the place of calibration, alongside zero and span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers: an empty scale that truly reads zero, and a known test weight that reads exactly its true value. The 120 Plus calibrates from the front panel or by EDP commands sent from a terminal or PC — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: The book says this about the setup switch: this operation should be performed only by a qualified technician; calibration of the indicator may be disqualified if performed by anyone else. 1. Press the recessed setup switch on the back of the indicator with a small non-conductive object. The display reads CONFIG.
2. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
3. In the Calibration menu, move to LATITD and enter the latitude, in degrees, of the place of calibration — the book allows 0 to 90.
4. Move to ELEVTN and enter the elevation, in meters, of the place of calibration — the book allows minus 9999 to 9999.
5. To edit a value the book's way: press the Enter key to allow numeric entry, press the Clear key to clear the value, key in the value with the numeric keys 0-9, then press the Enter key to save the value and return to the level above.
6. Press the two key until the display reads EXIT Y, then press the Enter key to exit configuration mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. Seal the indicator afterward — the book says it should always be sealed after initial configuration, with non-reversible lead seals or stickers.

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: The same calibration driven from a terminal or PC over the EDP port: WZERO, WVAL, WSPAN commands instead of key presses.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers: an empty scale that truly reads zero, and a known test weight that reads exactly its true value. The 120 Plus calibrates from the front panel or by EDP commands sent from a terminal or PC — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: The book says this about the setup switch: this operation should be performed only by a qualified technician; calibration of the indicator may be disqualified if performed by anyone else. The indicator should always be sealed after initial configuration — sealing materials can be non-reversible lead seals or stickers.
1. Press the recessed setup switch on the back of the indicator with a small non-conductive object. The display reads CONFIG.
2. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
3. Connect the indicator's EDP port to a terminal or personal computer. The book points to Section 2.2 for the EDP port pin assignments.
4. Place the indicator in configuration mode — the display reads CONFIG — with all weight off the scale, and any hooks or chains on the scale if the test weights need them.
5. Send the WZERO command to calibrate zero. The indicator displays *CAL* while calibration is in progress. During EDP command calibration the *CAL* message remains on the display, and an OKAY message is sent to the terminal or computer when calibration is complete.
6. Place the test weights on the scale and send the test weight value in this format: WVAL=nnnnnn, then a carriage return.
7. Send the WSPAN command to calibrate span. The indicator displays *CAL* while calibration is in progress.
8. To remove an offset value, clear all weight from the scale — including hooks or chains used to hang the test weights — then send the REZERO command. The indicator displays *CAL* while the zero and span calibrations are adjusted.
9. Press the two key until the display reads EXIT Y, then press the Enter key to exit configuration mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. Seal the indicator afterward — the book says it should always be sealed after initial configuration, with non-reversible lead seals or stickers.
References: Rice Lake 120 Plus Technical Manual PN 105914 Rev C — Setup Switch (§1.8), Calibration Menu and Front Panel Calibration (§3.3, printed pp. 25-26), EDP Command Calibration (§3.3.3). [PDF pp. 11, 25-26]

modes.title: Front Panel Calibration
modes.blurb: Use the indicator keys at the scale: set zero empty, enter the test weight, then set span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 120 can be calibrated from the front panel, or with EDP commands sent to its EDP port. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Remove the left fillister-head screw on the underside of the enclosure and remove the rectangular switch cover plate.
2. Insert a screwdriver into the access hole and press the setup switch. The display shows CONFIG.
3. To move through setup menus, scroll left or right on the same level, move up or down between levels, and use the TARE key as Enter to select parameter values, as described for front panel configuration.
4. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
5. Move until the display reads CALIBR, then move down to zero calibration, WZERO.
6. With WZERO displayed, press the key the book shows here to calibrate zero. The indicator displays *CAL* while calibration is in progress, then the display goes to WVAL.
7. With WVAL displayed, place the test weights on the scale and press the key the book shows here to show the test weight value.
8. Enter the actual test weight, then press the key the book shows here to save the value and go to span calibration, WSPAN.
9. With WSPAN displayed, press the key the book shows here to calibrate span. The indicator displays *CAL* while calibration is in progress, then the display goes to REZERO.
10. If no apparatus was used to hang the test weights, remove the test weights and finish. If hooks or chains were used, remove them and the test weights; with all weight removed, press the key the book shows here to rezero. The indicator displays *CAL* while the zero and span calibrations are adjusted.
11. Press the key the book shows here until the display reads EXIT Y, then press the key the book shows here to leave configuration mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. Replace the setup switch access screw.
References: Rice Lake 120 Extended Digital Weight Indicator Technical Manual PN 76699 Rev D — Configuration (Section 3.0, printed p. 15), Front Panel Configuration (Section 3.1.3, printed p. 16), Calibration Menu (Section 3.2.3, printed p. 21), Calibration (Section 4.0, printed p. 27), Front Panel Calibration (Section 4.1, printed p. 27), EDP Command Calibration (Section 4.2, printed p. 27), CALIBR EDP Commands (Table 5-5, printed p. 30). [PDF pp. 15-16, 21, 27, 30]

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: Use a terminal or personal computer connected to the EDP port and send the book's calibration commands.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 120 can be calibrated from the front panel, or with EDP commands sent to its EDP port. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Remove the left fillister-head screw on the underside of the enclosure and remove the rectangular switch cover plate.
2. Insert a screwdriver into the access hole and press the setup switch. The display shows CONFIG.
3. To move through setup menus, scroll left or right on the same level, move up or down between levels, and use the TARE key as Enter to select parameter values, as described for front panel configuration.
4. Connect the indicator EDP port to a terminal or personal computer.
5. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
6. Send WZERO to calibrate zero. The indicator displays *CAL* while calibration is in progress; during EDP calibration the *CAL* message remains on the display, and OK is returned when calibration is complete.
7. Place test weights on the scale and enter the test weight value with WVAL=nnnnnn, followed by a carriage return.
8. Send WSPAN to calibrate span. The indicator displays *CAL* while calibration is in progress.
9. To remove an offset, clear all weight from the scale, including hooks or chains used to hang test weights, then send REZERO. The indicator displays *CAL* while the zero and span calibrations are adjusted.
10. Send KUPARROW to exit configuration mode.
11. Press the key the book shows here until the display reads EXIT Y, then press the key the book shows here to leave configuration mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. Replace the setup switch access screw.

modes.title: Two-Point Calibration
modes.blurb: The book's main calibration: two points, in either order — zero with no load and the test weights. Use it when the indicator is first connected to a scale or when recalibration is necessary.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The Model 185 and 185B calibrate from the keypad in two ways: a two-point calibration using zero/no load and a test load, and a fine span adjustment under a test load of at least 10% of capacity. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Do not operate the membrane keypad with pointed objects such as pencils, pens, or fingernails; the book says damage from this practice is not covered under warranty. If your metrology laws require physical sealing, the book's lead and wire security seal prevents the calibration jumper from being removed and re-installed to enter setup and calibration, and the locking screws cannot be removed without damaging that seal.
1. With the indicator ON, loosen the four Phillips screws securing the rear housing to the front housing and remove the rear housing to reach calibration jumper J3.
2. Remove the calibration jumper J3. The first setup prompt is displayed.
3. Re-install the calibration jumper and press the TARE key. The Remote Display prompt is displayed.
4. At Remote Display, press the TARE key to view the current setting; press the TARE key again to keep it, or use the Fn key to change it and the TARE key to select it. If Remote Display is enabled, the Remote Serial Data Type prompt appears next.
5. Continue through the setup prompts before Calibration, keeping each current setting unless the job requires a change: Domestic or International, Legal For Trade, Weighing Unit 1, Interval Setting, Decimal Point Position, Capacity, and Weighing Unit 2. Stop at the Calibration prompt. For entries, the UNITS key moves the blinking cursor left, the Fn key changes the blinking character, and the TARE key retains the value and advances.
6. At the Calibration prompt, press the TARE key. Use the Fn key to select yes, then press the TARE key. The First Calibration Weight prompt is displayed.
7. Choose the first point: zero with no load, or the test weights. Put that load on the platform — or leave the platform empty for zero — then press the TARE key.
8. Use the UNITS and Fn keys to set the display to the actual weight on the scale platform.
9. Make sure the platform is stable, then press the TARE key. A series of dashes appears and then disappears, and the Second Calibration Weight prompt is displayed. The book stresses: while the dashes are showing, keep the loaded or empty scale stable.
10. Take the opposite point: if the first point was zero, place the test weights on the platform; if the first point was the test weights, remove the load so the scale is at zero with no load.
11. Press the TARE key, then use the UNITS and Fn keys to set the display to the actual weight on the scale platform.
12. Make sure the platform is stable, then press the TARE key. The dashes appear and disappear again, and the display advances to the Zero Tracking Range prompt.
13. From the Calibration prompt, continue through the remaining setup prompts until the setup and calibration process is complete; the indicator will reset and then display weight. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. modes.title: Fine Span Adjustment
modes.blurb: A final span correction after calibration. The book requires a test load of at least 10% of the scale capacity on the platform before adjustments can be made.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The Model 185 and 185B calibrate from the keypad in two ways: a two-point calibration using zero/no load and a test load, and a fine span adjustment under a test load of at least 10% of capacity. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Do not operate the membrane keypad with pointed objects such as pencils, pens, or fingernails; the book says damage from this practice is not covered under warranty. If your metrology laws require physical sealing, the book's lead and wire security seal prevents the calibration jumper from being removed and re-installed to enter setup and calibration, and the locking screws cannot be removed without damaging that seal.
1. With the indicator ON, loosen the four Phillips screws securing the rear housing to the front housing and remove the rear housing to reach calibration jumper J3.
2. Remove the calibration jumper J3. The first setup prompt is displayed.
3. Re-install the calibration jumper and press the TARE key. The Remote Display prompt is displayed.
4. At Remote Display, press the TARE key to view the current setting; press the TARE key again to keep it, or use the Fn key to change it and the TARE key to select it. If Remote Display is enabled, the Remote Serial Data Type prompt appears next.
5. Continue through the setup prompts before Calibration, keeping each current setting unless the job requires a change: Domestic or International, Legal For Trade, Weighing Unit 1, Interval Setting, Decimal Point Position, Capacity, and Weighing Unit 2. Stop at the Calibration prompt. For entries, the UNITS key moves the blinking cursor left, the Fn key changes the blinking character, and the TARE key retains the value and advances.
6. At the Calibration prompt, remove and re-install the calibration jumper J3. The Fine Span prompt is displayed.
7. Press the TARE key. The display changes to show the scale weight, with the Fine Span annunciator on.
8. Apply a TEST LOAD of at least 10% of the scale capacity.
9. If the displayed weight does not match the TEST LOAD weight, press the Fn key to increase the displayed weight or the UNITS key to decrease it until it matches.
10. Press the TARE key to return to the Calibration prompt.
11. From the Calibration prompt, continue through the remaining setup prompts until the setup and calibration process is complete; the indicator will reset and then display weight. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. modes.title: Dual-Point with Zero (First Zero)

modes.text:

1. Start with the display showing CAL or CAL?.
2. With CAL displayed, press the TARE key. The display changes to CAL1=.
3. With CAL? displayed, press the TARE key; the display changes to no. Press the Fn key to toggle to yes, then press the TARE key. The display changes to CAL1=.
4. How values are entered on this keypad: pressing the TARE key saves the value entered or displayed and advances to the next prompt. The blinking character is the cursor — press the UNITS key to move it to the left, and the Fn key to change the blinking character to the next value.
5. The display shows CAL1=. This is the first of two calibration weights. It can be zero with no load, or your test weights.
6. Press the TARE key to view the current setting.
7. If this point is zero with no load, press the TARE key.
8. If this point is your test weights, use the UNITS and Fn keys to input the value of the test weights.
9. Place the weights on the scale platform, then press the TARE key.
10. A series of dashes appears, running left to right, then the dashes disappear. The display shows CAL2=.
11. CAL2= is the second calibration weight — zero with no load, or your test weights, whichever you did not use first.
12. Press the TARE key to view the current setting.
13. If this point is zero with no load, press the TARE key.
14. If this point is your test weights, use the UNITS and Fn keys to input the value of the test weights.
15. Place the weights on the scale platform, then press the TARE key.
16. The dashes appear and disappear again, and the display shows CAL3=.
17. CAL3= is not used in this mode. Press the UNITS key to skip CAL3= and advance to the SetgC? prompt.
18. When the last calibration point is done, the display shows SetgC?. To skip the gravity-constant setup, press the TARE key to advance to the Sio? prompt. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Dual-Point with Zero (First Zero)
modes.blurb: First-time calibration and complete recalibration. Uses two points, zero and a test load, in any order.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 200 Panel Mount has five calibration modes named by the book: Dual-Point with Zero, Dual-Point without Zero, Single-Point for Span Only, Single-Point for Zero Only, and Calibration C Numbers. Four are drafted below from the steps in the extract; the C Numbers entry procedure is named but its detailed entry steps are not in the extract, so it is flagged rather than guessed. Pick the mode that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Turn the indicator ON.
2. Remove the 2 screws securing the calibration switch access cover on the rear panel.
3. Insert a small screwdriver or other tool through the calibration switch access hole and press and release the calibration switch.
4. Keep pressing and releasing the calibration switch to rotate through the setup starting menus until Calibration is the starting point.
5. At the Calibration prompt, press the TARE/ENTER key.
6. If the indicator asks whether calibration is desired, press the ASTERISK/UP ARROW key to change the answer to yes, then press TARE/ENTER to continue to the first calibration prompt, CAL1.
7. At CAL1, choose the first point. If it is zero, leave the scale empty and press TARE/ENTER.
8. If the first point is the test load, use the UNITS/LEFT ARROW and ASTERISK/UP ARROW keys to enter the true test-weight value. Digits enter from the right and move left.
9. Place the test weights on the scale platform, then press TARE/ENTER.
10. Wait while a series of dashes shows, then the display advances to CAL2.
11. At CAL2, take the opposite point. If it is zero, remove the weights and press TARE/ENTER.
12. If CAL2 is the test load, enter the true test-weight value, place the weights on the scale, then press TARE/ENTER.
13. Wait for the dashes to finish and the display to advance to CAL3.
14. CAL3 is not used. Press TARE/ENTER to skip it and advance out of calibration.
15. To exit setup, press the ASTERISK/UP ARROW key while any setup menu selection is displayed, or cycle power by pressing ON/OFF twice. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. The extract says the access cover is removed for entry, but it does not print a re-install or reseal instruction in the calibration extract, so none is included here.
References: Cardinal 200 Panel Mount Installation & Technical Manual Doc 8200-M035-O1 Rev C — Keypad Functions (printed pp. 13-15), Setup and Calibration and Enter Setup Mode (printed p. 19), setup exit (printed p. 20), Calibration modes (printed p. 29), Dual-Point with Zero (First Zero) Calibration (printed p. 30). 7. Make sure the scale is empty.
8. At CAL1, press the TARE/ENTER key.
9. When CAL2 is displayed, press the ZERO key.
10. Know how it lands: this establishes a new zero only. The conversion factor, or span, is not affected.
11. To exit setup, press the ASTERISK/UP ARROW key while any setup menu selection is displayed, or cycle power by pressing ON/OFF twice. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. The extract says the access cover is removed for entry, but it does not print a re-install or reseal instruction in the calibration extract, so none is included here.

modes.title: Load Calibration with Test Weights
modes.blurb: The 204's one calibration: a known load goes on the scale and you key in its true value. First-time setups and recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. On the 204 it is done entirely from the keypad — no computer needed — and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: If this indicator is used in a commercial application, it must be tested and sealed by your local weights and measurement official. The 204 is built to take a lead and wire security seal that keeps unauthorized hands out of the calibration adjustments.
1. Turn the 204 off.
2. Remove the calibration access screw on the upper left corner of the rear panel.
3. Insert a small non-metallic tool into the screw hole and press and hold the calibration switch.
4. While holding it, press the ON/OFF key. The display shows int= — you are in setup and calibration.
5. Three keys run setup: PRINT saves the setting shown and moves to the next prompt, ASTERISK moves the blinking cursor to the left digit, and UNITS changes the blinking character to the next value.
6. At int= (Scale Interval), press ASTERISK to show the current setting. If it is right, press PRINT to keep it and move on. To change it, press UNITS until the right interval — 1, 2, 5, 10 or 20 — shows, then press PRINT.
7. At Unit= (Weighing Units), press UNITS to show the current setting. Press PRINT to save what is shown, or press UNITS to change it and then press PRINT.
8. At dPP= (Decimal Point), press ASTERISK to show the setting, press UNITS until the number for the decimal position you want shows, then press PRINT.
9. At CAP= (Scale Capacity), press ASTERISK to show the setting. Enter the capacity digit by digit: UNITS sets the blinking digit, ASTERISK steps left to the next digit. When all digits are in, press PRINT.
10. At CAL=, press ASTERISK. The display shows 0, meaning No. Press UNITS to select 1, meaning Yes, then press PRINT. The display changes to LOAd=.
11. Make certain the scale platform is empty and free of debris, then place the calibrated test weights on the platform. The book recommends at least 50 percent of the scale's capacity; 70 to 100 percent is preferred.
12. Press PRINT.
13. Key in the exact amount of the test weights, using UNITS and ASTERISK the same way you entered the capacity. Check that the number matches the total weight of the test weights, and that the last digit agrees with the scale interval.
14. Press PRINT.
15. After a moment the display shows unLOAd. Remove the test weights from the platform, then press PRINT. The calibration factor is now stored in the indicator's nonvolatile memory.
16. Keep pressing PRINT to step through the remaining setup prompts — trA= (zero tracking) on through EoP= (end-of-print line feeds) — accepting each setting or changing it as the job needs, until the display shows dOnE. Remove the power from the indicator and re-assemble it for use, calibration access screw back in. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If this indicator is used in a commercial application, it must be tested and sealed by your local weights and measurement official — the 204 takes a lead and wire security seal to keep unauthorized hands out of the calibration adjustments.
References: Cardinal 204 Installation & Technical Manual Doc 8555-M313-O1 Rev G — Setup and Calibration [PDF pp. 17-21], Calibration [PDF p. 18], Calibration Seal Installation [PDF p. 23]

modes.title: Dual-Point with Zero (First Zero)
modes.blurb: The standard calibration: two points — empty zero and one test load, in either order. The book's pick for first-time calibration and complete recalibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 205 has five ways to calibrate — three need test weights, one needs only an empty scale, and one reuses the calibration C numbers recorded from a good calibration. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. With the calibration prompt displayed, press the TARE/ENTER key. The display shows the current setting.
2. If calibration is desired, press the UP ARROW key so the display changes to yes, then press TARE/ENTER to continue to the first calibration point. If not, press TARE/ENTER to advance past calibration to the next menu.
3. The display shows the first calibration weight prompt. This point can be zero with no load, or the test weights.
4. If this point is zero: make sure the scale is empty, then press TARE/ENTER.
5. If this point is the test weights: enter the true value of the calibrated test weights using the UNITS/LEFT ARROW key to move the blinking cursor left and the UP ARROW key to change the blinking character. Digits start on the right and proceed to the left.
6. Place the weights on the scale platform, then press TARE/ENTER.
7. A series of dashes marches across the display, left to right, then the display shows the second calibration weight prompt.
8. At the second prompt, take the opposite point: if the first was the weights, empty the scale and press TARE/ENTER for zero; if the first was zero, enter the test weight value, place the weights, and press TARE/ENTER.
9. The dashes march again, then the display advances to the next setup prompt. The calibration is stored.
10. When the second calibration point finishes, a series of dashes marches across the display and then the display advances to the next setup prompt — that is the book's signal the calibration took. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Calibration C Numbers
modes.blurb: Restore a previous calibration from its recorded C numbers — no test weights. Only honest if nothing that affects calibration has changed.
modes.text:

4. At the first C number prompt, press TARE/ENTER to show its current value.

modes.title: Guardian Scale Tweak
modes.blurb: Only when a Guardian scale is connected to the indicator. After linearization testing shows the reading off inside one band of weights, this nudges just that band into tolerance.
modes.text:

3. At the Guardian prompt, press the UP ARROW key to select YES.
4. At the tweak low weight prompt, enter the low end of the weight range that needs adjusting — the book's example: reading 5 pounds low between 10,000 and 15,000 pounds takes a tweak low weight of 10000 — using the UP ARROW and UNITS/LEFT ARROW keys, then press TARE/ENTER.
5. At the tweak high weight prompt, enter the high end of the range — 15000 in the book's example — then press TARE/ENTER.
6. At the tweak weight prompt, enter the amount of weight to add to that range to bring the reading into tolerance — 5 in the book's example. Pressing the NET key changes the sign, to subtract instead.
7. Press TARE/ENTER to save it and advance to the next menu.
8. When the second calibration point finishes, a series of dashes marches across the display and then the display advances to the next setup prompt — that is the book's signal the calibration took. modes.title: Two-Point Calibration
modes.blurb: The standard calibration: two points — empty-scale zero and one known test weight, in either order. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 220 calibrates with two or three weights — each point either empty-scale zero or your test weights — and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Getting into setup means removing the calibration switch access screw on the rear panel and pressing the switch behind it. The book says a 220 used in a commercial application must be tested and sealed by your local weights and measures official, and the indicator is built to take a lead and wire security seal to keep unauthorized hands out of the calibration adjustments.
1. Turn the indicator ON.
2. Remove the calibration switch access screw on the rear panel.
3. Put a small screwdriver or other tool through the calibration switch access hole and press and release the calibration switch. The display shows SETUP.
4. Keep pressing and releasing the calibration switch to rotate the starting menu until CALIBRATE shows.
5. Press the ENTER key — calibration starts at the CAL WT 1= prompt. If the display instead shows CALIBRATE? N, press the 1/YES key so it shows CALIBRATE? Y, then press ENTER to continue to CAL WT 1.
6. The display shows CAL WT 1=0. This first point is either zero with no load, or the test weights.
7. For zero: take all weight off the scale and press the ENTER key. For test weights: key in the true value of the weights — the digits enter from the right side of the display — put the weights on the scale platform, then press ENTER.
8. A series of dashes runs across the display, then the display shows CAL WT 2.
9. At CAL WT 2=0, set the second point the same way: empty scale and ENTER for zero, or key in the value, weights on the scale, then ENTER for the test load.
10. The dashes run again, then the display shows CAL WT 3.
11. Two-point calibration does not use CAL WT 3. Press ENTER to skip it and advance to SERIAL?.
12. Pressing the calibration switch at any prompt returns you to the SETUP menu. To leave setup, press the ASTERISK key with a menu selection showing, or cycle the power — press the ON/OFF key twice. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. Put the calibration switch access screw back in the rear panel, and if this scale works in a commercial application, have it tested and sealed by your local weights and measures official before it goes back into trade.

[PDF pp. 24, 41-42, 53-54, 85]

modes.title: Three-Point Calibration
modes.blurb: Three points instead of two: zero, a mid-point weight, and the full test load — a straighter line across the range.
modes.text:

CAUTION: Getting into setup means removing the calibration switch access screw on the rear panel and pressing the switch behind it. 6. The display shows CAL WT 1=0. In three-point calibration, each of the three weights can be zero with no load, the test weights or test load, or a mid-point weight.
7. Set the first point: empty scale and ENTER for zero, or key in the value — the digits enter from the right side of the display — weights on the scale platform, then ENTER.

10. The dashes run again, then the display shows CAL WT 3 — the last of the three calibration weights.
11. Set the last point the same way at CAL WT 3=. The dashes run, then the display shows SERIAL?.

modes.title: Calibration C Numbers
modes.blurb: No test weights at all: type in the four recorded C numbers and the indicator returns to the calibration they were recorded from.
modes.text:

modes.title: Fine Span Adjustment
