modes.title: Multi-Point Calibration
modes.blurb: Two test weights and an empty scale, three calibration points — CAL 1, CAL 2 and CAL 3 — covering zero, a mid-point weight and the test load, in any order. Builds two conversion factors for a straighter line.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 225 has seven ways to do it from its Scale 1 Calibration Menu — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time. Four of them use a test weight; the parameter and C number routes restore a recorded calibration without weights.
Start note: how to enter setup sits outside the calibration pages this guide was built from, so step 1 picks up at the setup menu.
1. Open the Setup Menu number 2 for this scale. From there, press the 5 key and then the ENTER key to proceed to the Scale 1 Calibration Menu.
2. From the Scale 1 Calibration Menu, press the 1 and 0 keys and then the ENTER key. The display shows the capacity, interval, decimal point position and CAL 1 equals 0.0 — that is where every calibration mode starts.
3. From the Scale 1 Calibration Menu, press the 1 and 0 keys and then the ENTER key. The display shows CAL 1 equals 0.0. This first point can be zero with no load, the mid-point weight, or the test load.
4. If the first point is zero with no load, press the ENTER key. The display flashes Calibrating for a few seconds, then shows CAL 2.
5. If the first point is the mid-point weight or the test load, place the weights on the scale, use the numeric keys to enter the true value of the load, and press the ENTER key. The display flashes Calibrating, then shows CAL 2.
6. At CAL 2: if this point is zero with no load, press the 0 key and then the ENTER key. The display flashes Calibrating, then shows CAL 3.
7. If CAL 2 is the mid-point weight or the test load, place the weights on the scale, enter the true value with the numeric keys, and press the ENTER key. The display flashes Calibrating, then shows CAL 3.
8. At CAL 3, the last of the three points: if it is zero with no load, press the 0 key and then the ENTER key, and the display returns to the Scale 1 Calibration Menu.
9. If CAL 3 is the mid-point weight or the test load, place the weights on the scale, enter the true value with the numeric keys, and press the ENTER key. The display flashes Calibrating, then returns to the Scale 1 Calibration Menu.
10. When the Scale 1 calibration is complete, press EXIT — the Navigation Keys Up Arrow — to return to Setup Menu number 2. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If you broke a wire seal or removed a screw to get in, the manual's setup-entry and seal pages are not in the pages pulled for this guide — check the book's Security Seals section before you reseal.
References: Cardinal 225 Installation and Technical Manual Doc 8200-M538-O1 — Calibration Modes (printed pp. 62-63), Multi-Point / Dual-Point with Zero / Dual-Point without Zero / Single-Point for Span Only / Single-Point for Zero Only / Calibration Parameters / Calibration C Numbers (printed pp. 64-70), Fine Span and High Resolution Adjustment (printed p. 63), Scale 1 Calibration Completed (printed p. 71). modes.title: Dual-Point with Zero (First Zero)
modes.blurb: The standard calibration: one test weight on an empty scale, two points — zero and test load, in any order. The book says to use this for first-time calibration and complete recalibration.
modes.text:

Four of them use a test weight; the parameter and C number routes restore a recorded calibration without weights.
Start note: how to enter setup sits outside the calibration pages this guide was built from, so step 1 picks up at the setup menu.
1. Open the Setup Menu number 2 for this scale. From there, press the 5 key and then the ENTER key to proceed to the Scale 1 Calibration Menu.
2. From the Scale 1 Calibration Menu, press the 1 and 0 keys and then the ENTER key. The display shows the capacity, interval, decimal point position and CAL 1 equals 0.0 — that is where every calibration mode starts.
3. From the Scale 1 Calibration Menu, press the 1 and 0 keys and then the ENTER key. The display shows CAL 1 equals 0.0. This first point can be zero with no load or the test load.
4. If the first point is zero with no load, press the ENTER key. The display flashes Calibrating, then shows CAL 2.
5. If the first point is the test load, place the weights on the scale, enter the true value of the test load with the numeric keys, and press the ENTER key. The display flashes Calibrating, then shows CAL 2.
6. At CAL 2: if this point is zero with no load, press the 0 key and then the ENTER key. The display flashes Calibrating, then shows CAL 3.
7. If CAL 2 is the test load, place the weights on the scale, enter the true value of the test load with the numeric keys, and press the ENTER key. The display flashes Calibrating, then shows CAL 3.
8. At CAL 3 the display shows CAL 3 equals blank. This weight is not used — press the ENTER key to skip it, and the display returns to the Scale 1 Calibration Menu.
9. When the Scale 1 calibration is complete, press EXIT — the Navigation Keys Up Arrow — to return to Setup Menu number 2. modes.title: Zero Calibration (CAL:ZERO)
modes.blurb: Teach the empty scale its zero with real weight readings. This is the first half of every calibration with test weights — the book says an initial Zero calibration must be performed before a Span calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The Model 250 calibrates with real test weights, or by entering the load cell's mV/V readings directly when test weights are not easily available, and it can add up to five linearization points for a scale that is not straight. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: The Model 250 will happily calibrate a scale that is wrong for Legal for Trade use — the book says it should not be assumed that just because it has successfully calibrated a scale, that the scale is correct for Legal for Trade. Always check the BUILD parameter against the approval specification, and refer to the book's approvals chapter for the details.
1. Make sure the BUILD and OPTION settings are configured first — the book says they MUST be configured before calibration is attempted.
2. Get into Full Setup. If the indicator is sealed, press the setup button on the rear of the indicator to enable setup mode; otherwise press and hold POWER and the function key together to open setup mode.
3. In Full Setup, select the CAL group using the GRP key.
4. Select CAL:ZERO and press the SEL key to start. The display shows the current weight.
5. Remove all weight from the scale.
6. Press SEL, EDT or OK to execute a Zero Calibration. The display shows Z.in.P to indicate that zeroing is in progress.
7. When the process is complete, the weight displays so you can check the zero. Press the ITM key to exit the Zero routine, or press SEL, EDT or OK to repeat the operation.
8. Press the ITM key to leave each calibration routine, and press POWER and the function key together to save changes and exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If this scale is sealed for Legal for Trade, place the physical seal plastic cover over the load cell and comm port connectors, install the drill head screw, and thread the wire security seal through the indentations in the plastic cover and the drill head screw — the setup mode cannot be accessed again without pressing the Setup button.

3. In Full Setup, select the CAL group using the GRP key.
4. Complete the zero and full scale span calibrations first — both points are used in the linearization, and they are assumed to have no linearization error.
5. Select ED.LIN. Press the SEL key to step through the list of points. Each point shows as L, the point number, and the approximate percentage of full scale — for example L1.050 means point one is active at about 50% of full scale; a row of dashes means the point is unused.
6. Press OK to change the selected point, or ITM to exit without changes. After pressing OK, the current weight reading displays.
7. Add the calibration test weight to the scale. The closer the test weight is to the point of maximum error in linearity, the more effective the correction will be.
8. Press OK to enter a corrected weight value for this point, using the SEL and EDT keys. Press the OK key to trigger the linearization routine — the display shows L.in P while it runs.
9. When the process is complete, the display shows the weight so you can check the new reading. Press ITM to leave the routine, or OK to repeat the operation. Repeat for up to five points total.
10. To clear a point: select CLR.LIN and press SEL to step through the points, then OK to choose the point to clear. The indicator prompts CONT. N — press ITM to switch between Cont. N (No) and Cont. Y (Yes), and press OK to accept your choice. Press ITM to return to CLR.LIN.
11. Press the ITM key to leave each calibration routine, and press POWER and the function key together to save changes and exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If this scale is sealed for Legal for Trade, place the physical seal plastic cover over the load cell and comm port connectors, install the drill head screw, and thread the wire security seal through the indentations in the plastic cover and the drill head screw — the setup mode cannot be accessed again without pressing the Setup button.

modes.title: Reset Calibration (FAC.CAL)
modes.blurb: Wipe the calibration back to factory condition. The book defines this in one paragraph only — it gives no keypress steps for it here, and sends you to the FAC.CAL menu item.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The Model 250 calibrates with real test weights, or by entering the load cell's mV/V readings directly when test weights are not easily available, and it can add up to five linearization points for a scale that is not straight. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: The Model 250 will happily calibrate a scale that is wrong for Legal for Trade use — the book says it should not be assumed that just because it has successfully calibrated a scale, that the scale is correct for Legal for Trade. modes.title: Front Panel Calibration
modes.blurb: The everyday calibration at the indicator itself: empty scale for zero, test weights on for span, and the hooks-or-chains rezero built into the same pass.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 320IS Plus calibrates from its front panel, or by EDP commands through the I/O Module — pick the way that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time. Every way has the same bones: zero on the empty scale, tell it the true test weight, span with the weights on, and an optional rezero if the weights hung from hooks or chains.
1. Place the indicator in setup mode — the display reads CONFIG.
2. Remove all weight from the scale platform.
3. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, for the zero calibration.
4. Press the key the book shows here until the display reads CALIBR, then press the key the book shows here. WZERO displays.
5. Press the key the book shows here to calibrate zero. The display shows *CAL* while calibration is in progress. When it finishes, the A/D count for the zero calibration is displayed. The book warns: do not adjust this value after WSPAN has been set.
6. Press the key the book shows here again to save the zero calibration value and go to the next prompt, WVAL.
7. Place the test weights on the scale.
8. Press the key the book shows here to show the test weight value, then use the numeric keypad to enter the actual test weight.
9. Press the key the book shows here to save the value. WSPAN displays.
10. Press the key the book shows here to calibrate span. The display shows *CAL* while it calibrates. When it finishes, the A/D count for the span calibration is displayed.
11. Press the key the book shows here again to save the span calibration value. REZERO displays.
12. If no hooks or chains were used to hang the test weights, take the test weights off and press the key the book shows here to return to the CALIBR menu.
13. If hooks or chains were used, remove them and the test weights so the scale is completely empty, then press the key the book shows here to rezero the scale. The display shows *CAL* while the zero and span calibrations are adjusted.
14. After a rezero, when the adjusted A/D count for the zero calibration is displayed, press the key the book shows here to save the value, then press the key the book shows here to return to the CALIBR menu.
15. Press the key the book shows here until the display reads CONFIG, then press the key the book shows here to exit setup mode. (The EDP path leaves setup with the KUPARROW command instead.) Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. When calibrating to a new scale, the book adds one more step after exiting setup mode: press the ZERO key to set zero and adjust for deadload. No screw or seal step is printed in this extract, so none is included.
References: Rice Lake 320IS Plus Installation Manual PN 85353 Rev F — Calibration overview (§4.0, printed p. 37), Front Panel Calibration (§4.1, printed p. 37), EDP Command Calibration (§4.2, printed p. 38). [PDF pp. 43-44]

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: No button-pushing at the indicator: WZERO, WVAL and WSPAN commands sent from a terminal or computer. The book says this needs the I/O Module — its EDP port is the connection.

modes.title: First Zero
modes.blurb: The most common zero: a fresh empty-scale zero, then span with a test weight. The book's choice for first-time calibration and complete recalibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. This book always starts calibration by establishing a zero — a no-load reference — and a complete calibration also needs a span, a test load reference. There are five ways to get the zero: First Zero, Last Zero, False Zero, Only Zero, and Cal Reset. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time. Any time during calibration, pressing the keys the book shows here lets you back up one step in the procedure.
1. From the Weigh Mode, start Fast Calibration. On the 350 IS, press the key combination the book shows here; the display reads Setup - Enter - Code! Then press the code keys the book shows here; the display reads Fast - Cal - First - Zero?
2. On the 355 IS, key in the code the book shows here; the display reads Setup - Enter - Code! Then key in the second code the book shows here; the display reads Fast - Cal - First - Zero?
3. Or, if you are already in the Setup Mode looking at any setup parameter, press the key the book shows here; the display reads Enter - =Cal! Press the key the book shows here, and the display reads First - Zero?
4. From First - Zero?, press the scroll key the book shows here to step through the five zero methods — First Zero, Last Zero, False Zero, Only Zero, and Cal Reset.
5. The display reads First - Zero?. Remove any load from the scale.
6. Press the key the book shows here to establish zero. The display reads 0.00.
7. Pause for motion delay. The display reads Enter - Load.
8. Place the test weight on the scale — the book's example uses a 100 pound test weight. You can enter the test weight value before or after putting the weight on; if you enter it first, the display reads Add - Load until the weight is applied.
9. Enter the true value of the test weight — the book's example enters 100.
10. Press the key the book shows here to establish span. The display reads the weight — 100.00 in the example.
11. Pause for motion delay. The display reads Cal - Good?.
12. If the display instead reads ReCal - ??? — that happens when the change from the previous calibration is significant, or the calibration weight is less than 5 percent of full scale — the book recommends running the calibration a second time: press the key the book shows here to recalibrate, or the other key the book shows here to skip it.
13. Press the key the book shows here to accept the calibration. The display reads Enter - =Stor.
14. To save and leave: at Enter - =Stor, press the key the book shows here to save the calibration; the display reads Enter - =End. Press the key the book shows here to exit calibration. To leave without saving: at Enter - =Stor, press the other key the book shows here instead; the display reads Enter - =Undo; then press the key the book shows here to exit. Prove it: with the test weight still on, the display reads exactly that weight — 100.00 in the book's example; take the weight off and it reads 0.00. The book warns that when you save a calibration, any parameters you changed in the Setup Mode are saved with their new selections too.
References: GSE Model 350/355 IS Intrinsically Safe Indicator Technical Reference Manual Version 1.0 — Chapter 4: Calibration: Setup Mode Calibration and Fast Calibration, Establishing Zero (First Zero, Last Zero, False Zero, Only Zero, Cal Reset), Establishing A Span, Exiting Calibration. [PDF pp. 76-88]

modes.title: First Zero — Full Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The full calibration: a fresh empty-scale zero, then one known test weight for the span. The book calls First Zero the most common zeroing procedure — use it for first-time calibration and complete recalibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The GSE 370 and 375 give you five ways to set the zero — First Zero, Last Zero, False Zero, Only Zero, and Cal Reset — and once the zero is set, the span follows the same way every time: put a known weight on, tell the scale what it is, and let it learn. The two models take different keys to say go: TARE on the 370, SAMPLE/Enter on the 375. Pick the way that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Get into Calibration Mode from weigh mode. Fast Calibration on the 370: press ZERO and SELECT together — the display reads Setup, Enter Code. Then press ZERO, PRINT, UNITS, TARE in that order — the display reads Fast Cal, then First Zero?
2. Fast Calibration on the 375: key in 100 and press SELECT — the display reads Setup, Enter Code. Then key in 54321 and press SAMPLE/Enter — the display reads Fast Cal, then First Zero?
3. Or come in through the Setup Mode: while viewing any setup parameter, press ZERO — the display reads Enter =Cal — then press TARE on the 370 or SAMPLE/Enter on the 375 to land on First Zero.
4. Calibration can also be started from a computer on the comm port: if the scale receives the data stream 100%s54321%e, it goes into Fast Calibration.
5. If access is refused and the display reads Unit Seald, the book says access to the Setup or Calibration Mode was denied — check the internal YES/NO program jumper.
6. From First Zero, press SELECT to scroll through the five zero methods — First Zero, Last Zero, False Zero, Only Zero, and Cal Reset — and stop on the one you want. On the 370 you confirm with TARE; on the 375 with SAMPLE/Enter. Any time during calibration, pressing ZERO or CLR backs up one step.
7. With First Zero? showing, remove any load on the scale.
8. Press TARE (370) or SAMPLE/Enter (375) to establish zero. The display reads 0.00.
9. Pause for the motion delay. The display reads Enter Load 0.00.
10. Place a test weight on the scale — the book's worked example uses a 100 lb test weight.
11. Key in the true value of the test weight — 100 in the book's example. The display shows your number.
12. You can also key the value in first: the display then reads Add Load, telling you to put the test weight on; then press TARE or SAMPLE/Enter.
13. Press TARE (370) or SAMPLE/Enter (375) to establish span. The display reads the test weight value — 100.00 in the example.
14. Pause for the motion delay. The display reads Cal Good? — the calibration is ready for the exit steps below.
15. If instead the display reads ReCal ??? — that happens when the calibration weight is less than 5% of full scale, or the change from the previous calibration is significant — the book recommends performing the calibration a second time: press TARE or SAMPLE/Enter to recalibrate, or press ZERO to skip recalibration.
16. Once zero and span are established, the new calibration has to be saved before it counts in Weigh Mode. At Cal Good?, press TARE (370) or SAMPLE/Enter (375) to accept; at Enter =Stor press it again to save; at Enter =End press it once more to exit calibration. To leave without saving: accept at Cal Good?, then at Enter =Stor press CLR — the display reads Enter =Undo — then press TARE or SAMPLE/Enter to reach Enter =End and once more to exit; the old calibration stays in effect. Prove it: take everything off and the scale should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. One warning from the book to keep in mind: when saving calibration, any parameters changed in the Setup Mode are saved along with it.
References: GSE Model 370 & Model 375 Precision Counting Scale Technical Reference Manual Version 1.0 — Chapter 4: Calibration: Setup Mode Calibration and Fast Calibration (printed p. 61) [PDF p. 67]; First Zero (printed p. 62) [PDF p. 68]; Last Zero (printed pp. 63-64) [PDF pp. 69-70]; False Zero (printed pp. 65-66) [PDF pp. 71-72]; Only Zero (printed pp. 66-67) [PDF pp. 72-73]; Reset Calibration (printed pp. 67-68) [PDF pp. 73-74]; Multi-Point Linearization (printed pp. 69-70) [PDF pp. 75-76]; Establishing a Span and Exiting Calibration (printed pp. 70-71) [PDF pp. 76-77]; Unit Seald setup error (printed p. 74) [PDF p. 80].

modes.title: Cal Reset — Recover From Over-Load or Under-Load
modes.blurb: For when an over-load or under-load condition (Code 02 or Code 03) blocks calibration from completing. Cal Reset adjusts the zero and gain factors of the A/D amplifier to factory default values for maximum sensitivity — and after it, a complete recalibration is required.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The GSE 370 and 375 give you five ways to set the zero — First Zero, Last Zero, False Zero, Only Zero, and Cal Reset — and once the zero is set, the span follows the same way every time: put a known weight on, tell the scale what it is, and let it learn. The two models take different keys to say go: TARE on the 370, SAMPLE/Enter on the 375. Pick the way that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Get into Calibration Mode from weigh mode. Fast Calibration on the 370: press ZERO and SELECT together — the display reads Setup, Enter Code. Then press ZERO, PRINT, UNITS, TARE in that order — the display reads Fast Cal, then First Zero?
2. Fast Calibration on the 375: key in 100 and press SELECT — the display reads Setup, Enter Code. Then key in 54321 and press SAMPLE/Enter — the display reads Fast Cal, then First Zero?
3. Or come in through the Setup Mode: while viewing any setup parameter, press ZERO — the display reads Enter =Cal — then press TARE on the 370 or SAMPLE/Enter on the 375 to land on First Zero.
4. Calibration can also be started from a computer on the comm port: if the scale receives the data stream 100%s54321%e, it goes into Fast Calibration.
5. If access is refused and the display reads Unit Seald, the book says access to the Setup or Calibration Mode was denied — check the internal YES/NO program jumper.
6. From First Zero, press SELECT to scroll through the five zero methods — First Zero, Last Zero, False Zero, Only Zero, and Cal Reset — and stop on the one you want. On the 370 you confirm with TARE; on the 375 with SAMPLE/Enter. Any time during calibration, pressing ZERO or CLR backs up one step.
7. If Code 02 (under-load) or Code 03 (over-load) is displayed during calibration, the book says: press CLR to perform a calibration reset.
8. Back up to the First Zero? prompt: press ZERO or CLR — the book says either key backs up one step in the procedure. In its worked example, after Code 03 shows with the test weight on, it presses ZERO to get back to First Zero?
9. Remove any load on the scale.
10. Press TARE (370) or SAMPLE/Enter (375) to establish zero. The display reads 0.00.
11. Pause for the motion delay. The display reads Enter Load 0.00.
12. Place a test weight on the scale — the book's example uses 100 lb — and key in its true value.
13. Press TARE or SAMPLE/Enter to establish span. Pause for the motion delay; the display reads Cal Good? — ready for the exit steps below.
14. The book is explicit about the finish: after a calibration reset, a complete recalibration is required, and the reset's effects do not take effect until the scale has been recalibrated and the calibration information saved — so do not skip the save in the exit steps.
15. Once zero and span are established, the new calibration has to be saved before it counts in Weigh Mode. At Cal Good?, press TARE (370) or SAMPLE/Enter (375) to accept; at Enter =Stor press it again to save; at Enter =End press it once more to exit calibration. To leave without saving: accept at Cal Good?, then at Enter =Stor press CLR — the display reads Enter =Undo — then press TARE or SAMPLE/Enter to reach Enter =End and once more to exit; the old calibration stays in effect. Prove it: take everything off and the scale should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. One warning from the book to keep in mind: when saving calibration, any parameters changed in the Setup Mode are saved along with it.

modes.blurb: Add up to five calibration points across the range to straighten out a load cell that reads a little off in the middle. The book says it may significantly improve accuracy if the load cell signal has good repeatability and stability. Parameter P119 turns it on.

modes.title: Standard Calibration
modes.blurb: The full front-panel calibration: empty-scale zero plus one known test weight. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 380 Synergy indicator (also 380X and 381) calibrates from the front panel or by serial EDP commands — an empty-scale zero and a known test weight for span, with up to four extra linear points when the job needs them. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: In certain Legal for Trade applications it is necessary to seal the indicator to restrict access to the CAL jumper. Breaking of the seal terminates the Legal for Trade status of the indicator because the seal limits access to the configuration menu. From this book: the CAL jumper must be removed to perform calibration.
1. Make sure the CAL jumper (JP3, inside the indicator) is removed — with the jumper open, the indicator can be calibrated and configured. Setup mode parameters cannot be reached with the jumper in place.
2. Power the indicator up and press the key the book shows here once, momentarily, during the startup sequence. Only press it once — do not press and hold, and do not double press; the key press must end before start-up completes. SETUP displays.
3. Move to Config. config displays.
4. Move to Calibr. Calibr displays.
5. Open the calibration menu. wzero displays. Note: see the alternative zero modes if the job calls for a rezero, a last zero, or a temporary zero.
6. Make sure there is no weight on the scale.
7. At WZERO, perform the zero calibration. ok displays.
8. Move to WVAL and display the current test weight value.
9. Enter the true value of the test weights you will use if it needs changing, then accept it. WSPAN displays.
10. Place the specified amount of test weight on the scale.
11. Perform the span calibration. ok displays.
12. Optionally move to SPNCNT to view the raw count at the span weight. Span calibration is complete at this point — continue to the Linear Calibration mode if the job needs extra points.
13. Return to weigh mode (the book's front-panel procedures finish by pressing the key shown three times). Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If this indicator is sealed for Legal for Trade, put the CAL jumper back in place first — short JP3, aligned squarely on the pins: on the 380 and 380X, torque the four front plate screws to 10 in-lb and run the lead sealing wire through the lower two fillister screws and the bottom-center hole, then seal the wire; on the 381, reseal with two self-destructive adhesive labels over the seam between the two halves.
References: 380/380X/381 Synergy Series Battery Powered Digital Weight Indicators Technical Manual Doc 201481 (PN 201481 Rev K) — Seal the Indicator (§4.1, printed p. 38), Setup – Calibration Menu (§4.3.3, printed p. 42), Calibration and Front Panel Calibration (§5.0–5.1, printed pp. 48-49), Alternative Zero Calibrations (§5.2, printed p. 49), EDP Command Calibration (§5.3, printed p. 50), Program Menu gravity parameters (§4.3.5, printed pp. 44-45) [PDF pp. 38-50]

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: No button-pushing: calibrate over a serial cable with SC commands. The indicator must respond OK after every step, or the procedure must be done again.
modes.text:

From this book: the CAL jumper must be removed to perform calibration.
1. Make sure the CAL jumper (JP3, inside the indicator) is removed — with the jumper open, the indicator can be calibrated and configured. Setup mode parameters cannot be reached with the jumper in place.
2. Power the indicator up and press the key the book shows here once, momentarily, during the startup sequence. Only press it once — do not press and hold, and do not double press; the key press must end before start-up completes. SETUP displays.
3. Move to Config. config displays.
4. Move to Calibr. Calibr displays.
5. Open the calibration menu. wzero displays. Note: see the alternative zero modes if the job calls for a rezero, a last zero, or a temporary zero.
6. Enter setup mode with the CAL jumper removed, and connect the indicator to a communication port.
7. For a standard calibration, remove all weight from the scale — except hooks or chains needed to attach the weights.
8. Send SC.WZERO#1 to calibrate the zero point. Wait for the OK response.
9. Apply the span calibration weight to the scale.
10. Send SC.WVAL#1= followed by the exact value of the weight applied.
11. Send SC.WSPAN#1 to calibrate the span point.

14. Send KSAVEEXIT to save and return to weigh mode.
15. Return to weigh mode (the book's front-panel procedures finish by pressing the key shown three times). modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The standard calibration from the front panel — empty scale for zero, one test load for span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 420 Plus calibrates from the front panel, by EDP commands, or through Revolution, and every route runs the same order: zero, test weight value, span — with optional linearization points and a rezero for hooks and chains. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Place the indicator in setup mode so the display reads CONFIG.
2. Press the menu key the book shows here until the display reads CALIBR.
3. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, for the zero calibration.
4. At WZERO, calibrate the zero. The display shows *CAL* while calibration is in progress; when it completes, the A/D count for the zero calibration is displayed.
5. Do not adjust that zero value after WSPAN has been set — the book warns against it.
6. Save the zero calibration value and go to the next prompt, WVAL.
7. At WVAL, show the stored calibration weight and enter the actual value of the test weights you will use for the span calibration. Store the entered value and go to span calibration, WSPAN.
8. Place the test weights on the scale. At WSPAN, calibrate the span. The display shows *CAL* while it works; when it completes, the A/D count for the span calibration is displayed.
9. Save the span calibration value and go to the next prompt.
10. Press the key the book shows here until the display reads CONFIG, then press the key the book shows to exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: No button-pushing: the indicator takes calibration commands over its EDP port from a terminal or computer.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 420 Plus calibrates from the front panel, by EDP commands, or through Revolution, and every route runs the same order: zero, test weight value, span — with optional linearization points and a rezero for hooks and chains. 10. Send the KUPARROW EDP command to exit setup mode.

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: No button-pushing: the indicator takes SC commands over COM 1 from a terminal or computer.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 482-AG calibrates from its front panel, and it can also take SC commands over COM 1. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Press the configuration switch only with a non-conductive tool, reached in through the access hole in the back of the enclosure — that is this book's own instruction.
1. Remove the configuration switch access screw from the back of the enclosure.
2. Insert a non-conductive tool into the access hole and press the configuration switch. The display changes to CONFIG.
3. Press the key the book shows here until CALIBR is displayed.
4. Connect COM 1 to a terminal or computer. The commands below are the CALIBR EDP commands from Section 6.0.
5. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights need hooks or chains, place them on the scale for the zero.
6. Send SC.WZERO to calibrate zero. The display shows *CAL* while it works.
7. Place the test weights on the scale and send the test weight value with SC.WVAL, in the form WVAL=nnnnnn and Enter.
8. Send SC.WSPAN to calibrate span. The display shows *CAL* while it works.
9. To remove an offset: clear all weight from the scale, including anything used to hang the test weights, then send SC.REZERO. The display shows *CAL* while the zero and span values are adjusted.
10. Send KUPARROW to exit configuration mode.
11. Stop at the CALIBR menu, back out until the display reads CONFIG, then exit configuration mode — Saving is displayed and the scale returns to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 482-AG Livestock Digital Weight Indicator Technical Manual Doc 167281 — Front Panel Calibration (§4.1, printed p. 42), EDP Command Calibration (§4.2, printed p. 43), Adjusting Final Calibration (§4.3, printed p. 43). [PDF pp. 42-43]

modes.title: Fine-Tune the Span
modes.blurb: The scale proves a hair high or low in a strain test. Nudge WVAL and the book's own math corrects it — 1.5 lb per 1000 lb in the book's example.

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The standard calibration — empty scale for zero, one test load for span. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:

1. Place the indicator in setup mode so the display reads CONFIG.
2. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, for the zero calibration.
3. Scroll the menu until the display reads CALIBR.
4. At WZERO, press the key the book shows to calibrate zero. The indicator displays *CAL* while it works; when it finishes, the A/D count for zero is displayed.
5. Press the key the book shows again to save the zero calibration value. The display moves on to WVAL.
6. At WVAL, press the key the book shows to display the stored calibration weight value.
7. Enter the actual value of the test weights you will use: the editing keys pick the digit and raise or lower it, and move the decimal point when one is needed.
8. Press the key the book shows to store the WVAL value. The display advances to WSPAN.
9. Place the test weights on the scale. At WSPAN, press the key the book shows to calibrate span. The indicator displays *CAL* while it works; then the A/D count for the span is displayed.
10. Press the key the book shows to store the span calibration value. The display moves on to WLIN; linearization is optional from here.

modes.title: Gravity Compensation (set before you calibrate)

modes.title: New Zero? — Full Calibration
modes.blurb: A brand-new calibration: empty-scale zero plus one known calibration weight. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. This book gives five calibration selections at the Calibration Mode prompt — New Zero, Last Zero, Temp Zero, Only Zero and Cal Reset — plus a multi-point linearization variation when linearization is turned on in setup. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time. The book also prints earlier-version calibration methods; its own introduction says those are not valid on later software versions, so this page uses the later methods only.
1. From weigh mode, press 1 0 0, then SELECT, then 2 3 6 4 0, then ID, then ENTER. Make any needed parameter adjustments in P110 through P119 for scale 1, then press ZERO. Or, from Setup Mode, just press ZERO.
2. The unit prompts ENTER = CAL!. Press ENTER to proceed. Pressing CLR here lets you exit Setup Mode without calibrating.
3. If more than one scale is enabled, the unit prompts Keyin Scl #. Key in the scale number and press ENTER. Scales 2, 3 and 4 are set up in parameters 120 through 149.
4. The display shows New Zero?. Press SELECT to scroll through the five calibration selections, and press ENTER when the one you want is showing. Pressing CLR at any point in a calibration routine backs you up one step.
5. Press SELECT until the display shows New Zero?, then press ENTER.
6. The display shows the dead load now on the scale. Remove any extra load so the scale is truly empty, with nothing but the platform on it.
7. Press ENTER. A new zero is established; the display shows Adj'g Zero, then prompts Keyin CalWt.
8. Place the calibration weight on the platform.
9. Key in the weight's true value on the numeric keypad, then press ENTER. If an entry is wrong, CLR clears it before ENTER is pressed.
10. The unit performs the calibration and prompts CAL OK?. Check the accuracy with weight now, without leaving Calibration Mode.
11. If the calibration is accurate, press ENTER. If it is not, press CLR — the system returns to the New Zero? prompt so you can run it again.
12. Know this: if the calibration weight was less than 5 percent of capacity, or the calibration changed a lot, the unit prompts ReCal Req'd. The book recommends performing the re-calibration rather than overriding it with CLR.
13. At the CAL OK? prompt the accuracy can be checked by weight without leaving Calibration Mode: with the scale empty it should read zero, and a known weight should read exactly that weight. If it is accurate, press ENTER, then press ENTER again at the save prompt to save the new calibration, and ENTER once more at the exit prompt to return to weigh mode. This book's calibration chapter prints no seal or screw steps, so nothing needs putting back after calibration.
References: GSE Models 550/570 Programmable Weigh Indicators (PWI) Technical Reference Manual, Version 4.0 (Fourth Edition, September 1994), Part 39-10-28983 — Chapter 7 Calibration Mode: §7.2 Calibration Mode (printed pp. 87-90), §7.4 Multi-Point Linearization (printed pp. 91-92), §7.5 Quick Calibration (printed p. 92). [PDF pp. 108-113]

modes.title: Last Zero? — Recalibrate With the Weight Still On
modes.blurb: For a calibration check that came up out of tolerance with the test load still applied — tank weighing and large-capacity scales where removing the load is the hard part.

modes.text:

This book gives five calibration selections at the Calibration Mode prompt — New Zero, Last Zero, Temp Zero, Only Zero and Cal Reset — plus a multi-point linearization variation when linearization is turned on in setup. modes.title: New Zero Calibration
modes.blurb: The full calibration: a new zero with the scale empty, plus a span with a test weight. First-time calibration and complete re-calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. This book gives six calibration methods, plus multi-point linearization when it is turned on in setup. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time. Two ways in: Quick Cal from the weigh mode, or the configuration menu. Nothing is saved until you exit and press ENTER at the ENTER=SAVE prompt — if power is lost mid-calibration, the previously saved values come back. The book's calibration chapter prints no seal or screw caution, so none is read here.
1. From the weigh mode, key in 100, then press SELECT.
2. Key in the access code, 54321, then press ENTER. That is the Quick Cal route.
3. Or use the configuration menu instead: from the main menu press F5 Setup, then F4 Setup Menus, then F1 CAL, key in the access code — 23640 or 54321 by default — and press ENTER.
4. Press SELECT to step through the calibration methods, then press ENTER to begin the one you want. If more than one scale is enabled, the display first prompts Keyin Scl number: key in the scale number and press ENTER.
5. Remove all weight from the scale.
6. Get into calibration and select the New Zero method.
7. Press ENTER at the New Zero? prompt to establish the new zero reference.
8. The default calibration units show for a moment, then the Keyin CalWt prompt.
9. Apply the calibration weight, key in its true value in the default calibration units, and press ENTER to establish span.
10. If you keyed the value in before the weight was on, the display prompts Add CalWT instead. Add the calibration weight and press ENTER.
11. After span, CAL OK? shows if the calibration looks acceptable, or ReCal??? if the book suggests repeating it.
12. To accept, press ENTER at the CAL OK? prompt. To repeat instead, press CLR at the CAL OK? prompt and run it again.

To leave without saving, press CLR at the ENTER=SAVE prompt, then ENTER at the ENTER=UNDO prompt and ENTER at ENTER=EXIT — but know that undoing also undoes any unsaved changes you made to the setup parameters. modes.title: Full Zero and Span Calibration
modes.blurb: The 680's complete guided calibration — unlock, get in, teach zero, then span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale two honest answers. Zero: what nothing feels like. Span: what a known test weight feels like. The 680 requires both — a WZERO and a WSPAN — before it will trust the line between them. First you get in — then you teach.
CAUTION: In Legal for Trade applications the indicator is sealed to restrict access to the setup switch. Breaking the seal terminates the Legal for Trade status of the indicator until it is resealed and recertified.
1. Look on the bottom of the enclosure for a small access hole with a screw in it. That screw covers the setup switch.
2. Check for a state seal guarding that screw. A sealed screw means the scale is locked for legal trade, and the seal must be broken to get in.
3. Remove the setup switch screw.
4. Push a non-conductive tool into the hole, about three quarters of an inch (19 millimeters), until the setup switch clicks. Be gentle — too much force can damage the switch.
5. The display shows Config. You are in setup mode, where the legal parameters live.
6. Know this before you go further: an audit jumper (J24, on the CPU board) decides whether the switch is required at all. If it is ever found ON where regulations require the switch, that is a compliance problem, not a shortcut — leave it as the certifying agent set it.
7. Press the Down key twice. Calibr shows on the display.
8. Press Enter. wzero shows — you are at the zero teaching point.
9. Take every bit of weight off the scale. Nothing on it at all.
10. Press Enter to teach zero. ok shows when the zero is stored.
11. Move on to wval and open it. The stored test weight value shows.
12. Type the true value of your test weights on the keypad, then press Enter to accept. wSpan shows — the scale is ready for weight.
13. Put the test weights on the scale, centered and settled.
14. Press Enter to teach span. ok shows when the span is stored.
15. Press Enter to return to weigh mode. Span calibration is complete.
16. Prove it: take the weights off — the scale should read zero. Put a known weight back on — it should read exactly that weight.
17. Put the setup switch screw back, snug at 10 inch-pounds. Have the unit resealed before the scale returns to trade.
References: Rice Lake 680 Synergy Plus Technical Manual PN 192627 — setup switch and audit jumper (Section 4.1, p.34), Section 5.0 Calibration and 5.1.1 Span Calibration (p.54), alternative zeros (Section 5.2, p.55), EDP command calibration (Section 5.3, p.56).

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The full front-panel calibration: empty scale for zero, one known test weight for span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 680HE calibrates from the front panel or by EDP commands; it needs a WZERO and a WSPAN, and up to four linear points in between are optional. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Access the setup menu via the setup jumper (Section 4.1). Config displays.
2. Press the key the book shows here twice. Calibr displays.
3. Press the key the book shows here. wzero displays.
4. Ensure there is no weight on the scale.
5. Press the key the book shows here to perform a zero calibration. ok displays.
6. Press the key the book shows here. zrocnt displays.
7. Press the key the book shows here. wval displays.
8. Press the key the book shows here. The current test weight value displays.
9. Press the key the book shows here and use the numeric keypad to enter a new value, if necessary.
10. Press the key the book shows here to accept the value. wSpan displays.
11. Place the specified amount of test weight on the scale.
12. Press the key the book shows here to perform a span calibration. ok displays.

modes.title: EDP Zero and Span

modes.text:

modes.text:

modes.title: EDP Temporary Zero

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span

2. Navigate to the Configuration menu within the Setup menu. Configuration displays.

modes.title: EDP Last Zero, Then Span

modes.title: EDP Temporary Zero, Then Span
modes.blurb: For a non-empty scale such as a hopper: temporarily zero the displayed load, calibrate the span, and keep the original zero calibration.
modes.text:

The 682 can be calibrated from the front panel or with EDP commands; it requires a zero calibration and a span calibration, and linear calibration points between them are optional. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.

modes.title: EDP Rezero for Hooks or Chains
modes.blurb: After a span calibration where hooks or chains suspended the test weights: remove everything and take the rigging offset back out.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 682 can be calibrated from the front panel or with EDP commands; it requires a zero calibration and a span calibration, and linear calibration points between them are optional. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.

modes.title: Two-Point Calibration with Test Weights
modes.blurb: The full calibration: one point with the scale empty (or with the test weights on), the other point with the opposite. First-time hookups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 748 gives you two ways to do it — with test weights, or with the four "C" numbers you wrote down after a good calibration — and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION (the book's own words, printed at the head of SETUP AND CALIBRATION): The membrane keyboard is not to be operated with pointed objects — pencils, pens, fingernails, and so on. Damage to the keyboard from this practice will NOT be covered under warranty.
1. Find the calibration switch on the main printed circuit board. On a NEMA 4X enclosure, open the door on the enclosure. On a desktop enclosure, take the instrument off its gimbal mount — loosen the smaller locking screw first, then remove the two large knobs — and remove the top and bottom screws from the right end cap. The switch is on the printed circuit board near the center.
2. Set the calibration switch on the printed circuit board to the CAL position, then press and release it. (The book shows the follow-on keypresses as pictures; press the keys the book shows to move on to the prompts.)
3. At the CAL? prompt, press the key the book shows to display the current selection — YES or NO. Press 1 to proceed with calibration (0 bypasses calibration and moves on to the zero tracking range), then press the key the book shows to accept your selection.
4. The first calibration weight prompt, CAL 1=, shows. Press the key the book shows and the display shows 0 for no load. If this first point is zero — the empty scale — press the key again. If this first point is the test weights, key in the total value of the calibrated test weights, place the weights on the scale platform, and press the key. After a few seconds the display moves on.
5. The second calibration weight prompt, CAL 2=, shows. This point is the opposite of the first: if the first was zero, this one is the test weight total; if the first was the test weights, this one is zero. Press the key the book shows and the display shows 0. For zero, make certain the scale platform is empty and press the key again. For the test load, key in the total of the calibrated test weights, place the weights on the platform, and press the key. After a few seconds the display moves on.
6. At the C1= prompt, leave the C1 value unchanged — that prompt is for restoring an old calibration from recorded numbers, not for a fresh test-weight calibration — and press the key the book shows to move on.
7. When the calibration is in, set the calibration switch back from CAL to the OPR position (the board marks the two positions OPR and CAL), close up the enclosure or refit the end cap, and prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero, and a known weight put on should read exactly that weight.
References: Cardinal 748 Weight Indicating Instrument Technical/Operation Manual Doc 8539-M041-O1 Rev H (11/98) — CALIBRATION and SETUP AND CALIBRATION, calibration-switch access and the CAL? / CAL 1= / CAL 2= / C1= / StodL= prompts (printed pp. 13, 16) [PDF pp. 14, 17]; printed p. 13 [PDF p. 14] also carries the keyboard CAUTION and the 0 = no / 1 = yes legend; CALIBRATION OF THE ANALOG OUTPUT (printed pp. 41-42) [PDF pp. 42-43]; calibration switch and OPR/CAL board markings, figure no. 11 (printed p. 8) [PDF p. 9].

modes.title: Restore Calibration from the Recorded "C" Numbers
modes.blurb: No test weights hung: type back the four "C" numbers you recorded after a previous good calibration and the 748 returns to that calibration. Only when nothing that affects calibration has been changed.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 748 gives you two ways to do it — with test weights, or with the four "C" numbers you wrote down after a good calibration — and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION (the book's own words, printed at the head of SETUP AND CALIBRATION): The membrane keyboard is not to be operated with pointed objects — pencils, pens, fingernails, and so on. Damage to the keyboard from this practice will NOT be covered under warranty.
1. Find the calibration switch on the main printed circuit board. On a NEMA 4X enclosure, open the door on the enclosure. 4. Move through the calibration prompts (CAL? — press 1 to proceed) until the C1= prompt shows.
5. At C1=, press the key the book shows to display the current C1 value, then key in the C1 value you recorded. The book works with four "C" numbers — enter each recorded value at its prompt the same way.
6. Remove all weight from the scale. At the StodL= prompt (store deadload value), press the keys the book shows to display YES, then press the key shown to store the current scale weight as the deadload weight.
7. When the calibration is in, set the calibration switch back from CAL to the OPR position (the board marks the two positions OPR and CAL), close up the enclosure or refit the end cap, and prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero, and a known weight put on should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Analog Output Calibration (Optional I/O Board Only)
modes.blurb: Only if the optional I/O board is fitted: trim the 0-to-10-volt and 4-to-20-milliamp analog output. Not a scale calibration — the book says this output is calibrated at the factory and should need no other adjustment.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 748 gives you two ways to do it — with test weights, or with the four "C" numbers you wrote down after a good calibration — and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION (the book's own words, printed at the head of SETUP AND CALIBRATION): The membrane keyboard is not to be operated with pointed objects — pencils, pens, fingernails, and so on. Damage to the keyboard from this practice will NOT be covered under warranty.
1. Find the calibration switch on the main printed circuit board. On a NEMA 4X enclosure, open the door on the enclosure. On a desktop enclosure, take the instrument off its gimbal mount — loosen the smaller locking screw first, then remove the two large knobs — and remove the top and bottom screws from the right end cap. The switch is on the printed circuit board near the center.
2. Set the calibration switch on the printed circuit board to the CAL position, then press and release it. (The book shows the follow-on keypresses as pictures; press the keys the book shows to move on to the prompts.)
3. Be in Calibration mode (calibration switch at CAL). When the 748 senses the optional I/O board, the calibration sequence includes these steps. The display shows CALdAC.
4. Press the ENTER key and the display shows NO. Press the 1 key to change it to YES to proceed (ENTER at NO ends the analog output calibration, and the 0 key changes the display back to NO). Press ENTER.
5. The display shows bH 0= — the weight below zero for the analog output to be minimum, 0 volts or 4 milliamps. Press ENTER to display the setting. Press ENTER to store it, or enter the desired weight and press ENTER.
6. The display shows dAC H= — the maximum voltage to output at capacity. Press ENTER to display the setting. Press ENTER to store it, or enter the desired value, 00.000 to 10.000, and press ENTER.
7. The display shows dAC Hi. The voltage and current output are set to the value you entered. Adjust the VOLTAGE potentiometer on the I/O board to set the voltage; the SPAN potentiometer may also be used now to set the current output. When the adjustment is complete, press the ENTER key.
8. The display shows dAC Lo. The voltage output is set to 0 volts and the current output to 4 milliamps. Adjust the OFFSET potentiometer on the I/O board to set the voltage output to zero and/or the current output to 4 milliamps. On completion, press ENTER.
9. The 748 returns to the CALdAC step. The book warns there is interaction between the OFFSET and SPAN adjustments: answer YES and repeat the calibration until no further adjustment is necessary.
10. When the calibration is in, set the calibration switch back from CAL to the OPR position (the board marks the two positions OPR and CAL), close up the enclosure or refit the end cap, and prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero, and a known weight put on should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Standard Calibration
modes.blurb: The full calibration: total increments, increment size, decimal position, empty-scale zero, then one known test weight. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 8140 has two ways to do it — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Open the enclosure and make sure the calibrate enable jumper, W2 on the main PCB, is shorting its two pins. Without it, the setup mode cannot be accessed.
2. Press both the TARE and CLEAR keys, then release them at the same time to enter setup mode. On newer units the setup mode starts as soon as the W2 jumper is inserted.
3. Let the indicator warm up a minimum of 15 minutes before calibrating. The book says this warmup is required to stabilize the electronics and let the load cell warm up.
4. Three keys run the whole programming routine: ZERO goes back to the previous step, CLEAR accepts what is shown and jumps to the last step, S FILE, and PRINT accepts what is shown and moves to the next step.
5. Work through the programming steps until the display shows CAL. Press Print if calibration is required; pressing Clear skips calibration and goes to the last step, S FILE.
6. The display shows C1 with the number of total increments. Press Test if the number shown is the correct number of full scale increments. Press Tare if it is not — each press moves to the next choice: 1000, 2000, 2500, 3000, 4000, 5000, 6000, 8000, or 10,000 increments.
7. The display shows C2, increment size. Press Test if the size shown is correct. Press Tare to move to the next choice: times 1, times 2, or times 5.
8. The display shows C3, decimal position. Press Test if the decimal position is correct. Press Tare to move through the choices: 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1, and 10. The book warns that if the increments, increment size, and decimal position do not make a valid scale capacity, the program returns to step C1.
9. The display shows E SCL, empty scale. Remove all weight from the scale platform, then press Print to continue.
10. The display shows 10 SEC. Wait — there is a 10 second wait while the 8140 sets initial zero.
11. The display shows Add Ld, add load. Place the selected test weight on the scale platform, then press Print to continue. The book notes the test weight must be a minimum of 10 percent of full capacity on early PCBs; newer PCBs with jumper W5 have no minimum value.
12. Enter the value of the test weight used. Only whole numbers are accepted — no fractions or decimals. The blank digit on the left is entered first: press Tare to count that digit up until it is right, press Test to shift to the next position to the right, and press Print to enter the whole display as the test weight value. A blank digit is entered as a 0.
13. The display shows 10 SEC again. Wait while the span is adjusted.
14. The display shows E SCL, empty scale. Remove the test weights, then press Print to let the 8140 recheck zero.
15. Wait through the last 10 SEC while zero is rechecked. The display then shows CAL d, calibration done, for about three seconds.
16. When the display shows S FILE, press Test to save the programming in memory — the W2 jumper must be inserted to save the file, and the display stays at S FILE if it is not. When the display shows CAL OFF, remove the setup jumper W2 and place it on just one pin so it is not misplaced; the 8140 exits the setup routine. The book also requires the sealant included with each unit to be applied to the door gasket after calibration and before closing, so the enclosure stays watertight. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Mettler Toledo 8140 Technical Manual — Setup jumpers W2 calibrate enable (printed p. 8), key functions and programming procedure (printed pp. 11-20), Calibration Procedure (printed pp. 18-20), Span Adjustment (printed p. 21). [PDF pp. 13-14, 16-26]

modes.title: Span Adjustment
modes.blurb: A small span correction without repeating the entire calibration. The book offers it for large capacity scales, tank scales, and hopper scales where a build-up procedure is used. A standard calibration must already be done — it provides the reference point.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 8140 has two ways to do it — pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Open the enclosure and make sure the calibrate enable jumper, W2 on the main PCB, is shorting its two pins. Without it, the setup mode cannot be accessed.
2. Press both the TARE and CLEAR keys, then release them at the same time to enter setup mode. On newer units the setup mode starts as soon as the W2 jumper is inserted.
3. Let the indicator warm up a minimum of 15 minutes before calibrating. The book says this warmup is required to stabilize the electronics and let the load cell warm up.
4. Three keys run the whole programming routine: ZERO goes back to the previous step, CLEAR accepts what is shown and jumps to the last step, S FILE, and PRINT accepts what is shown and moves to the next step.
5. Apply known test weights to the scale. If an adjustment is required, continue.
6. Install the setup jumper W2, then press both the TARE and CLEAR keys and release them at the same time to enter setup mode. Newer units go into setup mode as soon as W2 is inserted.
7. When the display shows F0 0, press the TEST key. The display shows 00000.
8. Enter the correct test weight applied to the scale, the same way as in the standard calibration: press TARE to count the blanked digit up, press TEST to move the digit being changed to the next position to the right, until the correct weight value is displayed.
9. Press the PRINT key.
10. When the display shows CAL OFF, remove the setup jumper W2 and place it on only one pin of W2. The display should now show the weight value corresponding to the test weight applied to the scale. The book notes the adjustment is limited to plus or minus 50 percent of the original weight value shown after standard calibration.
11. When the display shows S FILE, press Test to save the programming in memory — the W2 jumper must be inserted to save the file, and the display stays at S FILE if it is not. When the display shows CAL OFF, remove the setup jumper W2 and place it on just one pin so it is not misplaced; the 8140 exits the setup routine. modes.title: Front Panel Calibration (Zero and Span)
modes.blurb: The everyday calibration from the panel. Empty scale for zero, one known test load for span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 820i calibrates from its front panel, by serial commands from a terminal, or with Revolution on a PC — each way teaches zero, a test-weight value, and span, with optional five-point linearization and rezero. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Place the indicator in setup mode — the display reads Scale Configuration — and remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, for the zero calibration.
2. With the SCALES menu highlighted, press the down key, then select the scale to be calibrated. Press down again, with the GRADS parameter highlighted, then press left to highlight the CALIBR submenu. Press down to go to zero calibration, WZERO.
3. Make sure the scale is empty. Press down again to show the current WZERO value, then press the Calibrate softkey to calibrate zero. When it finishes, the new A/D count for the zero calibration shows.
4. Press Enter to save the zero calibration value and go to the next prompt, WVAL.
5. With WVAL displayed, press down to show the stored calibration weight value. Use the numeric keypad to enter the actual value of your calibration test weights, then press Enter to save the value and go to span calibration, WSPAN.
6. Place the test weights on the scale. Press down again to show the current WSPAN value, then press the Calibrate softkey to calibrate span. When it finishes, the new A/D count for the span calibration shows.
7. Press Enter again to save the span calibration value. The display moves on to WLIN — linearization is optional from here.
8. Press up to return to the SCALES menu, or press the Save and Exit softkey to exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 820i Programmable HMI Indicator/Controller Technical Manual PN 93018 Rev D — Calibration (§4.0, p. 53), Gravity Compensation (§4.1, p. 53), Front Panel Calibration (§4.2, pp. 53-54), Serial Command Calibration (§4.3, p. 55), Revolution Calibration (§4.4, p. 55) [PDF pp. 53-55]

modes.title: Five-Point Linearization (WLIN)
modes.blurb: Added accuracy across the whole range. After a standard calibration, the scale is also taught at up to five points between zero and span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 820i calibrates from its front panel, by serial commands from a terminal, or with Revolution on a PC — each way teaches zero, a test-weight value, and span, with optional five-point linearization and rezero. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.

2. With the SCALES menu highlighted, press the down key, then select the scale to be calibrated. Press down again, with the GRADS parameter highlighted, then press left to highlight the CALIBR submenu. Press down to go to zero calibration, WZERO.
3. Start here from the WLIN prompt, right after the span is saved. Know this: if linearization values were entered before, they are reset to zero during calibration, so re-teaching is part of the job.
4. With WLIN displayed, press down to go to the first linearization point, POINT 1. Press down again to show the weight value prompt, WGT 1, then down once more to show the weight value.
5. Place test weights on the scale, then use the numeric keypad to enter the actual test weight value. Press Enter to save the value and move to the CAL 1 prompt.
6. Press down to show the current calibration value, then press the Calibrate softkey to calibrate the linearization point. When it finishes, the A/D count for the point shows.
7. Press Enter again to save the calibration value and move to the next point, POINT 2. Repeat for up to five linearization points.
8. To exit the linearization parameters, press up to return to WLIN.
9. Press up to return to the SCALES menu, or press the Save and Exit softkey to exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Rezero for Hooks or Chains
modes.blurb: The test weights hung from hooks or chains during calibration. Rezero removes that rigging offset afterward. Caution from the book: rezero cannot be used with five-point linear calibration.
modes.text:

3. If no apparatus was used to hang the test weights, there is nothing to rezero: remove the test weights and press up to return to the CALIBR submenu.
4. If hooks or chains were used during calibration, remove them and the test weights until all weight is off the scale.
5. Go to the REZERO parameter, then press down to show the current zero value. Press the Calibrate softkey to adjust the zero and span calibration values.
6. Press Enter or up to return to the CALIBR submenu.

modes.title: Serial Command Calibration
modes.blurb: No button-pushing at the panel: a terminal or PC sends SC commands over the serial port to teach zero, value, and span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 820i calibrates from its front panel, by serial commands from a terminal, or with Revolution on a PC — each way teaches zero, a test-weight value, and span, with optional five-point linearization and rezero. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Place the indicator in setup mode — the display reads Scale Configuration — and remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, for the zero calibration.
2. With the SCALES menu highlighted, press the down key, then select the scale to be calibrated. Press down again, with the GRADS parameter highlighted, then press left to highlight the CALIBR submenu. Press down to go to zero calibration, WZERO.
3. Connect the indicator serial port to a terminal or personal computer.
4. Place the indicator in setup mode — the display reads CONFIG — and remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
5. Send the SC.WZERO command, with your scale number, to calibrate zero.
6. Place the test weights on the scale and send the test weight value with the SC.WVAL command, in the form WVAL equals the value.
7. Send the SC.WSPAN command, with your scale number, to calibrate span.
8. Up to five linearization points can be calibrated between zero and span: send SC.WLIN with a point's test weight value to set it, then send SC.WLIN with that point's C entry to calibrate it. Repeat point by point.
9. To remove an offset value, clear all weight from the scale, including the hooks or chains used to hang the test weights, then send the SC.REZERO command.
10. Send the KSAVE serial command to save the calibration changes, or send KEXIT to exit setup mode.
11. Press up to return to the SCALES menu, or press the Save and Exit softkey to exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Gravity Compensation (set before you calibrate)
modes.blurb: The indicator was calibrated in one place and will work in another. Set latitude and elevation first; the book credits the difference into the calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 820i calibrates from its front panel, by serial commands from a terminal, or with Revolution on a PC — each way teaches zero, a test-weight value, and span, with optional five-point linearization and rezero. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Place the indicator in setup mode — the display reads Scale Configuration — and remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, for the zero calibration.
2. With the SCALES menu highlighted, press the down key, then select the scale to be calibrated. Press down again, with the GRADS parameter highlighted, then press left to highlight the CALIBR submenu. Press down to go to zero calibration, WZERO.
3. In the FEATURE menu, set the LOCALE parameter ON.
4. Set LATUDE, the latitude, and ELEVAT, the elevation in meters, for where the scale will work.
5. Do this before calibrating. Then run the standard front panel calibration.
6. Worth knowing: if the indicator is later installed at a different location, gravity compensation can be applied to the already-calibrated indicator just by adjusting the LATUDE and ELEVAT parameters — no new test weights required by this section.
7. Press up to return to the SCALES menu, or press the Save and Exit softkey to exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Calibrate the Scale — Zero and Test Weights
modes.blurb: The full calibration: the empty scale plus one to four known test weights, in order. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. On the 825 you walk it through a row of known weights — the empty scale plus up to four test weights — and it learns from each one. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Calibration can be locked by a hardware jumper inside the indicator — jumper J11, marked CAL INHIBIT, on the edge of the circuit board. When the word CAL shows in the lower right corner of the screen, calibration is allowed. When it does not show, calibration is not permitted, and on an indicator sealed with a lock-wire seal you cannot calibrate unless you break the lock-wire security seal to reach the jumper and remove it.
1. Turn the 825 on with the push-button power switch on the rear enclosure. The display does a short self-test and shows the Start-Up screen. Catch it before the application program auto-starts — the book says the countdown begins at 8 seconds.
2. On the Start-Up screen, press LEGAL METROLOGY INFORMATION / SETUP on the touchscreen. Or press the S key, or highlight the selection with the Right Arrow key and press ENTER.
3. On the Legal metrology information / Setup screen, select the Setup menu — press the S key, or press the Down Arrow to highlight Setup and press ENTER. The Login screen appears.
4. Enter your login, press the Down Arrow to move to the password, enter the password with the numeric keys, and press ENTER. The book prints the factory defaults as login ADMIN and password 81440. After logging in, the Setup Menu screen shows.
5. On the Setup Menu screen, select Calibration: press the Calibration menu option, or press the b key, or highlight Calibration and press ENTER. The Setup Scale Number screen shows.
6. On the Setup Scale Number screen, select the scale to calibrate — for example 1. Scale 1. The Scale 1 - Calibration Options screen shows.
7. Check for the word CAL in the lower right corner of the screen. If instead the screen says Calibration locked by hardware jumper inside enclosure, the J11 jumper is still on both pins — power down, lower the front panel, and remove the jumper (off, or on one pin) before calibrating. See the caution at the start.
8. Know how many points you are running before you start. The Num Cal Pts parameter (under 1. Parameters) sets how many calibration points there are on top of the zero weight — 1 to 4. With one point you will only see Weight 1 and Weight 2 prompts; more points add Weight 3, Weight 4 and Weight 5 prompts. One of the weights must be the zero, no-load weight.
9. On the Scale 1 - Calibration Options screen, press 2. Calibrate. Or press the 2 key, or highlight 2. Calibrate and press ENTER. The Scale 1 - Calibration Weight 1 screen shows.
10. Calibration Weight 1: if this is the zero weight, make sure there is no load on the scale, enter 0 on the numeric keys, and press ENTER. If it is a loaded weight instead, place the weight on the scale, enter the current weight on the scale, and press ENTER.
11. The display shows Calibrating with a bar graph running left to right. When that step finishes, the Calibration Weight 2 screen shows.
12. Calibration Weight 2: place the mid-point weight on the scale, enter the current weight on the scale, and press ENTER. Or, if this point is the zero weight, leave the scale empty, enter 0, and press ENTER.
13. The display shows Calibrating again. When it finishes, the Calibration Weight 3 screen shows — if your Num Cal Pts setting calls for it. If not, you go straight to the Scale 1 - Fine Span screen.
14. Calibration Weight 3: place the test, or load, weight on the scale, enter the current weight on the scale, and press ENTER. Or, if this point is the zero weight, leave the scale empty, enter 0, and press ENTER.
15. The display shows Calibrating. When it finishes, the Scale 1 - Fine Span screen shows.
16. If you set more points, the Weight 4 and Weight 5 screens work the same way: place that weight on the scale, enter its true value, and press ENTER.
17. When the last calibration weight is done, the display shows the Scale 1 - Fine Span screen. If you are not making a fine span adjustment, press the Q key (Quit) to save the current settings and quit. Then back out screen by screen with the Esc key or the Left Arrow key, through the Calibration Options screen and the Setup Menu, back to the Start-Up screen, and start the application program. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If you removed the J11 calibration jumper to get in, put it back on both pins when calibration must be locked again, and have the lock-wire seal restored — with the jumper on, the book says calibration is not permitted.
References: Cardinal 825 Desktop Installation & Technical Manual Doc 8545-1151-0M Rev B — Calibration Jumper J11 / CAL INHIBIT (printed p. 38) [PDF p. 46], To Begin Setup and Login (printed pp. 41-42) [PDF pp. 49-50], Getting Into Calibration (printed p. 66) [PDF p. 74], Num Cal Pts (printed p. 76) [PDF p. 84], Calibration Methods and Calibration Weights 1-3 (printed pp. 85-88) [PDF pp. 93-96], Calibration from the Setup Menu (printed pp. 89-92) [PDF pp. 97-100], Fine Span Adjustment (printed p. 94) [PDF p. 102], Fine Span Adjustment with 2nd Order Linearization (printed pp. 95-97) [PDF pp. 103-105].

9. Leave the Calibration Weight 3 test weight on the scale, or place a calibrated test weight on the scale.
10. On the Scale 1 - Fine Span screen, press the Coeff menu selection. Or press the C key, or highlight Coeff and press ENTER. The Coefficient screen shows.
11. The book warns, in its own words: WARNING! Changing the Linear Coefficient or the 2nd Order Coeff will affect the indicator's ability to display the proper weight. Please consult the factory before making any changes.
12. Linear Coefficient: this number is applied to the load cell signal to calculate weight. If the value shown is right, press the Down Arrow. If not, enter a new Linear Coefficient on the numeric keys and press the Down Arrow.
13. 2nd Order Coeff: this number is applied to the square of the load cell signal to calculate the weight. If the value shown is right, press the Down Arrow. If not, enter a new value and press the Down Arrow.
14. Tweak low weight: the low end of the weight range that needs adjusting. The book's example: if the scale reads 5 pounds low between 10,000 and 15,000 pounds, the tweak low weight is 10000. Enter it and press the Down Arrow.
15. Tweak high weight: the high end of that range — 15000 in the book's example. Enter it and press the Down Arrow.
16. Tweak weight: how much weight to add or take away across that range to bring the display into tolerance — 5 in the book's example. Enter it and press ENTER to save the settings and return to the Scale 1 - Fine Span screen.
17. When the last calibration weight is done, the display shows the Scale 1 - Fine Span screen. If you are not making a fine span adjustment, press the Q key (Quit) to save the current settings and quit. Then back out screen by screen with the Esc key or the Left Arrow key, through the Calibration Options screen and the Setup Menu, back to the Start-Up screen, and start the application program. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If you removed the J11 calibration jumper to get in, put it back on both pins when calibration must be locked again, and have the lock-wire seal restored — with the jumper on, the book says calibration is not permitted.
