modes.title: Front Panel Calibration (Zero and Span)
modes.blurb: The standard calibration. Empty scale for zero, one known test load for span. First-time and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 880 calibrates with a zero, a test weight value, and a span from the front panel — with five-point linearization, rezero, last zero, and temporary zero routes when the job calls for them. It can also be calibrated by EDP commands. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in configuration mode using the setup switch on the back of the unit. If the audit trail is enabled, the book also allows the key it shows here instead.
2. Navigate to CALIBR.
3. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, for the zero calibration.
4. Go to the WZERO parameter. You can view the previously captured A/D count for zero there.
5. Press Enter to calibrate WZERO. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while it works; when complete, WVAL is displayed.
6. With WVAL displayed, display the stored calibration weight value.
7. Edit the value to the true weight of the test weights you will use: select each digit, change it, confirm when the value is correct, and set the decimal point where it belongs. On the 880 Plus, the keypad can enter the value directly.
8. Store the WVAL value and advance to WSPAN.
9. Place test weights on the scale equal to WVAL, then press Enter to calibrate WSPAN. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while it works; when complete, WLIN is displayed. Linearization is optional from here.
10. When calibration is complete, press the key the book shows here to return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake 880 Performance Series Technical Manual Doc 158387 — Calibration (§4.0), Front Panel Calibration (§4.1), Five-point linearization (§4.1.1), Rezero (§4.1.2), LAST (§4.2), TEMP (§4.3), Adjusting Final Calibration (§4.4), Gravity Compensation (§4.5), EDP Command Calibration (§4.6) [PDF pp. 68-72]

modes.title: Five-Point Linearization (WLIN)
modes.blurb: Extra accuracy across the range: up to five added points between zero and span, taught right after the span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. 2. Navigate to CALIBR.
3. Finish the zero and span calibration first. Linearization begins at WLIN, and any linearization values entered before are reset to zero when WZERO is calibrated.
4. With WLIN displayed, go to POINT1, then go to WGT1, and display the value.
5. Edit the value to the true weight you will place for point 1. Every linearization point must be less than the span point.
6. Place the test weights on the scale, then press the key the book shows here to calibrate. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while it works; when complete, WGT1 is displayed again.
7. Go to POINT2 and repeat, for up to five points total.
8. To leave the linearization parameters, return to WLIN.
9. When calibration is complete, press the key the book shows here to return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Rezero for Hooks or Chains

modes.title: Last Zero (LAST)
modes.blurb: The test weights are already on the scale. Uses your last empty-scale pushbutton zero, so the weights never have to come off.

modes.title: Temporary Zero (TEMP)
modes.blurb: Tank scales: zero the load sitting on the scale, teach the span with added test weights, and keep the original zero.
modes.text:

modes.title: Adjusting Final Calibration (Trimming)
modes.blurb: A strain test shows the scale a hair high or low. Nudge WVAL by the book's own math to correct it.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 880 calibrates with a zero, a test weight value, and a span from the front panel — with five-point linearization, rezero, last zero, and temporary zero routes when the job calls for them. It can also be calibrated by EDP commands. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in configuration mode using the setup switch on the back of the unit. If the audit trail is enabled, the book also allows the key it shows here instead.
2. Navigate to CALIBR.
3. Prove the error with a strain test first. The book's example: a scale calibrated with 1000 lb reads 3 lb high at 2000 lb.
4. Work out the correction from that error: 3 lb high at 2000 lb is 1.5 lb per 1000 lb, so WVAL comes down to 998.5.
5. Edit the WVAL value to the corrected number and store it.
6. When calibration is complete, press the key the book shows here to return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Gravity Compensation (set before you calibrate)
modes.blurb: The indicator will work somewhere other than where it was calibrated. Set latitude and elevation first and the gravity difference is credited in.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 880 calibrates with a zero, a test weight value, and a span from the front panel — with five-point linearization, rezero, last zero, and temporary zero routes when the job calls for them. 2. Navigate to CALIBR.
3. In the FEATUR menu, set the LOCALE parameter to ON. Do this before calibrating.
4. Set LATUDE, the latitude, and ELEVAT, the elevation in meters relative to sea level, for where the scale will work.
5. Now run the normal front panel calibration.

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: No keypad work: calibration by commands over the COM, USBCOM, or Ethernet port from a terminal or computer.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 880 calibrates with a zero, a test weight value, and a span from the front panel — with five-point linearization, rezero, last zero, and temporary zero routes when the job calls for them. It can also be calibrated by EDP commands. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in configuration mode using the setup switch on the back of the unit. If the audit trail is enabled, the book also allows the key it shows here instead.
2. Navigate to CALIBR.
3. Connect the indicator COM, USBCOM, or Ethernet port to a terminal or personal computer, and put the indicator in configuration mode.
4. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
5. Send SC.LC.CD#1 to calibrate zero. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while it works. The indicator answers OK when a command works, and two question marks when it does not.
6. Place the test weights on the scale. Send the test weight value with SC.WVAL#1, in the form SC.WVAL#1 equals the value, then Enter.
7. Send SC.LC.CW#1 to calibrate span. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while it works.
8. For linearization points, set each point's test weight with SC.WLIN.V1#1 and calibrate it with SC.WLIN.C1#1, changing the point number for up to five points.
9. To remove an offset, clear all weight from the scale, including hooks or chains used to hang test weights, then send SC.REZERO#1. Send KMENU or KEXIT to return to weigh mode.
10. When calibration is complete, press the key the book shows here to return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Speed Sensor — Calculated
modes.blurb: Speed worked out from the book numbers: the sensor's pulses per revolution and the pulley diameter. No belt run needed.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. This one is a belt scale integrator: the book calibrates the speed sensor first, then the weigh frame — its zero, its span, and up to five linearization points. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From weigh mode, open the menu and go to Setup, then Calibration. Every calibration procedure in this book starts at Calibration within the Setup menu.
2. Know the order before you touch anything: the book requires the speed sensor calibration to be done before the weigh frame calibration.
3. Go to Speed Sensor. Pulse Input 1 displays.
4. Go to Speed Cal Type and choose CALCULATED.
5. Open Pulse Per Revolution and key in the sensor's pulses per revolution.
6. Open Sensor Diameter and key in the pulley diameter.
7. Go to Calibrate. Start To Begin displays.
8. Start it. Complete briefly flashes when the calibration takes.
9. Press the menu key to return to weigh mode when the procedure finishes. Prove it: run the empty belt and it should read zero; then run a known weight of material across the scale and the totalizer should register exactly that weight. If it does not, run the material test again before you hand the scale back.
References: Rice Lake 882D Belt Scale Integrator Technical Manual Doc 184260 (PN 184260 Rev L) — Calibration (Section 5.0, printed p. 46), Speed Sensor Calibration (Section 5.1, printed pp. 46-49: Calculated 5.1.1 p. 47, Revolutions 5.1.2 pp. 47-48, Distance 5.1.3 p. 49), Weigh Frame Calibration (Section 5.2, printed p. 50: Static Zero 5.2.1 p. 50, Dynamic Span 5.2.2 pp. 50-52, Dynamic Zero 5.2.3 pp. 52-53, Linearization 5.2.4 pp. 53-54 with Correction Factor 5.2.4.1 p. 54) [PDF pp. 46-54]

modes.title: Speed Sensor — Revolutions
modes.blurb: Speed from counting belt revolutions against marks you make. The belt length must be configured first — that is the book's own warning.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. This one is a belt scale integrator: the book calibrates the speed sensor first, then the weigh frame — its zero, its span, and up to five linearization points. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.

2. Know the order before you touch anything: the book requires the speed sensor calibration to be done before the weigh frame calibration.
3. Before you start: mark a reference point on the conveyor belt and one on the conveyor frame, and make sure the belt length is configured.
4. Go to Speed Sensor, then Pulse Input 1.
5. At Speed Cal Type, scroll to REVOLUTIONS.
6. Open Test Revolutions and key in the number of revolutions you expect to run. The book says more revolutions give better accuracy.
7. Go to Calibrate. Press Start To Begin displays.
8. Start it. The display shows the pulses counted, the run time, and Press Stop To Finish. If the pulses are not changing, the book says that points to a bad sensor or bad wiring.
9. Stop the calibration after the belt completes your revolutions.
10. Key in the number of revolutions actually completed. The 882D works out the pulses per unit it uses for belt speed and totalizing.
11. Press the menu key to return to weigh mode when the procedure finishes. Prove it: run the empty belt and it should read zero; then run a known weight of material across the scale and the totalizer should register exactly that weight. If it does not, run the material test again before you hand the scale back.

modes.title: Speed Sensor — Distance

modes.title: Static Zero (belt stopped)
modes.blurb: Zero with the belt stopped and empty. The quick zero, taken from a few seconds of readings.
modes.text:

modes.title: Dynamic Span — Test Weight or Chain
modes.blurb: The main span calibration, using static test weights or a test chain on the running belt.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. This one is a belt scale integrator: the book calibrates the speed sensor first, then the weigh frame — its zero, its span, and up to five linearization points. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.

4. From Weigh Frame, scroll to Dynamic, then Span.
5. Choose Test Weight, or scroll to Chain if you are using a test chain.
6. Open Test Weight Value — or Chain Weight — and key in the amount of test weight or chain you will use.
7. Load the scale with the weights or chains.
8. Go to Calibrate. Press Start to Begin displays. Make sure the belt is running before you start — that is the book's own instruction.
9. Start it. Calibrating displays, and the run lasts for the Test Distance set in configuration, twenty feet or meters by default.
10. At the end the 882D shows the previous error and the current error. Press ENTER to accept — ACCEPTED displays and the new span is stored. Or press the key the book shows here to reject it — REJECTED displays.
11. Press the menu key to return to weigh mode when the procedure finishes. Prove it: run the empty belt and it should read zero; then run a known weight of material across the scale and the totalizer should register exactly that weight. modes.title: Dynamic Span — Material
modes.blurb: Span from a known amount of real material, pre-weighed or post-weighed. The truest check of the whole conveyor.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. This one is a belt scale integrator: the book calibrates the speed sensor first, then the weigh frame — its zero, its span, and up to five linearization points. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From weigh mode, open the menu and go to Setup, then Calibration. Every calibration procedure in this book starts at Calibration within the Setup menu.
2. Know the order before you touch anything: the book requires the speed sensor calibration to be done before the weigh frame calibration.
3. Run a Dynamic Zero first — the book says the dynamic zero determines the span's reference point.
4. From Weigh Frame, scroll to Dynamic, then Span.
5. Scroll from Test Weight to Material. Material Weight displays.
6. Go to Calibrate. Press Start to Begin displays.
7. Start it. The 882D starts recording span averages — Calibrating and the run time display while the weight totalizes at ten-times resolution.
8. Once all the material has run across the belt scale, stop the sequence.
9. The 882D prompts for the amount of material in tons, starting from the previous value. Accept the default, or key in the true pre-weighed or post-weighed amount.
10. It shows the previous error and the current error. Press ENTER to accept — ACCEPTED displays and the new span is stored. Or press the key the book shows here to reject it — REJECTED displays. Pressing the cancel key before this point aborts the calibration.
11. Press the menu key to return to weigh mode when the procedure finishes. Prove it: run the empty belt and it should read zero; then run a known weight of material across the scale and the totalizer should register exactly that weight. If it does not, run the material test again before you hand the scale back.

modes.title: Dynamic Zero (belt running)
modes.blurb: Zero with the belt running and empty. Run this before any dynamic span — the span references it.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. This one is a belt scale integrator: the book calibrates the speed sensor first, then the weigh frame — its zero, its span, and up to five linearization points. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From weigh mode, open the menu and go to Setup, then Calibration. Every calibration procedure in this book starts at Calibration within the Setup menu.
2. Know the order before you touch anything: the book requires the speed sensor calibration to be done before the weigh frame calibration.
3. From Weigh Frame, scroll to Dynamic, then scroll past Span to Zero.
4. Make sure there is no load on the belt and the belt is moving.
5. Go through Zero Counts to Calibrate. Press Start to Begin displays.
6. Start it. If a calculated speed calibration was performed, the 882D prompts for a distance to calibrate over. It takes its zero averages over that distance — the cancel key stops it at any time.
7. At the end it shows the new zero error percent and the previous zero error percent.
8. Press ENTER to accept — Zero ACCEPTED flashes briefly and the new zero is stored. Or press the key the book shows here to reject it — REJECTED displays.
9. Press the menu key to return to weigh mode when the procedure finishes. Prove it: run the empty belt and it should read zero; then run a known weight of material across the scale and the totalizer should register exactly that weight. If it does not, run the material test again before you hand the scale back.

modes.title: Linearization (up to five points)
modes.blurb: Up to five correction points across the range, worked out from material tests, so mid-range rates read true too.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. This one is a belt scale integrator: the book calibrates the speed sensor first, then the weigh frame — its zero, its span, and up to five linearization points. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From weigh mode, open the menu and go to Setup, then Calibration. Every calibration procedure in this book starts at Calibration within the Setup menu.
2. Know the order before you touch anything: the book requires the speed sensor calibration to be done before the weigh frame calibration.
3. Have a zero and span calibration done first. A span calibration fills Point 1 at one hundred percent capacity with its correction factor; this page adds the extra points.
4. From Weigh Frame, scroll to Linearization. Point 1 displays.
5. Scroll to the point you want. Percent Capacity for that point displays.
6. Open it and key in the percent of maximum capacity for this point, if it needs changing.
7. Open Correction Factor and key in the factor for this point.
8. To work a factor out from a material test: divide the actual weight by the weight the totalizer showed, and multiply by the current correction factor. The book recommends at least three material tests per point, with their factors averaged.
9. Repeat for each additional point, up to five. When you exit to weigh mode, the 882D reorganizes the points from lowest to highest percent capacity.
10. Press the menu key to return to weigh mode when the procedure finishes. Prove it: run the empty belt and it should read zero; then run a known weight of material across the scale and the totalizer should register exactly that weight. If it does not, run the material test again before you hand the scale back.

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The standard calibration — empty-scale zero, test weight value, then span. The book requires zero and span to be calibrated together.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 882IS calibrates from the front panel — zero, a test weight value, then span, with five-point linearization and hook-and-chain rezero when the job calls for them. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode. If the audit trail is enabled, use the audit-trail entry the book shows instead.
2. Navigate to the Calibrate menu.
3. Go to the Zero Calibration parameter.
4. View the previously captured A/D count value for zero.
5. Remove all weight from the scale. If the test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
6. Press the key the book shows here to perform the zero calibration. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while it works; when it finishes, Test Weight displays.
7. With Test Weight displayed, show the stored calibration weight value.
8. Edit the value to the true value of your test weights: select each digit, change it up or down, and move the decimal point as needed. During calibration the Tare key acts as the Enter key — press Tare to accept the value.
9. Store the test weight value and advance to Span Calibration.
10. View the previously captured A/D count value for span.
11. Place calibration weights on the scale equal to the test weight value.
12. Press the key the book shows here to perform the span calibration. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while it works; when it finishes, Linear Calibration displays. Linearization is optional from here — skip it if the job does not call for it.
13. Press the key the book shows here when calibration is complete, to return to Weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

[PDF pp. 53-56]

modes.title: Five-Point Linearization
modes.blurb: After zero and span, teach up to five more points in between for a straighter line across the range. Optional — skip Linear Calibration entirely if the job does not need it.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 882IS calibrates from the front panel — zero, a test weight value, then span, with five-point linearization and hook-and-chain rezero when the job calls for them. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode. If the audit trail is enabled, use the audit-trail entry the book shows instead.
2. Navigate to the Calibrate menu.
3. Know this first: if linearization values were entered before, they are reset to zero during zero calibration, so re-teaching them is part of the job.
4. With Linear Calibration displayed, press the key the book shows here. Point-1 displays.
5. Press it again. Weigh Point 1 displays.
6. Show the value of the weigh point.
7. Edit the value to the true value of the test weight for this point, using the keypad on the 882IS Plus or the numeric entry method.
8. Confirm the value. Calibration Point 1 displays.
9. Place the test weights on the scale. The previously captured A/D counts for the point display.
10. Calibrate the point. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while it works; when it completes, Weight Point 1 displays.
11. Move to Point-1, then on to Point-2.
12. Repeat for up to five points. Every linearization point must be less than the span calibration point. To leave the linearization parameters, return to Linear Calibration.
13. Press the key the book shows here when calibration is complete, to return to Weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Rezero for Hooks or Chains
modes.blurb: The test weights hung from hooks or chains during calibration. Rezero takes the rigging's weight back out so zero tells the truth.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 882IS calibrates from the front panel — zero, a test weight value, then span, with five-point linearization and hook-and-chain rezero when the job calls for them. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode. If the audit trail is enabled, use the audit-trail entry the book shows instead.
2. Navigate to the Calibrate menu.
3. With Rezero displayed, access the rezero function.
4. Remove all weight from the scale, including all hooks and chains. The A/D count from the previous zero calibration displays.
5. With all weight removed, rezero the scale. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while the zero and span calibrations are adjusted.
6. Press the key the book shows here when calibration is complete, to return to Weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Last Zero
modes.blurb: The test weights are already on and you have a good empty-scale pushbutton zero. Last Zero swaps it in, so the weights stay put.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 882IS calibrates from the front panel — zero, a test weight value, then span, with five-point linearization and hook-and-chain rezero when the job calls for them. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode. If the audit trail is enabled, use the audit-trail entry the book shows instead.
2. Navigate to the Calibrate menu.
3. Know the requirement first: a pushbutton zero must have been taken in Weigh mode while the scale was empty.
4. Perform a normal calibration — but at the zero step, select Last Zero instead of Zero Calibration. The indicator uses that last pushbutton zero as the zero point.
5. Go on with the test weight value and the span calibration as usual. The test weight does not need to be removed from the scale.
6. Press the key the book shows here when calibration is complete, to return to Weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Temporary Zero
modes.blurb: Tank scales: calibrate the span with product already sitting in the tank, and keep the original zero afterwards.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 882IS calibrates from the front panel — zero, a test weight value, then span, with five-point linearization and hook-and-chain rezero when the job calls for them. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode. If the audit trail is enabled, use the audit-trail entry the book shows instead.
2. Navigate to the Calibrate menu.
3. Know what it assumes: the previously calibrated zero point is still accurate. This only rents a zero for the span calibration.
4. Perform a normal calibration — but select Temporary Zero instead of Zero Calibration, and calibrate the temporary zero with the load sitting on the scale.
5. Enter into Test Weight only the value of the test weights you add — not the product already loaded on the scale.
6. Perform the span calibration. When it is done, the original zero is retained.
7. Press the key the book shows here when calibration is complete, to return to Weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Fine-Tune the Span (Trimming)
modes.blurb: A strain test says the scale runs a little high or low. Correct it by trimming the test weight value — the book's own math.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 882IS calibrates from the front panel — zero, a test weight value, then span, with five-point linearization and hook-and-chain rezero when the job calls for them. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode. If the audit trail is enabled, use the audit-trail entry the book shows instead.
2. Navigate to the Calibrate menu.
3. Put a known strained load on and note how far off the scale reads. The book's example: calibrated at 1000 pounds, a strain test shows the scale 3 pounds high at 2000 pounds.
4. Work the same proportion back to the test weight value: 3 pounds over 2000 is 1.5 pounds per 1000, so the book lowers the test weight value from 1000 to 998.5.
5. Change the Test Weight value to the adjusted number, and calibrate the span again with the same test weights.
6. Press the key the book shows here when calibration is complete, to return to Weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Gravity Compensation (set before you calibrate)
modes.blurb: Calibrated in one place, working in another. Set latitude and elevation first and the book credits the difference into the calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 882IS calibrates from the front panel — zero, a test weight value, then span, with five-point linearization and hook-and-chain rezero when the job calls for them. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode. If the audit trail is enabled, use the audit-trail entry the book shows instead.
2. Navigate to the Calibrate menu.
3. In the Features menu, set the Gravity Compensation parameter to ON.
4. Set Latitude for where the scale will work, and Elevation in meters above sea level. Do this before calibrating.
5. Run the Front Panel Calibration.
6. If the indicator later works in a different place, adjusting Latitude and Elevation applies gravity compensation to the already-calibrated indicator — no new calibration needed for the move.
7. Press the key the book shows here when calibration is complete, to return to Weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: No button-pushing: the indicator takes SC commands from a terminal or computer over the port. It answers OK when a command works.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The 882IS calibrates from the front panel — zero, a test weight value, then span, with five-point linearization and hook-and-chain rezero when the job calls for them. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Put the indicator in setup mode. If the audit trail is enabled, use the audit-trail entry the book shows instead.
2. Navigate to the Calibrate menu.
3. Connect an indicator or I/O Module port to a terminal or personal computer.
4. Put the indicator in setup mode and remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights require hooks or chains, place them on the scale for the zero.
5. Send SC.WZERO number 1 to calibrate zero. Calibrating, Please Wait shows while it works.
6. Place the test weights on the scale, and send SC.WVAL number 1 equals the test weight value, followed by Enter.
7. Send SC.WSPAN number 1 to calibrate the span.
8. For linearization points, send SC.WLIN.V1 number 1 equals the point weight, then SC.WLIN.C1 number 1 to calibrate point 1. Repeat with V2 through V5 and C2 through C5, for up to five points.
9. For rezero, clear all weight from the scale, including the hooks and chains, then send SC.REZERO number 1.
10. Send KMENU or KEXIT to return to Weigh mode.
11. Press the key the book shows here when calibration is complete, to return to Weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

[PDF pp. 53-56]

modes.title: Full Zero and Span Calibration
modes.blurb: The 920i's complete guided calibration — unlock, get in, teach zero, then span.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale two honest answers. Zero: what nothing feels like. Span: what a known test weight feels like. Everything else gets read on the line between those two teachers. First you get in — then you teach.
CAUTION: This job can break the legal seal. Removing or altering the seal voids the NTEP approval, and calibration must be performed by a qualified technician familiar with state and local regulations. The unit must be resealed by an authorized agent when the work is done.
1. Find the fillister head screw on the enclosure. That screw is the cover for the configuration switch.
2. Check for a wire seal on that screw. A sealed screw means the scale is locked for legal trade, and the seal must be broken to get in.
3. Remove the screw. Press the configuration switch inside with a non-conductive tool. The main menu shows on the display.
4. Highlight SCALES and press Enter. A list of the scales set up in this indicator shows.
5. Choose the scale you are calibrating. Move through its menu until CALIBR shows, then open it.
6. Take every bit of weight off the scale. If your test weights hang from hooks or chains, put the hooks and chains on the scale now.
7. Go to WZERO and open it. Check one more time that the scale is truly empty.
8. Press the Calibrate softkey. Zero is now taught. The new A/D count shows on screen when it finishes.
9. Press Enter to save the zero. WVAL shows next.
10. Open WVAL and type the true value of your test weights on the keypad. Press Enter to save. WSPAN shows next.
11. Put the test weights on the scale, centered and settled.
12. Open WSPAN and press the Calibrate softkey. Span is now taught. The new A/D count shows when it finishes.
13. Press Enter to save the span. WLIN shows next — skip it unless you are adding linearization points.
14. If you hung the weights from hooks or chains, take everything off now, then run REZERO from this menu.
15. Press the Save and Exit softkey to leave setup mode.
16. Prove it: take the weights off — the scale should read zero. Put a known weight back on — it should read exactly that weight.
17. Put the switch access screw back. Have the unit resealed by an authorized agent before the scale returns to trade.
References: Rice Lake 920i Technical Manual PN 67887 Rev N — configuration switch and seal (Section 4.3, p.34), front panel configuration (Section 4.4, p.35), Section 5.0 Calibration (p.64), calibration steps (p.65), linearization (Section 5.2.1, p.66).

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The standard calibration. Empty scale for zero, one known test load for span. First-time and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The CW-90 checkweigher calibrates from its front panel CALIBR menu: an empty-scale zero, one test weight for the span, and, when the job calls for it, up to five extra points in between and a rezero step for weights hung from hooks or chains. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Press the MENU key, then navigate to CALIBR.
2. Move to the WZERO parameter.
3. Press the key the book shows to view the A/D count. Make sure the scale is empty. If the test weights will hang from hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, empty, for the zero.
4. Press ENTER to calibrate WZERO. CALIBRATING, PLEASE WAIT displays. When it is done, WVAL displays.
5. Show the stored calibration weight, then enter the true value of the test weights you will use and press ENTER to store it. WSPAN displays.
6. Place test weights on the scale equal to the WVAL value.
7. Press ENTER to calibrate WSPAN. CALIBRATING, PLEASE WAIT displays. When it is complete, WLIN displays.
8. Leave the calibration menu with the keys the book shows and return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake CW-90/90X Checkweigher Firmware Version 1.10 Technical Manual Doc 105942 Rev J — Calibration (§4.0), Front Panel Calibration (§4.1), Five-Point Linearization (§4.1.1), Rezero (§4.1.2), EDP Command Calibration (§4.2), Adjusting Final Calibration (§4.3.1) [PDF pp. 52-56]

modes.title: Five-Point Linearization (WLIN)
modes.blurb: Optional accuracy across the range: up to five extra points between zero and span. The book requires the points to sit below the span point, and starting a fresh calibration resets any old ones.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The CW-90 checkweigher calibrates from its front panel CALIBR menu: an empty-scale zero, one test weight for the span, and, when the job calls for it, up to five extra points in between and a rezero step for weights hung from hooks or chains. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Press the MENU key, then navigate to CALIBR.
2. Finish the zero and span calibration first. Linearization begins at the WLIN prompt.
3. With WLIN displayed, press the key the book shows to go to the first point, PT-> 1.
4. Place test weights on the scale. This point must be below the span point.
5. Enter the actual test weight value, then press the key the book shows to calibrate. CALIBRATING, PLEASE WAIT displays. When it is complete, the A/D count for that point displays and WLIN displays again.
6. Press the key the book shows to advance to PT-> 2 and repeat. You can do up to five points.
7. To leave the linearization points, press the key the book shows to return to WLIN.
8. Leave the calibration menu with the keys the book shows and return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Rezero for Hooks or Chains
modes.blurb: Only when the test weights hung from hooks or chains. After the zero and span calibration, REZERO backs the rigging weight out so zero tells the truth.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The CW-90 checkweigher calibrates from its front panel CALIBR menu: an empty-scale zero, one test weight for the span, and, when the job calls for it, up to five extra points in between and a rezero step for weights hung from hooks or chains. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Press the MENU key, then navigate to CALIBR.
2. Use this only if hooks or chains hung the test weights. If no apparatus was used, take the test weights off and return to the CALIBR menu without rezeroing.
3. With REZERO displayed, press the key the book shows to open the rezero function.
4. Remove the hooks or chains and all test weights from the scale, then press the key the book shows until REZERO displays.
5. With all weight removed, press the key the book shows to rezero the scale. CALIBRATING, PLEASE WAIT displays; this adjusts the zero and span values. The adjusted A/D count for the zero calibration displays when it is done.
6. Leave the calibration menu with the keys the book shows and return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: Calibrate over the EDP port from a terminal or computer: zero, span, up to five linear points, and rezero, all with SC commands.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The CW-90 checkweigher calibrates from its front panel CALIBR menu: an empty-scale zero, one test weight for the span, and, when the job calls for it, up to five extra points in between and a rezero step for weights hung from hooks or chains. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Press the MENU key, then navigate to CALIBR.
2. Connect the indicator EDP port to a terminal or personal computer. The EDP port pin assignments are in Section 2.8.
3. Place the indicator in configuration mode so the display reads CONFIG, and remove all weight from the scale platform. If the test weights require hooks or chains, place them on the scale for the zero calibration.
4. Send the SC.WZERO command to calibrate zero. The indicator displays CALIBRATING, PLEASE WAIT while it works.
5. Place the test weights on the scale and send the test weight value with the SC.WVAL command in the form SC.WVAL=nnnnnn followed by a carriage return.
6. Send the SC.WSPAN command to calibrate span. The indicator displays CALIBRATING, PLEASE WAIT.
7. For linearization points, set a point's test weight with the SC.WLIN.V1 command, then calibrate it with the SC.WLIN.C1 command. Repeat with the SC.WLIN.Vx and SC.WLIN.Cx commands for up to five points.
8. To remove an offset value, clear all weight from the scale, including any hooks or chains, then send the SC.REZERO command. The zero and span calibrations are adjusted.
9. Send the SC.KUPARROW or SC.KEXIT command to return to normal mode.
10. Leave the calibration menu with the keys the book shows and return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Adjust Final Calibration (fine-tune)
modes.blurb: The scale proves a hair high or low in a strain test. Nudge WVAL; the book's example corrects 3 lb high at 2000 lb by setting WVAL to 998.5.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The CW-90 checkweigher calibrates from its front panel CALIBR menu: an empty-scale zero, one test weight for the span, and, when the job calls for it, up to five extra points in between and a rezero step for weights hung from hooks or chains. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Press the MENU key, then navigate to CALIBR.
2. Return to the WVAL prompt and press the key the book shows to display the test weight value.
3. Adjust the value up or down to move the calibration. The book's example: calibrated with 1000 lb, a strain test at 2000 lb reading 3 lb high is corrected by setting WVAL to 998.5, a linear correction of 1.5 lb per 1000 lb.
4. Press the key the book shows to save the value, then press the key the book shows to return to the CALIBR menu.
5. Leave the calibration menu with the keys the book shows and return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake CW-90/90X Checkweigher Firmware Version 1.10 Technical Manual Doc 105942 Rev J — Calibration (§4.0), Front Panel Calibration (§4.1), Five-Point Linearization (§4.1.1), Rezero (§4.1.2), EDP Command Calibration (§4.2), Adjusting Final Calibration (§4.3.1) [PDF pp. 52-56]

modes.title: Span Adjustment — Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The book's one calibration: find the zero point empty, then set the span with a calibrated weight of about the scale's total capacity. Use it after install, after service, or when the monthly check weight no longer reads right.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The DC-200/300 is a high-precision counting scale, and the book calls this job Span Adjustment: set the zero point with the platform empty, then set the span with a calibrated test weight of about the total capacity of the scale. Pick the mode below and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Make sure the scale is turned off. Then press the span switch to reset it. Figure 2-4 in the book shows where the span switch is.
2. Turn the scale back on. The scale displays the message CHANGE SPAN SWITCH.
3. While pressing the REZERO key, enter 8715 from the numeric keypad to enter the calibration mode.
4. The scale display confirms that you are in the Calibration Mode.
5. Press the REPRINT key to enter the zero setting mode.
6. Choose which scale platform you are calibrating. The scale defaults to platform A. To choose another platform, press the SCALE key until the platform you want is displayed.
7. Make sure nothing is on the scale platform, and press the CODE key to have the scale automatically search for the zero point.
8. The scale displays the zero point in the quantity window. It should be a value between 9000 and 11000. If the scale does not catch that range, the book says to call your local DIGI dealer, or call 1-715-736-0002 for service assistance.
9. Press the REZERO key to clear the Internal Count shown in the weight window.
10. Press the REPRINT key to enter the weight calibration setting.
11. Put a calibrated weight on the platform equal to the total capacity of the scale — for example, a 25 pound weight on a 25 pound scale. Or enter the weight from the numeric keypad instead. The weight appears in the quantity window.
12. Press the REPRINT key to save the calibration data. The display confirms the span settings are being saved, and the screen returns to CHANGE SPAN SWITCH.
13. Turn the span switch off — the scale automatically returns to operation mode. Then power the scale off and restart it so the new settings take effect. Prove it the way the book says: put your test weight back on the platform and verify the scale reads that weight; the book has you record that reading and check the scale against it every month or so.
References: Rice Lake DC-200/300 Counting Scale Service Manual Doc 77159 — Calibration (Span Adjustment), Section 2.7. [PDF pp. 16-18]

modes.title: Zero and Span Calibration
modes.blurb: The full calibration: set the zero reference with an empty scale, then set the span with a known test weight. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The E1010 calibrates from its front panel, inside the Service menu's CAL submenu: set the zero reference with an empty scale, set the span with a known test weight, and — if the scale needs to read straighter between those points — add linear points. I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: The indicator must be unsealed to perform calibration. The book says the indicator is unsealed when Jumper JP1 is on; it is sealed with Jumper JP1 removed. Jumper JP1 must be in place to unseal the indicator. Press the ESC key anytime to abort the calibration.
1. Before you start: the indicator must be unsealed to perform calibration. It is unsealed when Jumper JP1 is on — it is sealed with Jumper JP1 removed, and Jumper JP1 must be in place to unseal the indicator.
2. Press and hold the ESC key for 3 to 5 seconds. PASS_ is displayed.
3. Key in the Service menu password, 0101, and press ENTER. You must key in the password within 10 seconds or the display returns to normal operation mode. CAL is displayed.
4. Press the PRINT key. ZERO is displayed.
5. With ZERO displayed, press the PRINT key. Use this item to set the zero reference for the indicator and scale. Live weight is shown.
6. Remove all weight from the scale.
7. Press the ENTER key to perform the zero procedure. BUSY is briefly displayed, then the live weight, which should be 0.
8. Press the ENTER key to save and return to the ZERO menu item. ZERO is displayed.
9. Press the UNITS key. SPAN is displayed. Use this item to set the span for the indicator and scale.
10. Press the PRINT key. The current capacity is displayed.
11. Key in a new span weight value and press ENTER — when you start to key in the span weight, the old value is replaced by the new one — or just press ENTER to accept the current span weight value. The live weight is displayed.
12. Place the correct span weight on the scale and press ENTER when the weight is stable. BUSY is briefly displayed, then the weight.
13. Press the ENTER key to accept the calibration and return to the SPAN menu item. SPAN is displayed.
14. Press ESC to return to normal weighing mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. Remember the seal: the book says this indicator is unsealed only while Jumper JP1 is on, and it is sealed with Jumper JP1 removed.
References: Avery Weigh-Tronix Model E1010 Indicator Service Manual Doc AWT35-500132 Issue B — Accessing the Menus (printed p. 9), Service Menu CAL submenu ZERO (printed p. 13), SPAN and LINEAR (printed p. 14) [PDF pp. 12, 16-17]

modes.title: Linearization — Extra Calibration Points
modes.blurb: Adds extra calibration points between zero and span, so the scale reads straighter across its whole range. The book stores 2 to 5 calibration points and says linear points must be done in order, points 2 through 4, with increasing weight.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The E1010 calibrates from its front panel, inside the Service menu's CAL submenu: set the zero reference with an empty scale, set the span with a known test weight, and — if the scale needs to read straighter between those points — add linear points. I will read it one step at a time.

1. Before you start: the indicator must be unsealed to perform calibration. It is unsealed when Jumper JP1 is on — it is sealed with Jumper JP1 removed, and Jumper JP1 must be in place to unseal the indicator.
2. Press and hold the ESC key for 3 to 5 seconds. PASS_ is displayed.
3. Key in the Service menu password, 0101, and press ENTER. You must key in the password within 10 seconds or the display returns to normal operation mode. CAL is displayed.
4. Press the PRINT key. ZERO is displayed.
5. With SPAN displayed, press the UNITS key. LINEAR is displayed. Use this item to set extra calibration points.
6. Press the PRINT key. 2 is displayed. This represents cal point 2.
7. Press the PRINT key to set this calibration point. A numeric value is displayed.
8. Key in a weight value for this calibration point and press the ENTER key. The live weight on the scale is displayed.
9. Place the test weight for this calibration on the scale and press ENTER. Busy is briefly displayed, and then 2.
10. Press the UNITS key to move to the next calibration point. 3 is displayed.
11. The book says linear points must be done in order — points 2 through 4 — with increasing weight, so repeat the same key-in, place-the-weight, and ENTER capture for each remaining point. Honest flag: the pages of this manual in front of me stop right here, at point 3's display, so the exact finishing presses for the later points are UNCONFIRMED — the pattern above is the book's own for point 2, and the order rule is the book's own note on the same page.
12. Press ESC to return to normal weighing mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. Remember the seal: the book says this indicator is unsealed only while Jumper JP1 is on, and it is sealed with Jumper JP1 removed.

modes.title: Calibration Using a Weight
modes.blurb: The standard calibration: zero the empty pan, then weigh one known calibration weight. The book calls for it when the balance is first used, after it has been moved, when the ambient environment has changed, and for regular calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is how you teach this balance to weigh honestly. This book covers the A&D EK-i and EW-i compact balances. It gives two routes at the balance itself: calibrate with a real weight, or correct for local gravity when no weight can be prepared. It also gives check-mode calibration procedures to finish a job after a maintenance load cell or a main board is replaced. On models with the CAL prohibition set, the book cancels the prohibition before calibrating (Section 4.4) and sets it again afterward (Section 4.6). Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Warm up the balance for at least half an hour with nothing on the pan before you calibrate with a weight (the book's first instruction).
2. Slide down the calibration switch cover to reach the CAL switch.
3. With nothing on the pan, press and hold the calibration (CAL) switch until CAL appears on the display, then release the switch.
4. To change the calibration weight value, press the SAMPLE key: the display shows the calibration weight value in grams stored in the balance. SAMPLE selects the blinking digit to change, RE-ZERO sets the value of the digit selected, PRINT stores the value and returns, and MODE cancels the value and returns. The value you set is stored in memory even after the power is switched off. To use the value already in memory, skip this step.
5. With nothing on the pan, press the PRINT key to weigh the zero-point value. Do not touch the pan during weighing.
6. Place the calibration weight with the same value as displayed on the pan.
7. Press the PRINT key to weigh it. Do not touch the pan during weighing.
8. When the end display appears, remove the weight from the pan, and press the CAL switch or the MODE key to return to the weighing mode.
9. Take the calibration weight off the pan and press the CAL switch or the MODE key to return to the weighing mode — that is how the book ends the weight calibration. Prove it: with the pan empty the balance should read zero, and a known weight should read exactly its value. The book prints no seal or screw step for calibration; the CAL switch sits under a slide-down cover.
References: A&D EK-i/EW-i Series Compact Balances Maintenance Manual Doc WT+PD4000657A — Calibration mode (Section 4), Calibration using a weight (Section 4.1), Gravity acceleration correction (Section 4.2), CAL prohibition models (Sections 4.3-4.6), Setting for replacing the maintenance load cell (Section 6.1.2), Calibration after replacing the main board (Section 6.2.4). [PDF pp. 9-12, 19, 21]

modes.title: Gravity Acceleration Correction
modes.blurb: Use this when the balance has been moved and a calibration weight cannot be prepared: you tell the balance the gravity acceleration value of the area where it will be used instead. The book's note: this correction is not required when the balance is calibrated using a calibration weight at the place where the balance is to be used.
modes.text:

modes.title: Calibration for a Maintenance Load Cell
modes.blurb: After fitting a maintenance load cell and inputting its characteristic revised data (Section 6.1.1), this check-mode calibration finishes the job.
modes.text:

3. Enter the check mode (the book's flow chart: hold the ZERO and CAL keys, then press the ON/OFF key).
4. Display CAL of the function setting group. Press the PRINT key to enter the calibration mode. LC 0 is displayed.
5. Press and hold the ZERO key about 1 second: LC 1 will be displayed. Then press the PRINT key to set LC 1.
6. After End 0 is displayed and three preliminary weighings, press the PRINT key with nothing on the weighing pan. After it has stabilized, the data is input.
7. A weighing value is displayed. Place the calibration weight of the same value as displayed — the book warns that if there is no calibration weight of the same value, it is impossible to change the amount — and press the PRINT key to input the data.
8. End will be displayed. The calibration is finished.

modes.blurb: After replacing the main board or E2PROM — initialize it and set the functions and adjustment data first (Sections 6.2.1 to 6.2.3) — this check-mode calibration is the book's finishing step.

modes.title: Capture Zero
modes.blurb: Reset the empty-scale zero on its own, without touching the span. Analog load cells only.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. On the IND560 the calibration softkeys live on the Calibration screen under the Scale branch: Capture Zero, Capture Span, Step Calibration, and CalFREE — all for analog load cells. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: This book ties calibration access to the metrology security switch, SW1-1. If an approval (USA, OIML, Canada, or Australia) is configured and SW1-1 is ON, the Scale branch will not open in setup. If an approval is selected but SW1-1 is not ON, the terminal will not let you leave setup and shows the message Switch UNSECURED. Setting SW1-1 to ON without selecting an approval does not secure the scale until an approval is selected in setup.
1. Enter setup and open the Scale branch, then open Calibration. If the Scale branch will not expand, the metrology switch SW1-1 is in the approved position — see the caution above.
2. On the Calibration screen, set the Calibration Units. If the terminal was moved to a new region, enter the Geo Code for this location — geo codes are numbered 0 to 31.
3. If you plan to use extra span points, set Linearity Adjustment here: Disabled uses only zero and one span point; 3 point adds a midpoint and highpoint; 4 point adds lowpoint, midpoint, and highpoint; 5 point adds lowpoint, midpoint, mid-highpoint, and highpoint.
4. Empty the scale.
5. Press the CAPTURE ZERO softkey. A status message directs you to empty the scale and press the START softkey.
6. Press the START softkey. The status of the capture zero operation displays.
7. When the operation is complete, a final status message verifies the capture zero operation is done.
8. Know this: if motion is present during the zero capture, the terminal averages the weight readings and then displays an error message saying dynamic weight values were used. That message must be acknowledged to save the dynamic values.
9. Press the EXIT softkey to return to the Calibration screen, then leave setup back to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If an approval is configured, make sure SW1-1 is set back to ON so the scale is secured — the book warns the terminal cannot leave setup with an approval selected and the switch unsecured.
References: Mettler Toledo IND560 Terminal Technical Manual Doc 71209394 — Scale branch and metrology switch SW1-1 (printed pp. 3-7 to 3-8), Calibration screen, Geo Code, Linearity Adjustment and Analog Gain Jumper (printed pp. 3-9 to 3-10), Capture Zero (printed p. 3-10), Capture Span (printed p. 3-11), Step Calibration (printed pp. 3-11 to 3-12), CalFREE (printed pp. 3-12 to 3-13). [PDF pp. 73-79]

modes.title: Capture Span
modes.blurb: Teach the span with known test weights, independent of capturing zero. With Linearity Adjustment enabled, this same sequence captures the extra midpoint and high points. Analog load cells only.
modes.text:

Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.

If an approval (USA, OIML, Canada, or Australia) is configured and SW1-1 is ON, the Scale branch will not open in setup. If an approval is selected but SW1-1 is not ON, the terminal will not let you leave setup and shows the message Switch UNSECURED. Setting SW1-1 to ON without selecting an approval does not secure the scale until an approval is selected in setup.
1. Enter setup and open the Scale branch, then open Calibration. If the Scale branch will not expand, the metrology switch SW1-1 is in the approved position — see the caution above.
2. On the Calibration screen, set the Calibration Units. If the terminal was moved to a new region, enter the Geo Code for this location — geo codes are numbered 0 to 31.
3. If you plan to use extra span points, set Linearity Adjustment here: Disabled uses only zero and one span point; 3 point adds a midpoint and highpoint; 4 point adds lowpoint, midpoint, and highpoint; 5 point adds lowpoint, midpoint, mid-highpoint, and highpoint.

5. Press the CAPTURE SPAN softkey. The Capture Span setup screen displays.
6. Enter the weight for test load 1 — and all other test loads if linearity has been enabled — then press the ENTER key.
7. Place test load weight 1 on the scale.
8. Press the START softkey. The status of the weight capture displays; when complete, a status message verifies the weight capture. To abort instead, press the ESCAPE softkey to return to the previous screen.
9. If 2, 3, or 4 test load steps are enabled, the terminal prompts for the next calibration weight; otherwise it shows a successful or failed calibration sequence.
10. Repeat placing each test load and pressing START for test loads 2, 3, and 4 if enabled.
11. Read the result: Capture Span OK means it worked. Calibration Failure means repeat the capture span procedure; if it continues to fail, the book says to contact a local METTLER TOLEDO representative.

modes.title: Step Calibration
modes.blurb: Build-up calibration for tanks and hoppers: the same amount of test weight is added at each step, then substitute material fills to the target. Analog load cells only.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. On the IND560 the calibration softkeys live on the Calibration screen under the Scale branch: Capture Zero, Capture Span, Step Calibration, and CalFREE — all for analog load cells. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: This book ties calibration access to the metrology security switch, SW1-1. If an approval (USA, OIML, Canada, or Australia) is configured and SW1-1 is ON, the Scale branch will not open in setup. If an approval is selected but SW1-1 is not ON, the terminal will not let you leave setup and shows the message Switch UNSECURED. Setting SW1-1 to ON without selecting an approval does not secure the scale until an approval is selected in setup.
1. Enter setup and open the Scale branch, then open Calibration. If the Scale branch will not expand, the metrology switch SW1-1 is in the approved position — see the caution above.
2. On the Calibration screen, set the Calibration Units. If the terminal was moved to a new region, enter the Geo Code for this location — geo codes are numbered 0 to 31.
3. If you plan to use extra span points, set Linearity Adjustment here: Disabled uses only zero and one span point; 3 point adds a midpoint and highpoint; 4 point adds lowpoint, midpoint, and highpoint; 5 point adds lowpoint, midpoint, mid-highpoint, and highpoint.
4. Press the STEP CALIBRATION softkey. The Step Calibration setup screen displays.
5. Enter the target weight for the test load. The same amount of test load weight is used in each step.
6. Press the START softkey. The Step Calibration screen shows a live weight display, the target weight you entered, and the next step prompt: Add test weight.
7. Add test weight to the tank or hopper as prompted. The active display shows the weight as you add it.
8. When the full amount of test weight has been added, press the OK softkey. The display shows Capturing span while the test load is captured and span factors are saved, then prompts: Remove test weight then fill to target.
9. Remove the test weight. The active display returns to zero.
10. Fill the tank or hopper with a substitute material up to the target weight.
11. Press the OK softkey. The target weight recalculates to the substitute material weight plus the initial intended target weight, and the display prompts Add test weight again.
12. Add test weight to the tank or hopper, then press the OK softkey. If the actual weight does not equal the target, a new span factor calculates, the display shows Capturing span, and the active weight display changes to match the target weight.
13. Remove the test weight. The active display returns to the weight shown for the last test load.
14. Repeat the fill-and-add steps until an appropriate number of calibration steps have been completed for this application.
15. Press the EXIT softkey at any step to stop the step calibration and return to the Calibration screen.
16. Press the EXIT softkey to return to the Calibration screen, then leave setup back to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If an approval is configured, make sure SW1-1 is set back to ON so the scale is secured — the book warns the terminal cannot leave setup with an approval selected and the switch unsecured.
References: Mettler Toledo IND560 Terminal Technical Manual Doc 71209394 — Scale branch and metrology switch SW1-1 (printed pp. 3-7 to 3-8), Calibration screen, Geo Code, Linearity Adjustment and Analog Gain Jumper (printed pp. 3-9 to 3-10), Capture Zero (printed p. 3-10), Capture Span (printed p. 3-11), Step Calibration (printed pp. 3-11 to 3-12), CalFREE (printed pp. 3-12 to 3-13). [PDF pp. 73-79]

modes.title: CalFREE — Span Without Test Weights
modes.blurb: Precalibrate the span from the load cells' own numbers — total cell capacity and rated output — with no test weights hung. The zero still has to be captured the normal way afterward. Analog load cells only.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. On the IND560 the calibration softkeys live on the Calibration screen under the Scale branch: Capture Zero, Capture Span, Step Calibration, and CalFREE — all for analog load cells. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: This book ties calibration access to the metrology security switch, SW1-1. If an approval (USA, OIML, Canada, or Australia) is configured and SW1-1 is ON, the Scale branch will not open in setup. If an approval is selected but SW1-1 is not ON, the terminal will not let you leave setup and shows the message Switch UNSECURED. Setting SW1-1 to ON without selecting an approval does not secure the scale until an approval is selected in setup.
1. Enter setup and open the Scale branch, then open Calibration. If the Scale branch will not expand, the metrology switch SW1-1 is in the approved position — see the caution above.
2. On the Calibration screen, set the Calibration Units. If the terminal was moved to a new region, enter the Geo Code for this location — geo codes are numbered 0 to 31.
3. If you plan to use extra span points, set Linearity Adjustment here: Disabled uses only zero and one span point; 3 point adds a midpoint and highpoint; 4 point adds lowpoint, midpoint, and highpoint; 5 point adds lowpoint, midpoint, mid-highpoint, and highpoint.
4. Check the Analog Gain Jumper setting on the Calibration screen first: it must indicate the actual jumper position on the Main board — 2 mv/V means the jumper is installed on both pins; 3 mv/V means the jumper is removed — or CalFREE will not operate properly. The terminal ships in the 3 mv/V setting.
5. Press the CALFREE softkey. The CalFREE screen displays.
6. Enter the total load cell capacity. The book's example: a tank with three 5000 kg cells is 3 times 5000, or 15000 kg. If multiple load cells are used, enter the average output of all cells as the rated output.
7. Enter an estimated preload value if you know it. It is optional: the terminal only uses it to test for A/D converter input saturation at full scale capacity, and it is not used as a zero reference point. If the preload is unknown, leave the field blank.
8. Press the OK softkey. The span is calculated from the values you entered.
9. Read the result: Calibration OK means it worked. Calibration Failure means repeat the CalFREE procedure; if it continues to fail, the book says to contact a local METTLER TOLEDO representative.
10. Press the ESCAPE softkey to return to the Calibration screen.
11. Know the limit: CalFREE sets the span only. The zero reference point must still be captured using the normal zero calibration procedure — run Capture Zero on the empty scale.
12. Press the EXIT softkey to return to the Calibration screen, then leave setup back to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If an approval is configured, make sure SW1-1 is set back to ON so the scale is secured — the book warns the terminal cannot leave setup with an approval selected and the switch unsecured.
References: Mettler Toledo IND560 Terminal Technical Manual Doc 71209394 — Scale branch and metrology switch SW1-1 (printed pp. 3-7 to 3-8), Calibration screen, Geo Code, Linearity Adjustment and Analog Gain Jumper (printed pp. 3-9 to 3-10), Capture Zero (printed p. 3-10), Capture Span (printed p. 3-11), Step Calibration (printed pp. 3-11 to 3-12), CalFREE (printed pp. 3-12 to 3-13). [PDF pp. 73-79]

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The everyday calibration at the indicator: empty scale for zero, one known test weight for span. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ 210 calibrates from its front panel — empty scale for zero, a known test weight for span — or by EDP commands from a terminal. Pick the way that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Remove the large fillister head screw on the enclosure backplate. Insert a screwdriver into the access hole and press the setup switch to enter setup mode. The display reads CONFIG.
2. Know your two navigation buttons in setup mode: UNITS is the RIGHT button — it scrolls right on the same menu level. ZERO is the ENTER button — it moves down a level and selects values.
3. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for zero calibration.
4. Press the RIGHT button (UNITS) until the display reads CALIBR, then press ENTER (ZERO) to go to zero calibration, WZERO.
5. With WZERO displayed, press ENTER to calibrate zero. The indicator displays CAL while calibration is in progress. When complete, the A/D count for the zero calibration is displayed. Press ENTER again to save the zero calibration value and return to the WZERO prompt, then press RIGHT to go to the WVAL prompt.
6. With WVAL displayed, press ENTER to show the test weight value. If the value equals the test weight you are using, press ENTER again to save it. If it is wrong, edit it: press RIGHT to select the flashing digit, press ENTER (ZERO) to change that digit, and press RIGHT to move to the next digit; when done press ENTER to save. Then press RIGHT to go to WSPAN.
7. If the primary unit is LB/OZ, enter the WVAL value in ounces — for a 5 pound test weight, enter 80.
8. Place the test weights on the scale. With WSPAN displayed, press ENTER to calibrate span. The indicator displays CAL while calibration is in progress. When complete, the A/D count for the span calibration is displayed. Press ENTER again to save the span calibration value.
9. If no hooks or chains were used to hang the test weights, remove the test weights and press RIGHT to return to the CALIBR menu.
10. Press the setup switch to exit setup mode (from EDP, send KEXIT instead), then replace the setup switch access screw. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake IQ Plus 210 Installation Manual PN 64640 Rev D — setup switch and CONFIG display (§3.0, printed p. 16), front panel menu navigation (§3.1.3, printed p. 17), Calibration Menu parameters (§3.2.3, printed p. 22), Front Panel Calibration (§4.1, printed pp. 25-26), EDP Command Calibration (§4.2, printed p. 26). [PDF pp. 16-17, 22, 25-26]

modes.title: Rezero for Hooks or Chains
modes.blurb: Use after a zero and span calibration when hooks or chains hung the test weights, to take the rigging's offset back out. The book says use this only after WZERO and WSPAN have been set.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ 210 calibrates from its front panel — empty scale for zero, a known test weight for span — or by EDP commands from a terminal. Pick the way that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Remove the large fillister head screw on the enclosure backplate. Insert a screwdriver into the access hole and press the setup switch to enter setup mode. The display reads CONFIG.
2. Know your two navigation buttons in setup mode: UNITS is the RIGHT button — it scrolls right on the same menu level. ZERO is the ENTER button — it moves down a level and selects values.
3. Finish the zero and span calibration first, with the hooks or chains on the scale for the zero calibration.
4. Remove the hooks or chains and the test weights, so all weight is off the scale.
5. At the REZERO prompt, press ENTER to rezero the scale. This adjusts the zero and span calibration values; the indicator displays CAL while the adjustment runs.
6. When complete, the adjusted A/D count for the zero calibration is displayed. Press ENTER again to save the rezero value, then press RIGHT to return to the CALIBR menu.
7. Press the setup switch to exit setup mode (from EDP, send KEXIT instead), then replace the setup switch access screw. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: Calibrate from a terminal or personal computer connected to the indicator's EDP port, sending commands instead of pressing buttons.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ 210 calibrates from its front panel — empty scale for zero, a known test weight for span — or by EDP commands from a terminal. Pick the way that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Remove the large fillister head screw on the enclosure backplate. Insert a screwdriver into the access hole and press the setup switch to enter setup mode. The display reads CONFIG.
2. Know your two navigation buttons in setup mode: UNITS is the RIGHT button — it scrolls right on the same menu level. ZERO is the ENTER button — it moves down a level and selects values.
3. Connect the indicator EDP port to the terminal or personal computer.
4. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale for zero calibration.
5. Send the WZERO EDP command to calibrate zero. The indicator displays CAL while calibration is in progress.
6. Send the WVAL command to enter the test weight value, in the format WVAL=nnnnnn, followed by a carriage return.
7. Place test weights on the scale equal to the WVAL value you sent.
8. Send the WSPAN EDP command to calibrate span. The indicator displays CAL while calibration is in progress.
9. To remove an offset value, clear all weight from the scale, including any hooks or chains used to hang the test weights, then send the REZERO EDP command.
