modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span Calibration
modes.blurb: The everyday calibration: empty scale for zero, certified test weights for span. First-time and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ plus 310A calibrates from its front panel — empty scale for zero, certified test weights for span — or by EDP commands over the serial port. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Set the Operate/Setup Switch on the rear panel to the SETUP position.
2. Press the PRINT key to scroll right until CALIBRT is displayed.
3. Using the down arrow (GROSS/NET) key, scroll down once to display ZERO. If ZERO is not displayed, scroll right until ZERO is displayed.
4. Clear the platform of all weight. If your calibration requires hooks or chains to hang the test weights, calibrate the zero with the chains or hooks on the scale.
5. Press TARE (Enter). The message *CALIB* is displayed — the indicator is calibrating zero weight (deadload).
6. When zero calibration is finished, SPAN is displayed, ready to calibrate the span weight.
7. Press the down arrow (GROSS/NET) key once. The number displayed is the full-scale capacity value (GRADS times DSP DIV). Place certified test weights on the scale. If the test weights equal full-scale capacity, skip the next step.
8. If the test weight is less than full-scale capacity, adjust the displayed number to match the test weight value, using the panel keys as described in Section 3.2. Enter the value exactly as it will appear with the decimal point programmed in the DEC PNT parameter — for example, calibrating a 100.00 lb by 0.01 lb scale with a 50-lb test weight, enter 50.00.
9. Press TARE (Enter). *CALIB* is displayed while the span is calibrated. If the number stays and *CALIB* does not appear, the span value entered is outside the scale capacity set by the first four parameters of the SETUP menu.
10. After span calibration finishes, TW SPAN (Tweak Span) is displayed. If an extremely fine adjustment of span is not required, press PRINT and move on — the fine-tuning route is its own mode here.
11. RE-ZERO is used mainly when hooks or a chain hung the test weights: clear the platform of all weight, including the chains or hooks. While the indicator is prompting RE-ZERO, press TARE (Enter). *CALIB* appears; do not disturb the platform until the re-zero is finished.
12. Return the Operate/Setup Switch to the OPERATE position and install the switch cover and legal seal according to Section 4.3 of the book. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake IQ plus 310A Installation Manual Doc 22979 — Calibrating Zero and Span (§4.1, printed p. 25), Fine-Tuning (Tweaking) Span and Re-Zero (§4.2) and Installing the Legal-for-Trade Seal (§4.3) (printed p. 26), EDP Calibration Commands (§6.2, printed p. 29). [PDF pp. 27-28, 31]

modes.title: Fine-Tuning (Tweaking) Span and Re-Zero
modes.blurb: The last fine nudge after a span calibration: adjust the test-weight value with an extra decade of resolution, then re-zero with the hooks and weights off.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ plus 310A calibrates from its front panel — empty scale for zero, certified test weights for span — or by EDP commands over the serial port. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Set the Operate/Setup Switch on the rear panel to the SETUP position.
2. Press the PRINT key to scroll right until CALIBRT is displayed.
3. While TW SPAN is displayed, press the down arrow (GROSS/NET) key. The number displayed is the test weight with an extra decade of resolution — no decimal point or dummy zeros are shown.
4. Press the up (ZERO) and down arrow (GROSS/NET) keys to make a fine adjustment to this test weight. If you press and hold either key, the value increments by 0.1 grad intervals.
5. Press TARE to store the result. RE-ZERO is displayed. RE-ZERO removes the offset of test-weight hooks and re-centers the zero band.
6. Remove all test weights and hooks from the scale.
7. Press TARE. *CALIB* appears. Do not disturb the platform until it is finished.
8. Return the Operate/Setup Switch to the OPERATE position and install the switch cover and legal seal according to Section 4.3 of the book. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake IQ plus 310A Installation Manual Doc 22979 — Calibrating Zero and Span (§4.1, printed p. 25), Fine-Tuning (Tweaking) Span and Re-Zero (§4.2) and Installing the Legal-for-Trade Seal (§4.3) (printed p. 26), EDP Calibration Commands (§6.2, printed p. 29). [PDF pp. 27-28, 31]

modes.title: EDP Command Calibration
modes.blurb: Calibrate over the EDP serial port with a connected terminal or computer, using the book's two-letter commands. Valid only in SETUP mode; the indicator displays CALIB while it works and returns OK when a calibration is completed.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ plus 310A calibrates from its front panel — empty scale for zero, certified test weights for span — or by EDP commands over the serial port. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Set the Operate/Setup Switch on the rear panel to the SETUP position.
2. Press the PRINT key to scroll right until CALIBRT is displayed.
3. Set the Operate/Setup Switch to SETUP and connect the sending device to the EDP port.
4. Clear the platform of all weight — with hooks or chains on the scale if they will hang the test weights — then send CD to calibrate deadload (zero).
5. Place the test weights on the scale. If the test weight equals full-scale capacity, send CW. If it does not, send CW followed by the numerical value of the test weight, then a carriage return — see Section 4.1 for entering test-weight values.
6. To re-zero, clear all weight from the scale including the hooks or chains, then send CZ. See Section 4.2.
7. Know this: serial input and keyboard commands are ignored until the calibration in progress is completed.
8. Return the Operate/Setup Switch to the OPERATE position and install the switch cover and legal seal according to Section 4.3 of the book. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake IQ plus 310A Installation Manual Doc 22979 — Calibrating Zero and Span (§4.1, printed p. 25), Fine-Tuning (Tweaking) Span and Re-Zero (§4.2) and Installing the Legal-for-Trade Seal (§4.3) (printed p. 26), EDP Calibration Commands (§6.2, printed p. 29). [PDF pp. 27-28, 31]

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The standard calibration — empty scale for zero, one test load for span. First-time and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ plus 355 is calibrated from its front panel with a zero, a test weight value, and a span, right in the CALIBR menu. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Place the indicator in setup mode — the display reads CONFIG.
2. Remove all weight from the scale platform. If your test weights require hooks or chains, place the hooks or chains on the scale now, for the zero calibration.
3. Scroll until the display reads CALIBR, then move down to WZERO.
4. With WZERO displayed, calibrate zero. The indicator displays *CAL* while calibration is in progress; when complete, the A/D count for the zero calibration is displayed.
5. Do not adjust this value after WSPAN has been set. Save the zero calibration value and move to the next prompt, WVAL.
6. With WVAL displayed, place the test weights on the scale and show the test weight value. Enter the actual test weight, then save the value and move to span calibration, WSPAN.
7. With WSPAN displayed, calibrate span. The indicator displays *CAL* while calibration is in progress; when complete, the A/D count for the span calibration is displayed.
8. Save the span calibration value and move to the next prompt, REZERO.
9. Scroll until the display reads CONFIG, then exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Fine-Tune the Span
modes.blurb: The scale proves a hair high or low in a strain test. Nudge WVAL and the book's own math corrects it — 1.5 pounds per 1000 in the book's example.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ plus 355 is calibrated from its front panel with a zero, a test weight value, and a span, right in the CALIBR menu. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Place the indicator in setup mode — the display reads CONFIG.

3. Scroll until the display reads CALIBR, then move down to WZERO.
4. Return to the WVAL prompt and show the test weight value.
5. Adjust the calibration up or down. The book's example: calibrated with 1000 pounds, a strain test shows 2000 pounds reading 3 pounds high, so WVAL is tweaked to 998.5 — a linear correction of 1.5 pounds per 1000.
6. Save the value and return to the CALIBR menu.
7. Scroll until the display reads CONFIG, then exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.text:

modes.title: Front Panel Zero and Span
modes.blurb: The full front panel calibration: an empty scale teaches the zero constant, one known test weight teaches the span constant, channel by channel.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ plus 800/810 keeps its calibration numbers in the CALIBRT menu and works them from the front panel — one channel at a time, up to four. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Before you start calibrating with test weights, turn off AC power to all equipment controlled by setpoints or their associated digital outputs. Continuous setpoints set at or below your test weights may trip while you load and unload the scale during the calibration procedure.
1. Power the indicator up and let it warm up for approximately 15 minutes before beginning calibration.
2. Slide the setup switch on the CPU board to the setup position — the display reads CONFIG.
3. Press SETPOINT until the display reads CALIBRT.
4. Know your keys in this menu: TIME/DATE moves down a level, DISP TARE moves up a level, and SETPOINT or CLEAR moves between W ZERO, W VAL and W SPAN.
5. Press TIME/DATE to show CHAN 1 — work with the channel you are calibrating, one through four.
6. Press TIME/DATE again to show WEIGHT, then again to show W ZERO. If W VAL or W SPAN appears instead, press SETPOINT or CLEAR until the display reads W ZERO.
7. Remove all load from the scale and allow time for the scale to settle.
8. Press TIME/DATE to display the current default value. Press ENTER and wait until a value reappears on the display. That number is the W ZERO calibration constant for this channel — write it down. Repeat a few times to verify the results come out similar each time.
9. Press DISP TARE to show W ZERO, then press CLEAR to display W VAL.
10. Press TIME/DATE to display the current default value. Enter the true test weight value and press ENTER. Write that down as the W VAL value for this channel.
11. Press DISP TARE to show W VAL, then press CLEAR to show W SPAN.
12. Press TIME/DATE to display the current default value. Place the test weight on the scale and allow time for it to settle. Press ENTER and wait until a value reappears — that is the W SPAN calibration constant. Repeat to verify the results are similar, write it down, then remove the test weight.
13. If the indicator has more scale channels, press DISP TARE back to the channel selection level and run these same steps for each channel.
14. Press DISP TARE to step back out of the calibration menu — from channel selection, one more DISP TARE exits calibration, and DISP TARE locks in the calibration settings. Then slide the setup switch on the CPU board back to the run position to exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If this is a legal-for-trade scale, the book says the case is closed with a legal seal once the scale is configured, calibrated and inspected — so have it sealed properly before it goes back into trade.
References: Rice Lake IQ plus 800/810 Digital Weight Indicators Installation Manual Doc 42100 — Calibration Menu (Table 3-10, printed p. 37), Calibration (§4.0, printed p. 38), Front Panel Calibration (§4.1, printed pp. 38-39), EDP Command Calibration (§4.2, printed p. 40), Adjusting Final Calibration (§4.4, printed p. 40); legal seal (§5.1, printed p. 41) [PDF pp. 43-47]

8. Follow the same W ZERO, W VAL and W SPAN prompts as the front panel calibration: clear scale at W ZERO, enter the test weight at W VAL, weights on at W SPAN.
9. When calibration is complete, send the KUPARROW command to exit the calibration menu.
10. Slide the setup switch to the run, normal mode, position.
11. Press DISP TARE to step back out of the calibration menu — from channel selection, one more DISP TARE exits calibration, and DISP TARE locks in the calibration settings. Then slide the setup switch on the CPU board back to the run position to exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If this is a legal-for-trade scale, the book says the case is closed with a legal seal once the scale is configured, calibrated and inspected — so have it sealed properly before it goes back into trade.

modes.title: Fine-Tune the Span (Adjust W VAL)
modes.blurb: Calibrated at one weight but a strain test proves it a hair high or low at another. Nudging W VAL gives a linear correction.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The IQ plus 800/810 keeps its calibration numbers in the CALIBRT menu and works them from the front panel — one channel at a time, up to four. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Before you start calibrating with test weights, turn off AC power to all equipment controlled by setpoints or their associated digital outputs. Continuous setpoints set at or below your test weights may trip while you load and unload the scale during the calibration procedure.
1. Power the indicator up and let it warm up for approximately 15 minutes before beginning calibration.
2. Slide the setup switch on the CPU board to the setup position — the display reads CONFIG.
3. Press SETPOINT until the display reads CALIBRT.
4. Know your keys in this menu: TIME/DATE moves down a level, DISP TARE moves up a level, and SETPOINT or CLEAR moves between W ZERO, W VAL and W SPAN.
5. Return to the W VAL prompt in the CALIBRT menu.
6. Press TIME/DATE to show the test weight value.
7. Enter the adjusted value, then press ENTER to save it. The book's example: a scale calibrated with 1000 lb reads 3 lb high at 2000 lb in a strain test, so W VAL is tweaked to 998.5 — a linear correction of 1.5 lb per 1000 lb.
8. Press the DISP TARE key to return to the CALIBRT menu.
9. Press DISP TARE to step back out of the calibration menu — from channel selection, one more DISP TARE exits calibration, and DISP TARE locks in the calibration settings. Then slide the setup switch on the CPU board back to the run position to exit setup mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight. If this is a legal-for-trade scale, the book says the case is closed with a legal seal once the scale is configured, calibrated and inspected — so have it sealed properly before it goes back into trade.

modes.title: Theoretical Calibration
modes.blurb: No test weights. The scale is taught from the load cells' own capacity and sensitivity values already entered for the cells.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The iQUBE2 is calibrated from the connected 920i front panel in this chapter — pick the calibration type that fits the cells and the job, and I will read it one step at a time. No minimum test weight is required, but the book recommends at least 10% of scale capacity. Do not mix calibration types (section, corner, 2-point); span adjustments must be made in the appropriate calibration type.
1. Verify that the iQUBE2 is connected to the 920i with power applied.
2. Use the 920i setup switch to make sure the indicator is in configuration mode.
3. Make sure the configuration has been downloaded from the 920i to the iQUBE2 before calibrating.
4. Leave the iQUBE2 SW1 switch alone — the book says it should remain in the OFF position.
5. On the 920i, navigate to the CALIB menu for the scale you are calibrating.
6. Make sure the scale is empty and navigate to the Theoretical Calibration parameter.
7. Press the Calibrate softkey.
8. The dead load value is captured, and the cells are trimmed based on the capacity and sensitivity values entered for the cells. Scale capacity is set at the total of the load cell capacities.
9. Press the Save and Exit softkey to return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake iQUBE2 Digital Diagnostic Junction Box Installation Manual PN 106113 Rev M — 920i Calibration (§4.2, printed p. 65), CALIB Menu Parameters (Table 4-7, printed p. 66), Front Panel Calibration (§4.2.1, printed p. 67), Advanced Calibration Options (§4.2.2, printed p. 68). [PDF pp. 67-70]

modes.title: 2-Point Calibration

modes.text:

7. Press ENTER or DOWN to go to the WZERO submenu.
8. Make sure there is no weight on the scale, then press the Calibrate softkey to calibrate WZERO.
9. Press ENTER to accept the value and move to the next prompt, WVAL.
10. With WVAL displayed, press ENTER or DOWN to view the stored test weight value. Use the numeric keypad to enter the desired value.
11. Press ENTER to advance to WSPAN.
12. With WSPAN displayed, press ENTER or DOWN to view the A/D count. Place test weights on the scale equal to WVAL, then press the CALIBRATION softkey to calibrate WSPAN.

modes.title: Cal-Match Calibration (Corner or Section)
modes.blurb: For multi-cell scales. CORNER places the weight over each load cell; SECTION places it over load-cell pairs. The iQUBE2 works out the trim factors from those readings.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The iQUBE2 is calibrated from the connected 920i front panel in this chapter — pick the calibration type that fits the cells and the job, and I will read it one step at a time. No minimum test weight is required, but the book recommends at least 10% of scale capacity. 1. Verify that the iQUBE2 is connected to the 920i with power applied.

4. Leave the iQUBE2 SW1 switch alone — the book says it should remain in the OFF position.
5. On the 920i, navigate to the CALIB menu for the scale you are calibrating.
6. Navigate to the CALIB sub-menu. Select which calibration type to use: CORNER or SECTION.
7. Press ENTER or UP to go to the WVAL menu.
8. Press ENTER or DOWN to view the stored test weight value. Use the numeric keypad to enter the desired value, then press ENTER to accept the value and advance to Cal-Match.
9. Make sure all weight is removed from the scale and press the Calibrate softkey to begin the calibration. The Cal-Match calibration can be canceled by pressing the CLEAR key or the CANCEL softkey.
10. Know the book's warning before you go on: Cal-Match will overwrite any previous calibration. The Cal-Match can be discarded and revert to the previous calibration by cycling power to the iQUBE2 before pressing Save and Exit.
11. After initializing, Cal-Match Point 1 is displayed. Place a test weight over the first cell or section to be tested, then press ENTER.
12. Once the iQUBE2 has read the cell, Cal-Match Point 2 is displayed on the 920i.
13. Move the test weight to the next cell or section and press ENTER. Repeat until all cells have been measured.
14. When the last cell has been measured, the iQUBE2 automatically sets the load cell trim factors. Press TWEAK or ENTER to view trim values.
15. Press UP to return to the SCALES menu.
16. Press the Save and Exit softkey to return to weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Five-Point Linearization
modes.blurb: Optional, after a basic calibration. Up to five extra taught points between zero and span, for non-linear scale systems.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The iQUBE2 is calibrated from the connected 920i front panel in this chapter — pick the calibration type that fits the cells and the job, and I will read it one step at a time. 6. Finish a basic calibration first. If linearization values were entered before, know this: they are reset to zero during the zero calibration.
7. With WLIN displayed, press ENTER or DOWN to go to the first linearization point (PT-> 1).
8. Place test weights on the scale and press ENTER twice to display the weight value entry prompt.
9. Enter the actual test weight value using the numeric keypad. Press ENTER to accept the value.
10. Enter the Calibrate sub-menu. Use the CALIBRATE softkey to begin calibration of the linear point. When complete, the A/D count for the linear calibration is displayed. Press ENTER to acknowledge the value.
11. Use the LEFT and RIGHT keys to enter the next linearization point PT-> 2.
12. Repeat for up to five linearization points.
13. To exit the linearization parameters, press UP to return to WLIN.

modes.title: Rezero for Hooks or Chains
modes.blurb: The test weights hung from hooks or chains during calibration. Rezero removes that rigging offset from the zero and span values afterward.

modes.title: Last Zero and Temp Zero (Advanced Zero Choices)
modes.blurb: Advanced zero sources for a scale that cannot be emptied. The book defines these two choices but prints no separate keypress walk-through for them — treat this as the book's definition, not a proven button sequence.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The iQUBE2 is calibrated from the connected 920i front panel in this chapter — pick the calibration type that fits the cells and the job, and I will read it one step at a time. No minimum test weight is required, but the book recommends at least 10% of scale capacity. modes.title: Standard Calibration
modes.blurb: The plain zero-and-span calibration with one known test weight. Note: the extract picks this procedure up at the weight-entry prompt, after zero has been captured — the book's opening steps for this mode were not in the extract.
modes.text:
The iQUBE3 junction box is calibrated from the 1280 indicator it is connected to — this book covers the 1280 Enterprise, version 2.09 and up. Pick the way that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Enter 1280 Configuration Mode. The book points to Section 3.3 on printed page 37 for how.
2. Press Scales. The Format interface displays.
3. Select Calibration. The Calibration Screen displays.
4. Press Calibrate Scale. The iQUBE3 Scale Calibration menu displays.
5. The extract joins this procedure at the calibration weight entry prompt, with zero already captured. The book's earlier steps for this mode are not in the extract.
6. Press 123... The Calibration Weight entry prompt displays.
7. Enter the calibration weight for the test weight and press DONE.
8. Place the test weight on the scale.
9. Press Calibrate Span. The indicator calibrates span.
10. Press Next. The Calibration Results display.
11. From the Calibration Results, remove the test weight and press Next. If resistance boards are installed, the Resistance: Load Cell prompt displays — press YES to test the resistance cards, then select NO if the load cells are 4-wire or YES if they are 6-wire, and the indicator runs the resistance test. Press Next and Calibration Complete displays. Select Finish to return to the Scale Setup, then select Save and Exit — weigh mode displays. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake iQUBE3 Digital Diagnostic Junction Box Technical Manual PN 228701 Rev D — Standard Calibration (Section 4.1) [PDF p. 52], Corner Match Calibration (Section 4.2, printed pp. 53-54) [PDF pp. 53-54], Auto-Trim Calibration (Section 4.3, printed pp. 55-57) [PDF pp. 55-57], Calibration Results and Resistance Tests (Section 4.4, printed pp. 58-59) [PDF pp. 58-59].

modes.title: Corner Match Calibration

modes.text:

10. Enter the calibration weight for the test weight and press DONE.

12. Place the calibration weight over the corner that corresponds with the current load cell — it is highlighted with a red box.
13. Press Calibrate Corner. The display proceeds to the next load cell.
14. Repeat the last two steps until all load cells have been calibrated.
15. Press Next. The Calibration Results display.
16. From the Calibration Results, remove the test weight and press Next. modes.title: Scale Calibration (Zero and Span)
modes.blurb: The full calibration: empty scale for the initial (zero), then one known test weight for span. First-time setups and complete recalibrations.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The PANTHER calibrates in its F1 Scale Interface Program Block: first the unit your test weights are in, then an empty-scale zero and one known test weight for span. There are also small touch-up adjustments for zero and span on their own, a shift adjust for DigiTOL scales, and a Geo Code for gravity. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Get into setup and bring up the F1 Scale Interface Program Block. The pages this hub is built from start inside that block, so the exact setup-entry key presses are not confirmed here — see the flags below.
2. At F1.2, CALIBRATION UNITS, enter the value for the kind of test weights you will use: 1 for lb, 2 for kg, 3 for g, 4 for oz, 5 for lb-oz, 6 for ozt, 7 for dwt, 8 for t, 9 for ton. Calibration is done in this unit, the primary unit.
3. At F1.3, SCALE CAPACITY, the current scale capacity shows and can be edited by numeric entry. Only legal scale capacities from the book's table are permitted.
4. At F1.4, INCREMENT SIZE, the current increment size shows for selection-list editing. Press the SELECT key to toggle through the valid selections. Note: for lb-oz mode, the capacity must be entered in whole ounces.
5. At the CAL prompt, set X to 1 to continue the calibration procedure. X is 0 to skip it.
6. The display shows E SCL. Empty the scale platform and press ENTER to continue.
7. The display shows 15 CAL and counts down while the initial (zero) is set. If motion sensitivity is not disabled and motion is detected, the display returns to E SCL — steady the scale and start again.
8. The display shows Add Ld. Place the test weight on the scale platform and press ENTER.
9. Enter the test weight value. The display shows a zero followed by four digits, and no decimal point is permitted. The maximum test weight is 105 percent of full scale capacity. In lb-oz mode, enter the test weight value in ounces.
10. The display shows 15 CAL and counts down while the span is set. If motion is detected at this step, the display returns to the Add Ld prompt.
11. The display shows CAL d — calibration done — for a moment. The calibration is complete.
12. Work through to the end of setup to save and return to weighing — the book's span-adjust text speaks of proceeding to the end of setup, but the exact exit key presses are not in the pages this hub is built from (see flags). Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Mettler Toledo PANTHER Terminal Technical Manual E14957000A (10/2008) — F1.2 Calibration Units (printed p. 3-7), F1.3 Scale Capacity and F1.4 Increment Size (printed p. 3-8), Scale Calibration Procedure (printed p. 3-9), F1.5 Shift Adjust, F1.6 Zero Calibration Adjust, F1.7 Span Calibration Adjust, F1.8 Geo Code (printed pp. 3-9 to 3-10). [PDF pp. 48-51]

modes.title: Shift Adjust (DigiTOL Only)
modes.blurb: For DigiTOL scales only: teaches the terminal each load cell one at a time so the scale reads the same over every cell. Setting X to 2 instead sets all shift constants to 1.0 and skips the rest — the book's route for tank or hopper scales where a shift test is not practical.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The PANTHER calibrates in its F1 Scale Interface Program Block: first the unit your test weights are in, then an empty-scale zero and one known test weight for span. There are also small touch-up adjustments for zero and span on their own, a shift adjust for DigiTOL scales, and a Geo Code for gravity. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Get into setup and bring up the F1 Scale Interface Program Block. The pages this hub is built from start inside that block, so the exact setup-entry key presses are not confirmed here — see the flags below.
2. At F1.2, CALIBRATION UNITS, enter the value for the kind of test weights you will use: 1 for lb, 2 for kg, 3 for g, 4 for oz, 5 for lb-oz, 6 for ozt, 7 for dwt, 8 for t, 9 for ton. Calibration is done in this unit, the primary unit.
3. At F1.3, SCALE CAPACITY, the current scale capacity shows and can be edited by numeric entry. Only legal scale capacities from the book's table are permitted.
4. At F1.4, INCREMENT SIZE, the current increment size shows for selection-list editing. Press the SELECT key to toggle through the valid selections. Note: for lb-oz mode, the capacity must be entered in whole ounces.
5. At F1.5, SHIFT ADJUST, set X to 1 to continue with shift adjust. X is 0 to skip it. Setting X to 2 sets the shift constants to 1.0 and skips the remainder of the procedure, removing any previously stored shift adjust values so the load cell outputs are used with no trim built in.
6. The display shows E SCL. Empty the scale platform and press ENTER to continue.
7. The display counts down from 15 while the initial is set. The weight will be averaged if motion occurs during this process.
8. The display shows CELL X. Place the test weight on the platform over cell X and press ENTER. Load cell number 1 is to the left of the J-Box, viewed from the top of the deck; cells 2, 3, and 4 are located as shown in the book's illustration.
9. The display counts down from 15 while the weight reading is recorded. The weight will be averaged if motion occurs during this process.
10. The CELL X step followed by the countdown step repeats until all the load cells connected have been shift compensated.
11. Work through to the end of setup to save and return to weighing — the book's span-adjust text speaks of proceeding to the end of setup, but the exact exit key presses are not in the pages this hub is built from (see flags). Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Mettler Toledo PANTHER Terminal Technical Manual E14957000A (10/2008) — F1.2 Calibration Units (printed p. 3-7), F1.3 Scale Capacity and F1.4 Increment Size (printed p. 3-8), Scale Calibration Procedure (printed p. 3-9), F1.5 Shift Adjust, F1.6 Zero Calibration Adjust, F1.7 Span Calibration Adjust, F1.8 Geo Code (printed pp. 3-9 to 3-10). modes.title: Zero Calibration Adjust (F1.6)
modes.blurb: A touch-up, not a full calibration: stores what is on the scale right now as the new zero. Use it when the zero has drifted and the span is still good.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The PANTHER calibrates in its F1 Scale Interface Program Block: first the unit your test weights are in, then an empty-scale zero and one known test weight for span. There are also small touch-up adjustments for zero and span on their own, a shift adjust for DigiTOL scales, and a Geo Code for gravity. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Get into setup and bring up the F1 Scale Interface Program Block. The pages this hub is built from start inside that block, so the exact setup-entry key presses are not confirmed here — see the flags below.
2. At F1.2, CALIBRATION UNITS, enter the value for the kind of test weights you will use: 1 for lb, 2 for kg, 3 for g, 4 for oz, 5 for lb-oz, 6 for ozt, 7 for dwt, 8 for t, 9 for ton. Calibration is done in this unit, the primary unit.
3. At F1.3, SCALE CAPACITY, the current scale capacity shows and can be edited by numeric entry. Only legal scale capacities from the book's table are permitted.
4. At F1.4, INCREMENT SIZE, the current increment size shows for selection-list editing. Press the SELECT key to toggle through the valid selections. Note: for lb-oz mode, the capacity must be entered in whole ounces.
5. At F1.6, ZERO CALIBRATION ADJUST, set X to 1 to store the current initial on the scale as zero. X is 0 to skip the zero adjustment.
6. The display shows 15 CAL and counts down from 15 to 0 while scale readings are being taken. Scale motion causes the countdown to restart from 15.
7. Know the escape: pressing CLEAR during the countdown aborts the zero adjust, so the motion sensitivity selection can be modified.
8. When the countdown reaches 0, the scale reading is adjusted to the new zero reading.
9. modes.title: Set Up the Scale Before Calibrating
modes.blurb: The groundwork the calibration stands on: channel type, number of channels, decimal point, units, divisions and ranges. Do this before a first calibration or whenever the scale setup changes.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The SCT-1100 is a weight transmitter, so these jobs run in setup mode at the transmitter itself, one channel at a time when you have more than one. Pick the way that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. Restart the transmitter. Momentarily press the key the book shows here during startup to display setup mode.
2. To move through a menu, press the scroll keys the book shows here. To open a parameter or confirm a value, press the confirm key the book shows here.
3. To enter a number: press the digit key the book shows to select the digit to change, then press the up or down key the book shows to increase or decrease it.
4. Restart the transmitter. Momentarily press the key the book shows here during startup to display setup mode. tyPE displays. Press the confirm key the book shows here.
5. Navigate to select the channel type. Press the confirm key when the channel type you want is displayed.
6. Navigate to setup, then ConFiG, then nChan. Press the confirm key to set the parameter.
7. Navigate to set the number of channels — Ch 1 to Ch 4. Press the confirm key to confirm. FiLt.SO displays.
8. Navigate to CALib. Press the confirm key to set the parameter. dECi displays. Press the confirm key again.
9. Navigate the menu to select the decimal point location. Press the confirm key to confirm. u.M. displays. Press the confirm key.
10. Navigate to select the unit of measure. Press the confirm key to confirm. div displays. Press the confirm key.
11. Navigate to select the scale's minimum division, or the first range of a dual-range scale. Press the confirm key to confirm the value. rAnGE1 displays. Press the confirm key.
12. Enter the total capacity of the scale, or Range 1 if you are using multi-range functioning. Press the confirm key to confirm.
13. Dual-range scales only: navigate to rAnGE 2 and press the confirm key, enter the second range, and press the confirm key to confirm. Calib.P displays.
14. Press the exit key the book shows here until the transmitter displays SAVE?. Press the confirm key to confirm. Store displays briefly and the transmitter reboots.
15. The book's note: perform this procedure for each connected channel.
16. Bring the transmitter out of setup the book's way: press the exit key the book shows here until SAVE? displays, then press the confirm key the book shows here. Store displays briefly and the transmitter reboots into weigh mode. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake SCT-1100 Advanced Series Weight Transmitter Technical Manual PN 185658 Rev E (June 10, 2025) — Calibration Parameters (Section 5.1, printed p. 41), Procedure (Section 5.2, printed p. 41), Calibration Single Channel (Section 5.3) and Multi Channel (Section 5.4, printed p. 42), Calibration With Linearization Points (Section 5.5, printed pp. 42-43), Theoretical Calibration (Section 5.6, printed pp. 43-44), Gravity Setting (Section 5.7, printed p. 45). [PDF pp. 41-45]

5. Navigate to setup, then ConFiG, then GraV. Press the confirm key the book shows here to set the parameter.
6. Enter the local gravity and press the confirm key. Heads up: the book's gravity section prints the default as 9.80390, while its calibration parameter table prints 9.80655 — the book gives both, so trust the value your own display shows.
7. Slowly press the exit key the book shows here multiple times to exit the menus until SAVE? displays.
8. Press the confirm key to confirm and return to weigh mode. Pressing any other key cancels and exits without saving.
9. The book's own caution: the gravity correction function has not been evaluated by an approvals agency, so it is up to the authorized scale dealer to ensure the device is accurate at the intended point of use.
10. Bring the transmitter out of setup the book's way: press the exit key the book shows here until SAVE? displays, then press the confirm key the book shows here. modes.title: Theoretical Calibration — Legal for Trade
modes.blurb: No test weights hung: the span is set from the load cells' rated data — total build, average sensitivity, and division size. This must be completed before any test-weight calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration on the SCT-20 starts with the load cells' own numbers, then gets proven with real test weights. The book's order is fixed: theoretical calibration first, then Zero Setting, then the Weight (Span) Calibration.
CAUTION: The SCT-20 is sealed with a self-destructive adhesive label placed over the seam between the two halves of the indicator. The seal prevents the top and bottom half from being separated and prohibits access to the jumper inside. The jumper is closed by default for all models shipping from Rice Lake Weighing Systems, and with the jumper closed the SCT-20 can be calibrated and configured. The jumper will need to be removed before the SCT-20 is sealed for Legal for Trade applications, and for Legal for Trade a new self-destructive adhesive label (PN 162882) and SCT-20 Capacity label (PN 162881) are required after each calibration.
1. Press and hold the first key the book shows, then press the second key the book shows, to enter the setup menu. CALIB is displayed.
2. Press the Enter key to open the calibration menu. FS-TEO, the system full scale, is the first parameter.
3. For numeric entries: press the Enter key and the first digit flashes and can be edited. Press the Scroll key to select the desired digit, then press the Next key to increment the digit.
4. With CALIB displayed, open the calibration menu. FS-TEO is displayed first. Set the system full scale: one load cell capacity multiplied by the number of load cells used. The book's example: 4 cells of 1000 kg gives a full scale of 4000. The instrument is supplied with a theoretical full scale value dENO corresponding to 10000; to restore factory values, set 0 as full scale.
5. Move to SENSIB and set the sensitivity — a load cell rated parameter expressed in mV/V. Set the average sensitivity value indicated on the load cells. The book's example: for 4 cells of 2.00100, 2.00150, 2.00200 and 2.00250, enter 2.00175.
6. Move to E and set the minimum weight increment value, equal to 1/10000 of full scale. It can be changed between 0.0001 and 100 with x1 x2 x5 x10 increments. On multi-interval instruments these are E1, E2 and E3, one per range.
7. Know what this does: if changes are made to the theoretical Full Scale, the Sensitivity or the Divisions, the Weight (Span) Calibration is canceled and only the theoretical calibration is considered valid, and all the system's parameters containing a weight value will be set to default values — setpoints, hysteresis, etc.
8. Press the Escape key twice to exit the setup menu. Prove it with the book's own check: load two known test weights together and correct the indicated weight to their combined value; then remove them one at a time — the system must show the weight still on it, and with both removed it must read zero. If this does not happen, the book says there is a mechanical problem affecting the system linearity: identify and correct any mechanical problems before repeating the procedure. For Legal for Trade applications, set a new self-destructive adhesive label (PN 162882) over the seam between the two halves of the SCT-20 and set the SCT-20 Capacity Label (PN 162881) on the SCT-20 after each calibration.

modes.title: Weight (Span) Calibration with Test Weights

1. Press and hold the first key the book shows, then press the second key the book shows, to enter the setup menu. CALIB is displayed.
2. Press the Enter key to open the calibration menu. FS-TEO, the system full scale, is the first parameter.
3. For numeric entries: press the Enter key and the first digit flashes and can be edited. Press the Scroll key to select the desired digit, then press the Next key to increment the digit.
4. First perform the theoretical calibration and the Zero Setting — the book requires both before this.
5. Load the test weight onto the scale. Use as high of a percentage of the maximum quantity to be weighed as possible.
6. From CALIB, move to WEIGHT and press the Enter key. The value of the weight currently on the system will be flashing on the display, and all of the LEDs are off.
7. If adjustment is not required, skip ahead to the confirm step. If it is, adjust the value on display to match the weight loaded on the scale, using the numeric editing keys. The LEDs will begin scrolling.
8. Press the Enter key. The new set weight is displayed with all the LEDs flashing.
9. Press the Enter key again. WEIGHT will be displayed again.
10. Know which calibration you are on: if the theoretical full scale and the recalculated full scale in Weight (Span) Calibration are equal, the calibration currently in use is theoretical; if they are different, the calibration in use is the Weight (Span) Calibration based on calibration weights. If the correction changes the previous full scale by more than 20%, all the parameters with settable weight values are reset to default values.
11. Press the Escape key twice to exit the setup menu. modes.title: Linearization — up to Five Points

modes.title: Calibration with a Known Weight
modes.blurb: The standard calibration: the scale is taught with real sample weights, using one to three calibration points. Use this whenever known test weights are on hand.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The SCT-2200 can be calibrated with a known weight, or theoretically from the load cells' own numbers when a known weight is not available, and its gravity setting can correct for the difference between where it was calibrated and where it works. Pick the job that fits and I will read it one step at a time. Note from the book: returning the instrument to default settings cancels the present calibration.
1. Restart the indicator. Momentarily press the key the book shows during startup to display setup mode.
2. Navigate to setup, then ConFiG, then Calib, then deC1. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.
3. Navigate to select the decimal place value. Press the key the book shows to confirm the selection. U.M. displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter. The book notes: by setting the divisions of the first range, the divisions for the second range are automatically set.
4. Navigate to select the unit of measure. Press the key the book shows to confirm the selection. div displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.
5. Navigate to select the scale's minimum division, or the first range of dual range. Press the key the book shows to confirm the value. rAnGE1 displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.
6. Set the total capacity of the scale, or ranGe1 if using multi-range functioning. Press the key the book shows to confirm.
7. For a dual range scale only: navigate to select rAnGE 2 and press the key the book shows to set the parameter. Set the second range and press the key the book shows to confirm. Calib.P displays. Press the key the book shows to enter the menu. ntP displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter. The book notes rAnGE2 is disabled if set at 000000.
8. Navigate to select the desired number, 1 to 3, of calibration points and press the key the book shows. tP O displays. Press the key the book shows.
9. Unload the scale and wait until ddt1 displays. Press the key the book shows.
10. Set the weight value of the first sample weight. Press the key the book shows to confirm.
11. Navigate to select tP1. Press the key the book shows.
12. Put the weight on the scale. Press the key the book shows. Wait until the display stops flashing between the scale counts and TP1. The book notes: when the weight acquisition is complete and a calibration point is set, the internal divisions value momentarily displays followed by ntP; if using multiple calibration points, the unit automatically advances to the next point, ddt2, ddt3.
13. Repeat the point steps for each calibration point. The book notes the calibration points must be in increasing order: point 1 less than point 2 less than point 3.
14. Remove all weight from the scale. The book marks this step optional, but warns: if the auto-zero function is active, after saving the calibration the weight on the scale displays as zero even if the weight has not been removed.
15. Once the calibration is complete, press the key the book shows until the instrument displays SAVE?. Press the confirm key to store the calibration to the instrument memory — Store displays; press any other key to cancel and exit without saving. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake SCT-2200 Advanced Series Weight Transmitter Technical Manual PN 183522 Rev G — Calibration Procedure (§5.2) [PDF pp. 41-42]; Theoretical Calibration (§5.3) [PDF pp. 42-43]; Setting Local Gravity (§5.4) [PDF p. 43]; Calibration Parameters (Table 5-1) [PDF p. 41].

modes.title: Theoretical Calibration (no known weight)
modes.blurb: Use a theoretical calibration when a weight of known value is not available, or a manual calibration cannot be performed. The span is worked out from the load cells' sensitivity, capacity, and the scale's dead load.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The SCT-2200 can be calibrated with a known weight, or theoretically from the load cells' own numbers when a known weight is not available, and its gravity setting can correct for the difference between where it was calibrated and where it works. 1. Restart the indicator. Momentarily press the key the book shows during startup to display setup mode.
2. Navigate to setup, then ConFiG, then Calib, then deC1. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.
3. From deC1, navigate to select the decimal place value. Press the key the book shows. U.M. displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.
4. Navigate to select the unit of measure. Press the key the book shows to confirm the selection. div displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.
5. Navigate to select the scale's minimum division. Press the key the book shows. rAnGE1 displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.
6. Set the total capacity of the scale, or ranGe1 if using multi-range functioning. Press the key the book shows to select the digit to be modified, and the keys the book shows to increase or decrease the digit. Press the key the book shows to confirm.
7. For a dual range scale only: navigate to select rAnGE 2 and press the key the book shows to set the parameter. Set the second range and press the key the book shows to confirm. The book notes rAnGE2 is disabled if set at 000000.
8. Navigate to select thEo.CA. Press the key the book shows to enter the menu. CeL.Sen displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.
9. Set the cell sensitivity in mV/V. Press the key the book shows to confirm. CeL.CAP displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter. The book notes: if several load cells are connected through a junction box, enter the average sensitivity value of the cells.
10. Set the total load cell capacity in the configured unit of measure. Press the key the book shows to confirm. dEAd.Ld displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.
11. Enter the known weight of the scale structure dead load on the load cells with no weights added. Press the key the book shows to confirm. kno.WGt displays. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter. GEt.Wt? displays.
12. Enter the known value in the configured unit of measure. Press the key the book shows to confirm. The book notes: the first character indicates the sign — 0 indicates a positive value, minus indicates a negative value — and entering 000000 if the value is not known sets the dead load as acquired.
13. If the weight is unstable, Er.MOt may momentarily display, then Store? displays. Press the key the book shows to confirm and save. Or press the key the book shows for next confirmation; rEtry? displays — press the key the book shows to confirm and repeat the operation.
14. Press the key the book shows to exit the calibration. th.CAL? displays. Press the key the book shows to confirm and apply the new calibration, or press the key the book shows to cancel.
15. Repeat this procedure for each connected scale.
16. Once the calibration is complete, press the key the book shows until the instrument displays SAVE?. Press the confirm key to store the calibration to the instrument memory — Store displays; press any other key to cancel and exit without saving. 5. Navigate to setup, then ConFiG, then Grav. Press the key the book shows to set the parameter.

7. Slowly press the key the book shows multiple times to exit the menus until SAVE? displays. Press the key the book shows to confirm and return to weigh mode, or press any other key to cancel and exit without saving.

9. Important, in the book's own words: the gravity correction function has not been evaluated by an approvals agency, therefore it is up to the authorized scale dealer to ensure the device is accurate at the intended point of use.
10. Once the calibration is complete, press the key the book shows until the instrument displays SAVE?. Press the confirm key to store the calibration to the instrument memory — Store displays; press any other key to cancel and exit without saving. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Theoretical Calibration
modes.blurb: No test weights hung. Set the span from the load cells' own rated numbers: total capacity, average sensitivity in millivolts per volt, and display division. The book says changing any of these cancels a Weight (Span) Calibration.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The SCT-40 transmitter calibrates from its setup menu: enter the load cells' own rated numbers for a theoretical calibration, then set zero, and prove it with real test weights. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From the weight display, press and hold the first key the book shows, then press the second key the book shows. CALIB is displayed.
2. Press the key the book shows to enter. FS-TEO is displayed.
3. If the parameter you need is not FS-TEO, press the keys the book shows to scroll until your parameter is displayed, then press the key the book shows to enter it.
4. With FS-TEO displayed, press the key the book shows.
5. Press the key the book shows to select a digit, then press the key the book shows to increment it, until the total load cell capacity is displayed. The system full scale is one cell capacity multiplied by the number of cells used. To restore the factory value, set 0.
6. Press the key the book shows. SENSIB is displayed. Press the key the book shows.
7. Select and increment the digits until the load cells' average sensitivity is displayed. Sensitivity is a load cell rated parameter in millivolts per volt; the book allows 0.50000 to 7.00000. To average cells, add their sensitivities and divide by the number of cells.
8. Press the key the book shows. DIVIS is displayed. Press the key the book shows.
9. Select and increment the digits until the display division size you want is shown. The book says it is calculated as one ten-thousandth of full scale and can be changed.
10. Press the key the book shows, then press the exit key the book shows twice to leave the setup menu.
11. Press the exit key the book shows until you are back at the weight display. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.
References: Rice Lake SCT-40 Series Signal Conditioning Transmitter/Indicator Technical Manual PN 171954 Rev F — Calibration (§2.2), Theoretical Calibration (§2.2.1), Equalization (§2.2.3), Zero Setting (§2.2.4), Zero Value Manual Entry (§2.2.5), Weight (Span) Calibration (§2.2.6), Linearization Option [PDF pp. 14-19]

modes.title: Real Equalization
modes.blurb: Balances up to eight load cells against one sample weight, one cell at a time. The book requires a sample weight of at least 50 percent of a single load cell's capacity. Zero Setting comes after, then a check with known weights.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The SCT-40 transmitter calibrates from its setup menu: enter the load cells' own rated numbers for a theoretical calibration, then set zero, and prove it with real test weights. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From the weight display, press and hold the first key the book shows, then press the second key the book shows. CALIB is displayed.
2. Press the key the book shows to enter. FS-TEO is displayed.
3. If the parameter you need is not FS-TEO, press the keys the book shows to scroll until your parameter is displayed, then press the key the book shows to enter it.
4. Scroll until EQUAL is displayed, then press the key the book shows. EQREA is displayed.
5. Press the key the book shows. EQUAL0 is displayed.
6. Unload the scale, wait for stability, and confirm by pressing the key the book shows. EQUAL1 is displayed.
7. Place the sample weight on load cell 1 and wait for stability. Confirm by pressing the key the book shows. EQUAL2 is displayed.
8. Move the sample weight to the next load cell, wait for stability, and confirm the same way, working through each load cell.
9. If equalization completes, VALID is displayed. Confirm by pressing the key the book shows. If an error occurs, FAILED is displayed. Confirm and repeat the equalization procedure.
10. After equalization, perform the Zero Setting mode, then check the calibration with known weights and correct the indicated weight with a Weight (Span) Calibration if needed.
11. Press the exit key the book shows until you are back at the weight display. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Theoretical Equalization
modes.blurb: Equalize from the load cells' paperwork instead of a sample weight: enter each cell's sensitivity, and leave inactive cells at 0.
modes.text:

modes.title: Zero Setting
modes.blurb: Zero the scale after use, or to compensate for changes from environmental factors. The book says to set the Theoretical Calibration data first. This menu can also be opened straight from the weight display by holding the key the book shows for three seconds.
modes.text:

modes.title: Zero Value Manual Entry
modes.blurb: Hand-enter a dead load value instead of zeroing the structure. The book limits this to when the scale cannot be emptied, for example product that cannot be unloaded.
modes.text:

modes.title: Weight (Span) Calibration with Test Weights
modes.blurb: The real-weight proof and correction. The book asks for the Theoretical Calibration, Equalization, and Zero Setting first, and a test weight of at least 50 percent of the maximum quantity to be weighed.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The SCT-40 transmitter calibrates from its setup menu: enter the load cells' own rated numbers for a theoretical calibration, then set zero, and prove it with real test weights. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.
1. From the weight display, press and hold the first key the book shows, then press the second key the book shows. CALIB is displayed.
2. Press the key the book shows to enter. FS-TEO is displayed.
3. If the parameter you need is not FS-TEO, press the keys the book shows to scroll until your parameter is displayed, then press the key the book shows to enter it.
4. Load the test weight onto the scale.
5. Enter the calibration menu so CALIB is displayed, then press the key the book shows. FS-TEO is displayed.
6. Scroll until WEIGHt is displayed, then press the key the book shows. The weight currently on the system flashes on the display, with all of the symbols off.
7. If the displayed value already matches the weight loaded, skip to the confirm step. If it needs adjusting, select and increment the digits until the display shows the true value of the loaded test weight. The symbols begin scrolling.
8. Press the key the book shows. The new set weight appears with all the symbols flashing.
9. Press the key the book shows. WEIGHt is displayed.
10. Prove it the book's way: take part of the weight off and the reading should drop by exactly that much; take all of it off and the system should read zero. If it does not, the book says there is a mechanical problem affecting linearity — identify and correct it before repeating this procedure.
11. Press the exit key the book shows until you are back at the weight display. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Linearization on Up to Five Points
modes.blurb: Straightens the reading across the range using the Weight (Span) Calibration with up to five different test weights. The book gives this as a paragraph, not numbered steps.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. The SCT-40 transmitter calibrates from its setup menu: enter the load cells' own rated numbers for a theoretical calibration, then set zero, and prove it with real test weights. Pick the one that fits the job and I will read it one step at a time.

2. Press the key the book shows to enter. FS-TEO is displayed.
3. If the parameter you need is not FS-TEO, press the keys the book shows to scroll until your parameter is displayed, then press the key the book shows to enter it.
4. The book defines this as performing the Weight (Span) Calibration with up to a maximum of five points, using five different test weights. It gives no separate keypress steps for the extra points.
5. After the fifth value is entered, press the key the book shows. The procedure ends at that point.
6. Know the limit first: after that, the calibration value can no longer be changed. To redo it, return to the weight display and re-enter the calibration menu for a new Weight (Span) Calibration.
7. The book also says that pressing the key the book shows after a sample weight is confirmed makes the full scale display the maximum test weight entered, referenced to the cell sensitivity set in the Theoretical Calibration.
8. Press the exit key the book shows until you are back at the weight display. Prove it: with the scale empty it should read zero; put a known weight on and it should read exactly that weight.

modes.title: Zero Calibration (Cal.Zero)
modes.blurb: The plain zero: empty scale, record the zero point. Run this first, then the Span procedure.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. On the ZM510 the calibration lives in the ADMIN menu, under Setup, then Calib — pick the scale, pick a procedure, and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Check the seal first. The User menu shows the seal status — SEAL or NO SEAL — and the book says if the unit is sealed, no changes can be made to the configuration of the indicator.
1. Press and hold the SETUP key until the password entry screen appears.
2. Key in the ADMIN menu password, 3088, and press ENTER.
3. Highlight the Setup icon and press ENTER.
4. Open Calib, highlight the scale you want to calibrate — Scale 1 through 4; if only one scale is connected, Scale 1 is the only choice — and press ENTER.
5. The procedure list appears: Zero, Span, Linear, Input, Gravity, Display, Cal Unit and Print.
6. In the Calib menu, highlight Zero and press ENTER.
7. Highlight Cal.Zero and press ENTER. The CALIBRATE window appears — the word CALIBRATE on the display means you are in the calibration procedure.
8. Empty the scale and press ENTER. Busy shows briefly, then the weight is displayed.
9. Press ENTER to accept the zero point calibration.
10. To get out: use the ESC softkey if it is on the screen; when it is no longer available, press the up arrow softkey repeatedly until you are asked if you want to save the changes. Use the Up or Down key to make your choice and press ENTER to accept — the indicator reboots to the startup screen with the new changes active. Then do it the book's way: test the accuracy with a known weight. The book prints no seal-screw step here; if you want a record, the Calib menu's Print item prints a calibration report through Port 1, Port 2, Port 3 or USB, and the book says that information can be used to restore calibration later.
References: Avery Weigh-Tronix ZM510 Indicator Service Manual AWT35-501664 Issue AB — Exiting a menu (printed p. 18), Seal status (printed p. 20), ADMIN menu access (printed pp. 27-28), Calibrate menu and Zero procedure (printed p. 29), TEMP/LAST zero and Span procedure (printed p. 30), Linearity, Input and Gravity procedures (printed p. 31), Gravity save-and-test note, Display, Cal Unit and Print (printed p. 32). [PDF pp. 18, 20, 28-32]

modes.title: Temporary Zero (Temp)
modes.blurb: For a tank or vessel you cannot empty: the product weight is temporarily zeroed, you span it, and the original zero comes back.

modes.title: Span Calibration
modes.blurb: The test-weight half of the job: tell it the calibration weight, put the weights on, and capture the span.
modes.text:

modes.title: Gravity Adjustment
modes.blurb: Scale was calibrated somewhere with a different gravity pull and you cannot re-calibrate with test weights: key in the local gravity factor, or have the indicator work it out from latitude and altitude.
modes.text:
Calibration is teaching the scale honest answers. On the ZM510 the calibration lives in the ADMIN menu, under Setup, then Calib — pick the scale, pick a procedure, and I will read it one step at a time.
CAUTION: Check the seal first. The User menu shows the seal status — SEAL or NO SEAL — and the book says if the unit is sealed, no changes can be made to the configuration of the indicator.
1. Press and hold the SETUP key until the password entry screen appears.
2. Key in the ADMIN menu password, 3088, and press ENTER.
3. Highlight the Setup icon and press ENTER.
4. Open Calib, highlight the scale you want to calibrate — Scale 1 through 4; if only one scale is connected, Scale 1 is the only choice — and press ENTER.
5. The procedure list appears: Zero, Span, Linear, Input, Gravity, Display, Cal Unit and Print.
6. In the Calib menu, highlight Gravity and press ENTER.
7. If you know the local gravitation factor, key it in under G-Fact. The book's allowable range is 9.70000 to 9.90000.
8. If you do not know it, key in the installation site's latitude under Lat — the valid range is 0 to 90 — and the altitude under Alt, 0 to 30,000 feet (10,000 metres).
9. Choose Calc. The indicator calculates the gravity factor and loads it as the gravity factor.
10. The book's cautions: verify with local agencies that adjusting the gravity factor is accepted in your area — calibration with certified weights may be required — and follow all local weights and measures regulations. Save the changes when you exit, and test the accuracy with a known weight.
11. To get out: use the ESC softkey if it is on the screen; when it is no longer available, press the up arrow softkey repeatedly until you are asked if you want to save the changes. Use the Up or Down key to make your choice and press ENTER to accept — the indicator reboots to the startup screen with the new changes active. Then do it the book's way: test the accuracy with a known weight. The book prints no seal-screw step here; if you want a record, the Calib menu's Print item prints a calibration report through Port 1, Port 2, Port 3 or USB, and the book says that information can be used to restore calibration later.
References: Avery Weigh-Tronix ZM510 Indicator Service Manual AWT35-501664 Issue AB — Exiting a menu (printed p. 18), Seal status (printed p. 20), ADMIN menu access (printed pp. 27-28), Calibrate menu and Zero procedure (printed p. 29), TEMP/LAST zero and Span procedure (printed p. 30), Linearity, Input and Gravity procedures (printed p. 31), Gravity save-and-test note, Display, Cal Unit and Print (printed p. 32).
